title: Circum-Arctic Sediment PROvenance Database (CASPROD): a database of mineralogy and geochemistry for the Circum-Arctic surface sediments
abstract: Arctic amplification is fundamentally reshaping the cryosphere, leading to accelerated sea-ice retreat, permafrost thaw, and intensified riverine discharge. These shifts collectively modify sediment source-to-sink dynamic processes in the Arctic Ocean. While surface sediments in this semi-enclosed basin integrate complex signals from diverse Eurasian and North American source regions, disentangling these provenance signatures requires a robust, multi-proxy framework that has historically been hampered by fragmented, heterogeneous datasets. title: Continental pollutants modulate organic nitrogen and light absorption of marine organic aerosols over East Asian marginal seas
abstract: Organic nitrogen (ON) in marine aerosols is not only an important fraction of atmospheric nitrogen deposition but also a vital contributor to light-absorbing organic aerosols. However, observational evidence is lacking on the driving factors of ON formation or its role in organic aerosol absorption, especially in marine atmosphere. Here, shipboard observations were conducted in spring, summer, and autumn over the Yellow Sea and Bohai Sea (YBS) to understand the spatiotemporal distributions and sources of aerosol ON over East Asian marginal seas. abstract: Natural selection is imposed by both abiotic environmental filtering and biotic interactions, yet their relative roles in shaping the deep phylogeny of widespread, generalist host-associated bacteria remain unclear. Here, we integrate large-scale phylogenomics, environmental sequencing, functional genomics, and global metagenomic analysis to demonstrate that tidal zonation overrides host association as the dominant macroevolutionary force structuring the marine bacterial genus Ruegeria. title: Drone-Transect: a non-destructive operational protocol for drone-based conservation studies on intertidal coral reefs
abstract: With many functions attributed to drone use, different applications have been employed along the coastal environment. Most studies have focused on quantifying live and non-live cover, without measuring or quantifying species at the individual level. Thus, we proposed the Drone-Transect method, which, based on aerial images captured by drones, can identify benthic organisms on a broad spatial scale, determining abundance and spatio-temporal distribution. abstract: Abstract As coastal communities confront accelerating sea-level rise, planning practice faces a growing tension between preserving heritage and ensuring climate resilience. A critical gap exists regarding how designation practice has hampered the integration of community-defined historic places (sites whose significance is rooted in local narratives, social relationships, working landscapes, and social continuity) into local hazard resilience planning systems. title: Surveying Biodiverse Coral Reef Ecosystems Across the Tree of Life With Environmental DNA
abstract: A central challenge in evaluating biodiversity using environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding is that each primer set has biases resulting in selective amplification of taxonomic diversity. Here we test 11 primer pairs to assess Central Pacific coral reef diversity in the five kingdoms of marine eukaryotes: Chromista, Fungi, Metazoa, Plantae and Protozoa. title: Underwater Archaeology in Archives: Georeferencing and Spatial Validation of Archival Documentation at the Medieval Harbour of Puck (Poland)
abstract: This study presents a workflow for georeferencing legacy underwater archaeological plans from the medieval harbour in Puck (Poland) and integrating them into GIS. Archival drawings from the 1980s and 1990s, based on different local grids, were digitised, spatially reconstructed and validated against multibeam echosounder (MBES) data with RTK positioning. abstract: ABSTRACT High‐density polyethylene (HDPE) is widely applied in marine engineering infrastructures, but its service in sustained dynamic impact scenarios is severely constrained by the inherent mismatch among tensile strength, impact toughness, and environmental stress cracking resistance (ESCR). abstract: Evidence-informed architectural heritage planning requires a robust understanding of long-term urban morphogenesis. This paper reconstructs the spatial evolution of Bejaia (Bougie), Algeria, from 1833 to 1962 and tests how diachronic Geographic Information System (GIS)-based indicators can substantiate safeguarding priorities in Mediterranean coastal historic centres. title: Is Deep-Sea Mining the New “Green Frontier”? A Corpus-assisted Discourse Analysis of Arguments on the Climate Crisis and Deep-Sea Mining in the Pacific
abstract: With its abundance of minerals identified as essential for the green transition, the ocean floor is regarded by Deep-Sea Mining (DSM) proponents as the new “green frontier” of resource extraction. This framing of DSM is particularly significant for the Pacific Island Countries (PICs), which are positioned at the geographic center of DSM pursuits. title: Observational Evidence for Accelerated Warming and Salinification Propagating Into the Deep Mediterranean
abstract: Abstract Acceleration, rather than a gradual linear response, is emerging as a defining feature of ocean change in the Anthropocene. Surface‐forced warming propagates into the deep ocean over decades to centuries, but semi‐enclosed basins such as the Mediterranean Sea may respond more rapidly. Here, we analyse an in situ Mediterranean‐wide multiplatform data set spanning 1950–2025 and show that warming and salinification of the upper 1,000–2,000 m are not only continuing but accelerating, at increasing rates over the record. title: Bacterial inoculation elicits changes to the coral epigenome
abstract: Environmental shifts can cause epigenetic modifications in corals associated with changes in gene expression and physiology, although it remains unclear if associated bacteria can also induce such changes. Here, we inoculate nubbins of the coral Pocillopora verrucosa with an opportunistic pathogen, Vibrio coralliilyticus, and/or a coral probiotic, Cobetia sp., and subject the nubbins to heat stress. title: Community-level eDNA decay patterns in marine zooplankton: Implications for optimizing eDNA-based marine environmental monitoring
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has the potential to greatly transform marine ecological monitoring, yet its capacity for accurate biodiversity estimates is constrained by its decay process. Previous research has largely focused on laboratory-cultured single species, and thus the dynamics of mixed-species eDNA from natural communities remain poorly understood. title: Mitigating the impacts of oligotrophication and thermal stress on Pacific oyster Magallana gigas aquaculture through solar-powered artificial upwelling
abstract: Abstract Recent oligotrophication and rising water temperatures in the Seto Inland Sea of Japan have led to a decline in oyster production in Hiroshima Prefecture. This study developed and evaluated the “Seawater Pump-up Apparatus for Localized Oceanic Warming-mitigation” (SPALOW), a device designed to supply cool and nutrient-rich bottom water and diatom resting cells from the sediment to the surface layer. title: Identifying Optimal Hiking Locations Using a GIS-Based Suitability Model
abstract: The growth of ecotourism and hiking is one pillar of Saudi Vision 2030. However, the Kingdom lacks an up-to-date national spatial classification that would enable systematic coverage and strategic decision-making on potentially suitable hiking areas. In response, this study developed a GIS-based MCDA framework to classify hiking zones and assess their suitability across mountainous, desert, and coastal environments. title: Ant Diversity of the Xisha Islands: Community Structure, Exotic Species Colonization, and Ecological Functions in a Tropical Coral Archipelago
abstract: ABSTRACT The Xisha Islands in the South China Sea are a typical tropical coral archipelago at the forefront of global climate change and anthropogenic disturbance, yet their ant diversity and ecological functions remain uncharacterized. In this study, we systematically surveyed ants across seven islands, integrating morphological identification with molecular species delimitation (based on COI barcodes, with ABGD, ASAP, and bPTP methods) to compile the species inventory, and analyzed the effects of island geographic traits, anthropogenic disturbance, and vegetation type on ant communities. title: Immersive human–computer interaction simulation and emergency buoyancy control of submerged body in the South China Sea internal solitary wave
abstract: Oceanic internal solitary waves (ISWs) produce strong nonlinear variations in density stratification and flow fields, posing considerable risks to submerged body navigation. In this study, high-resolution ISW data in the South China Sea were simulated using the Massachusetts Institute of Technology General Circulation Model (MITgcm), and a continuous three-dimensional visualization of ISWs was developed based on isopycnal depth extraction. abstract: ABSTRACT Uranium extraction from seawater represents a vital route for exploring non‐conventional uranium resources. Enhancing the mass transfer performance and antifouling capabilities, and constructing synergistic promotion are crucial for improving adsorption efficiency and durability of uranium extraction materials in large‐scale marine tests. title: Feeling the noise: behavioural responses in ascidians are associated with substrate-borne vibrations rather than sound pressure alone
abstract: Abstract Marine anthropogenic noise pollution has increased substantially in recent decades, raising concerns about its effects on marine organisms. While research has primarily focused on marine mammals and – to a smaller extent – on fish, comparatively little is known about how sessile benthic invertebrates perceive and respond to underwater vibroacoustic stimuli. abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective community surveillance of respiratory diseases relies on the timely collection and analysis of high quality clinical and virology data. The aim was to develop interactive dashboards for general practice, public health, and researcher groups. This would improve the visualisation, utilisation, and quality of virology data from an English sentinel network, support disease trend monitoring, early outbreak response, and thereby reduce poor health outcomes and their societal impact. abstract: Carijoa riisei is a branching colonial octocoral widely distributed in reef and estuarine environments along the coast of Pernambuco, northeastern Brazil. Owing to the structural complexity of its colonies, it provides both habitat and substrate for a diverse assemblage of associated organisms. abstract: Floods can be very destructive natural hazard; it causes significant environmental, social, and economic impacts. Havza is a district in Northern part of Türkiye, experienced major flood events in May 1998 and May 2026, which emphasize the need of identify flood-prone areas and analyze the factors that influence flood vulnerability. The aim of this study is to asses flood risk and analyzes land use/land cover (LULC) monitoring derived from remote sensing data in Havza. journal: Black Sea Journal of Engineering and Science

title: Dynamic emperor penguin colonies
abstract: Abstract Understanding how species respond to environmental change is critical for predicting their resilience to future climate impacts. For emperor penguins, relocation of breeding colonies may provide an important mechanism for coping with changing sea ice conditions. Using medium and very high-resolution satellite imagery, we study penguin colony locations in West Antarctica and show that five colonies have moved significant distances over the last decade. title: The contribution of marine benthic habitats for maintaining fish biodiversity
abstract: Abstract Elucidating how biodiversity is distributed across marine habitats is essential to guide conservation efforts at a time of unprecedented anthropogenic impacts. However, the relative importance of different benthic habitats for maintaining fish biodiversity remains unclear because studies have typically focused on a single marine substrate. title: Spatial Patterns of Marine Vessel Accidents Determinants and Forecast Future Casualties Along Inland Waterways in Rivers State, Nigeria
abstract: This study analyzes the spatial patterns of marine vessel accidents, examines their determinants, and forecasts future casualties along inland waterways in Rivers State, Nigeria. The study adopts a retrospective longitudinal research design integrating Geographic Information Systems (GIS), statistical techniques, and time-series forecasting. title: Developing a Sustainable Coastal Economic Development Model in the Seribu Islands Regency: A Natural Resources-Based View Approach and Blue Growth
abstract: Coastal areas play a strategic role and possess significant potential in achieving national economic development goals. However, economic development in coastal regions faces various challenges, including limited knowledge regarding sustainable development roadmaps for these areas. This study aimed to develop a conceptual hierarchical model to guide coastal economic development based on the Natural Resources-Based View and Blue Growth approaches. title: Building digital competence for a high-skilled workforce: An institutional analysis of North Central and Central Coastal Vietnam
abstract: Digital competence is often treated as an individual attribute, although its development depends on institutions connecting education, labour demand and innovation. This study examines that institutional problem in North Central and Central Coastal Vietnam. A qualitative policy-document case study analysed 14 national and regional strategies, decisions, statistical publications and diagnostic reports issued between 2020 and 2024. title: Real-time integrated sea surface height and wave monitoring using a GNSS buoy based on PPP-B2b service
abstract: High-precision real-time observation of sea surface height and wave parameters is essential for maritime safety, offshore engineering, disaster warning, and marine resource development. To overcome the high cost and operational complexity of in situ instruments and the limited spatiotemporal resolution of satellite remote sensing, this study proposes a global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) buoy method for integrated sea surface height and wave monitoring using the Beidou global navigation satellite system-3 (BDS-3) B2b service. title: Jeju lava seawater enhances biological stability, growth, and biomass quality during pilot-scale inland cultivation of Tetraselmis suecica
abstract: In large-scale microalgae cultivation, contamination from grazers, competing algae, bacteria, and viruses can lead to culture collapse and productivity loss. However, pre-treating large water volumes entails high costs and logistical challenges. Therefore, securing naturally clean, biologically safe water sources that do not require sterilization is important for stable and sustainable biomass production. Korea University of Science and Technology

title: The Carbonate Raman Processing and Plotting Tool: A Software Application for 2‐Dimensional Raman Image Peak‐Fitting and Visualization
abstract: ABSTRACT We present the Carbonate Raman Processing and Plotting tool (CaRPP), designed to perform peak‐fitting and visualization on two‐dimensional Raman maps of calcium carbonate specimens. The CaRPP software enhances transparency and image‐processing capabilities specific to carbonates compared to existing alternatives. Although designed for visualizing peak width and wave number spatial patterns in the shells and skeletons of marine calcifying organisms, CaRPP has potential to be used for Raman spectra peak‐fitting and plotting on a wider range of sample types.

title: Accuracy Evaluation of Satellite-Based Bathymetry Data Extracted from Digital Elevation Model against Echo Sounder Measured Data in Gurara Reservoir, Nigeria
abstract: Digital elevation models are satellite-derived imageries which comprise valuable source of elevation data for engineering applications. More specially, Digital elevation models are often used in geographic information systems, and are among the critical input parameters for digitally-produced sensitivity maps. In this regard, this paper proposes a method of generating bathymetry data from Digital elevation models which is easily accessible. journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

title: Implementation of Governance Capacity on Blue Economy Development Policy in Coastal Areas: A Case Study from East Nusa Tenggara Province
abstract: The capacity for governance is a critical factor that influences the success of implementing public policy. However, studies focusing on the capacity for governance in relation to the development of blue economy development policies are scarce. A previous research has mainly been conducted on the topics of climate change, urban issues, and covid-19, while blue economy research has mainly focused on economic and environmental aspects. This paper aims to examine the implementation of the governance capacity on blue economy development policy in the coastal area, with East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) Pro

title: Ecosystem management analysis study in tourist villages
abstract: Background: Arborek Island (8.2 ha), within Raja Ampat's Dampier Strait Marine Protected Area, is a global hub for community-based marine ecotourism and rich biodiversity. Surging tourism imposes acute socio-ecological pressures on fragile habitats and threatened megafauna (Mobula alfredi, Chelonia mydas), exposing vulnerabilities inherent to small-island systems. Methods: This study develops an empirical spatial-ecological and polycentric governance framework, combining multi-criteria GIS overlay (1:25,000) of infrastructure and statutory forest designations with a micro-spatial threat matrix
journal: Journal of Marine Problems and Threats.

title: Histopathology of scuticociliate tissue loss associated with Philaster guamense (brown band disease) in Acropora cf. muricata from the Republic of Maldives
abstract: Abstract Corals with rapidly progressing tissue loss marginated by a brown band on exposed skeleton are typically given a field diagnosis of brown band disease (BrB). It is associated with scuticociliates, protists capable of causing epidemic mortality in a wide range of marine organisms, but with uncertain pathogenic role in BrB. This study presents the first comprehensive pathological description of BrB affecting Acropora cf. muricata from the Maldives. title: Immersive geospatial learning for flood disaster education: Integrating GIS, augmented reality, spatial literacy, and ecopedagogy
abstract: Flood disasters remain a recurring challenge in many regions and underscore the importance of educational approaches that help students understand environmental risks and develop preparedness capacities. Although Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Augmented Reality (AR), spatial literacy, and environmental learning have gained increasing attention in disaster education, these elements are often implemented independently, limiting opportunities for more integrated learning experiences. This research designed and evaluated immersive geospatial learning for flood disaster education by bringing
journal: Journal of Education and e-Learning Research

title: Evaluation and combination of multi-sensor shipborne gravity surveys in the German exclusive economic zone of the North Sea
abstract: Between 2015 and 2024, a series of five shipborne gravimetry campaigns was conducted within the German exclusive economic zone of the North Sea and adjacent waters. The goal was to obtain an accurate, consistent and properly 3D geo-referenced gravity dataset in the area. This shall serve to compute the marine geoid as the official height reference surface in the German territorial waters, and to validate and calibrate less accurate and reliable historical shipborne gravity data available in the area. title: From sea to farm: Repurposing invasive macroalgae into biocidal and defense-enhancing tools against tomato late blight (Phytophthora infestans)
abstract: Marine seaweeds are increasingly recognized as sources of bioactive compounds with potential applications in sustainable agriculture, including as biocontrol agents. The selection of invasive species such as Asparagopsis armata and Sargassum muticum offers a dual benefit: obtaining bioactive metabolites from a low-cost resource while simultaneously mitigating their ecological impacts using this harmful biomass. title: Waterbirds of Atrangarai Estuary, Southeastern India: A First Baseline Assessment with Emphasis on Breeding Waterbirds at a Traditional Fishing Center
abstract: Estuarine ecosystems provide important feeding, roosting and breeding habitats for waterbirds, yet many smaller coastal wetlands remain poorly documented. Atrangarai Estuary, a traditional fishing center on the southeastern coast of India, has received no systematic ornithological attention. We conducted monthly surveys (August 2025 to July 2026) to document the composition, richness, abundance and breeding activity of waterbirds. title: Spatial variability of soil fertility indicators using GIS for sustainable land management in Banaskantha district western India
abstract: Soil fertility assessment is fundamental for sustainable land management and precision agriculture, particularly in semi-arid regions where soil properties exhibit considerable spatial variability. This study investigated the spatial distribution of major soil fertility indicators across Banaskantha district, Gujarat, India, using a systematic 15 × 15 km grid-based sampling approach integrated with Geographic Information System (GIS) analysis and multivariate statistics. title: Mapping perennial brown macroalgae in the Baltic sea using multitemporal Sentinel-2 imagery
abstract: Satellite observations can extend benthic biodiversity monitoring beyond sparse point surveys, but their value depends on robust field validation and transparent uncertainty. We used high-quality Sentinel-2 MSI (S2) imagery from 2016–2023 and ground-truth observations to map the spatial extent of ecologically significant perennial brown macroalgae habitats across three Baltic Sea sites: Vilsandi (Estonia), Gotland and Blekinge (Sweden). title: Worldwide water gaps: Using relative elevation modelling to identify transverse drainages
abstract: Transverse drainages are stream reaches that flow through, rather than around, topographic high grounds. The development of transverse drainage is intimately tied to the tectonic history of an area, but the identification of transverse reaches has historically been a matter of subjective opinion. Here, a GIS-based method is presented that uses relative elevation modelling to identify and quantify transverse stream reaches. title: Futurities: human extinction, space visualization and the other side of sustainability
abstract: This paper explores how speculative practices engage with evolving ideas on human extinction, space cosmology, post-humanism, and sustainability through expanded photography. Focusing on two projects—Here There Are Lions by Ioannis Galanopoulos Papavasileiou and Alien Landscapes by Ioannis Kontos—it examines how these works reframe themes of planetary precarity, space migration, and ecological collapse. title: Exploratory Spatiotemporal Analysis and Preliminary Conditional Scenarios of Land Cover and Surface Temperature for Sustainable Coastal Planning: A Case Study of Arraial do Cabo (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil)
abstract: Evaluating spatiotemporal dynamics is essential to measure and monitor environmental sustainability in coastal zones under rapid urban expansion. Future scenarios of the earth’s surface can be estimated from identified changes in remote sensing. The objectives of this study were to evaluate changes in the land surface temperature (LST), estimated with Landsat 8 images of the Brazilian coastal municipality of Arraial do Cabo on two summer dates—2014 and 2017—and to project a scenario for 2030. abstract: In oligotrophic oceans, the stoichiometric ratios of apparent oxygen utilization (AOU) to nutrients often deviate from the classical Redfield ratio, yet the mechanisms remain poorly constrained. Contrary to the commonly held view that these ratios are typically elevated, we found that the mean ratios of AOU to dissolved inorganic nitrogen (DIN) and AOU to dissolved inorganic phosphorus (DIP) over the upper 2000 m of the oligotrophic Northwest Pacific are only 6.28 and 86.79, respectively, both below the classical values of 8.6 and 138. title: Native biocrust microbes modulate salinity‐driven recruitment filters in coastal wetlands
abstract: Abstract Introduction Mediterranean coastal wetlands are biodiversity hotspots increasingly threatened by climate change, particularly by salinization, which strongly constrains plant recruitment during early life stages. Native soil microbiota may provide nature‐based solutions (NbS) to enhance plant establishment under saline conditions. title: Satellite telemetry suggests significant regional variation in post-fledging survival of Adélie penguins
abstract: Abstract Post-fledging periods represent one of the most vulnerable stages for juvenile seabirds. Adélie penguins Pygoscelis adeliae must quickly develop foraging skills while minimizing predation risk immediately after fledging. In the Antarctic Peninsula (AP) region, where populations are declining, previous studies have suggested that an acute post-fledging survival bottleneck exists. title: Multi-hazard risk mapping using geospatial techniques in coastal Bangladesh: implications for resilience
abstract: Coastal areas play a vital role in supporting livelihoods, resources, and economic activities, yet in Bangladesh they are highly vulnerable to climate-induced hazards such as cyclones, floods, salinity intrusion, and erosion. These hazards are expected to intensify under changing climatic conditions, increasing risks to coastal communities. This study focuses on Kalapara Upazila in the southern coastal region of Bangladesh and develops an integrated multi-hazard risk map using geospatial techniques. title: Seasonal water quality assessment and GIS-based pollution mapping of the Brantas River toward sustainable water management and SDG 6
abstract: Abstract The Brantas River is an important freshwater resource supporting domestic, agricultural, industrial, and ecological functions in East Java, Indonesia. Increasing urbanization, industrial expansion, agricultural intensification, and population growth have contributed to substantial environmental pressures on river water quality, creating challenges for sustainable watershed management and Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6) implementation. title: Aftermath of rebuilding low-head dams in river basins: hydraulic study of two rivers located in the northern and western hydrological regions of Estonia
abstract: Localized and distributed energy losses arising from the extreme flow conditions at the lowland rivers' barriers are hydraulically estimated. To perform a standard hydraulic analysis of rapidly varying flows at two Estonian rivers’ sites, specific-energy and momentum-equation functions for the channels with non-rectangular cross-sections are introduced. title: Historical ecology of the Swan Islands (Islas del Cisne) chronicles long-term anthropogenic changes in the Western Caribbean
abstract: Abstract The Swan Islands in the western Caribbean Sea are two of the most remote islands in the region given their diminutive size, distance from land masses, relative isolation from larger human settlements, and lack of accessibility historically. Despite these features, they have been highly sought out by a succession of explorers, naturalists, and biologists since the late 1800s under the guise of studying “pristine” natural places seemingly unspoiled by humans. title: Environmental controls on zooplankton community composition across the Bangladesh coast: integrating hydrochemistry, multivariate ordination, and threshold indicator analysis
abstract: Understanding the impact of hydrochemical variability on zooplankton communities is fundamental for assessing the ecological status of coastal ecosystems. This study investigated how seasonal and spatial hydrochemical conditions shaped zooplankton communities across three contrasting coastal ecosystems of Bangladesh using multivariate approaches and threshold indicator taxa analysis (TITAN). title: Environmental distribution and polymer characterization of microplastics in the Miagao Estuary, Iloilo, Philippines
abstract: The Philippines contributes significantly to marine plastic pollution, yet little is known about microplastics (MPs) in its many estuaries. This study was the first to examine how many MPs are present, where they are located, and what types are present in Brgy. Baybay Sur, Miagao, Iloilo. Surface water samples were collected from three sampling sites: sample site 1 (SP1), sample site 2 (SP2), and sample site 3 (SP3) along the estuary, then separated, and MPs were isolated. title: Identification of Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) Along Kerala Coast, India
abstract: Parameters that refer to fish existence can be identified by remote sensing techniques using satellite sensor data. Identification of potential fishing zones with the aid of remote sensing technology is a crucial need for the fisher flocks to get profitable catch by less fuel consumption, effort, and time as well. In this study, two different parameters, chlorophyll concentration and sea surface temperature (SST), were taken from satellite-derived data. title: Weak governance, cumulative impacts, and socioeconomic factors driving vulnerability in coastal small-scale fisheries
abstract: Abstract This study analyzes the dynamics of vulnerability in coastal small-scale fisheries under high level of pressure from port-industrial complex in Baixada Santista, Brazil. We employed a socioeconomic survey ( n = 401), transdisciplinary focus-group workshops ( n = 6) with fishers ( n = 40), and stakeholder semi-structured interviews ( n = 5). title: Co-creating eco-visualizations: a human–AI collaborative pipeline for data-driven visual design
abstract: Abstract Communicating complex environmental phenomena requires forms of visualization that go beyond analytical accuracy to support engagement, interpretation, and reflection. Eco-visualization addresses this challenge by combining data representation with aesthetic and narrative elements, but its creation often demands technical skills. This paper presents a Human–AI co-creative pipeline for the design of eco-visualizations, in which AI acts as an active collaborator throughout the visual creation process. journal: Journal of Ambient Intelligence and Humanized Computing

title: Serra Gelada (Alicante, Spain): Evidence and implications of a paleo-island setting during the Jurassic-Cretaceous transition
abstract: This study revisits the uppermost Jurassic-lowermost Cretaceous succession of Serra Gelada (Alicante, SE Spain) based on new field observations and petrographic analyses. It is the second publication presenting and discussing results and interpretations of the PhD thesis of the first author, defended forty years ago. title: Insult to Injury: Population Impacts of Sublethal Entanglement and Vessel Strikes of Common Bottlenose Dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) in Barataria Basin, Louisiana, 2011–2023
abstract: ABSTRACT Human interactions, specifically fishery entanglements (FI) and vessel strikes (VI), threaten marine mammals, including the Barataria Bay Estuarine System (BBE) Stock of common bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ). We reviewed whole‐body photographs to estimate the prevalence of sublethal entanglement and vessel strike scars for 227 dolphins sampled during catch‐and‐release health assessments, with 128 dolphins meeting analysis criteria. title: Under-water ignition and combustion of PDMS processed Al/CuO nanoparticle composite
abstract: This study investigates the fabrication and performance of hydrophobic nanothermite powders prepared by combining liquid polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) prepolymers with thermite powders in a dispersion medium. The resulting composite remained dry when submerged underwater and could be ignited by laser irradiation. High-speed imaging measurements showed an ignition delay of 2.3 ms under underwater conditions. title: Macroalgae respond to consumer‐mediated nutrient cycling in a temperate ecosystem
abstract: Primary production in coastal upwelling regions has often been presumed to be supported primarily by allochthonous nutrients, but inconsistent nutrient delivery and the metabolic cost of nitrate assimilation can leave producers nitrogen limited during the growing season. As a potential supplement for insufficient allochthonous supply, nutrient provisioning through the metabolic wastes of animals, termed consumer-mediated nutrient cycling (CNC), provides easily assimilated nitrogen in the form of ammonium. abstract: This research aims to detect subsurface discontinuities influencing groundwater flow in the Mô watershed by integrating gravimetric anomaly processing and SRTM Digital Elevation Model (DEM) analysis within a GIS framework. Gravity data from Geosoft Oasis Montaj underwent advanced filtering including reduction to the equator, vertical/horizontal derivatives, Tilt derivative, analytic signal, and Euler deconvolution to extract geostructural information. abstract: This article presents the results of a study on the distribution and monitoring of the large humpbacked saxaul locust found in saxaul agrophytocenoses of the Southern Aral Sea region. The research was conducted in the Muynak district of the Republic of Karakalpakstan. The coordinates of the pest’s habitats were determined using a GPS device, and electronic maps were created based on the ArcGIS Pro software. title: Iron rich concretions accelerate localized degradation of marine recovered bluish white glaze
abstract: Iron-rich concretions are common on marine-recovered ceramics, but their role in glaze degradation remains poorly constrained. We combine archaeological characterization of bluish-white porcelain from the Nanhai I shipwreck with controlled replica exposures to evaluate how iron-rich microenvironments affect glaze alteration. title: Development and Web-Based Visualization of a Domain-Specific Semantic Model for Coffee Culture and Production Processes
abstract: The global agricultural supply chain is a complex network with different data silos, complicated cultivation parameters and highly subjective sensory evaluation metrics. Formal knowledge representation is a must, if real semantic interoperability is to be achieved across this multidimensional domain. This work consists of the rigorous design, implementation and quantitative evaluation of the “Coffee Culture and Production Processes Ontology” and a custom client-side web-application named the “Coffee Ontology Explorer”. title: Building-level demolition and material output forecasting using 4d-GIS: a case study of Kitakyushu City, Japan
abstract: Abstract This study proposes a disaggregated modeling approach to estimate building-level demolition probabilities and project future material output. Many existing Material Stock and Flow Analysis (MSFA) studies rely on aggregated spatial units at national, prefectural, or municipal levels, which limits their ability to capture intra-urban variation. To address this issue, a Weibull Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) model was applied to building-level data in Kitakyushu City, Japan, incorporating structural, locational, and demographic variables. title: Long-lived replenishment of magmas in the oceanic upper mantle revealed by chromite nodules in ophiolites
abstract: Magmas produced at depth pass through the upper mantle before they form oceanic crust at spreading centers, but the timescales and thermal evolution of magma replenishment remain poorly constrained. Chromite nodules of ophiolites formed in magma conduits in the upper mantle and record these processes. title: Preliminary comparative assessment of Vibrio harveyi virulence in Galleria mellonella larvae and European sea bass
abstract: Vibrio harveyi is a major bacterial pathogen in Mediterranean aquaculture, causing high mortality and economic losses, particularly in European sea bass ( Dicentrarchus labrax ). Despite extensive efforts to develop vaccines, no effective commercial option exists, highlighting the need to better understand infection mechanisms. Studies using fish hosts are labor-intensive, costly, and ethically demanding, emphasizing the value of alternative in vivo models. title: Data-driven Atlas of Acinetobacter baumannii vaccine research: a multi-database bibliometric and visualization analysis
abstract: Introduction Acinetobacter baumannii is a major multidrug-resistant pathogen for which effective preventive strategies are urgently needed. This study aimed to characterize the global research landscape, knowledge structure, and emerging trends in Acinetobacter baumannii vaccine research. Methods Publications from 2011 to 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus. After integration, deduplication, and independent screening, 243 publications were included. title: Bridging the gap between genomic, phenotypic, and modeling data in picophytoplankton–virus interactions
abstract: We present a comprehensive synthesis of recent developments in methodological approaches to combine experimental and genomic studies of picophytoplankton-virus interactions. This synthesis will not only enhance our understanding of these relationships but also stimulate new hypotheses for the interpretation of metagenomic data and enrich current modeling efforts. Marine picophytoplankton are significant primary producers despite their low contribution to biomass. title: GIS-Based Multi-Criteria Modelling of Soil Erosion Susceptibility Using AHP in Ikere-Ekiti, Southwestern Nigeria
abstract: Soil erosion remains a critical environmental challenge in tropical regions, particularly in areas experiencing rapid land-use change and geomorphic instability. This study presents a GIS-based multi-criteria modelling approach for assessing soil erosion susceptibility in Ikere-Ekiti, Southwestern Nigeria. Twelve conditioning factors-land use/land cover (LULC), slope, aspect, elevation, drainage density, soil type, rainfall, Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), geology, rainfall erosivity (R-factor), soil erodibility (K-factor), and Topographic Wetness Index (TWI)-were integrated usi

title: Reproductive cycle influences trace metal(loid) distribution in the spottail mantis shrimp Squilla mantis from the Adriatic Sea
abstract: This study investigated the accumulation of 13 metal(oid) s (Ag, Al, As, Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Fe, Hg, Mn, Ni, Pb, and Zn) in muscle and gonadal edible tissues of Squilla mantis from the central Adriatic Sea, considering pre-spawning, spawning, and post-spawning reproductive phases. title: Integrated electrochemical modelling, spatial site selection, and multi-objective optimization of renewable-powered alkaline water electrolysis for green hydrogen production
abstract: Green hydrogen produced through renewable-powered alkaline water electrolysis represents a promising pathway toward decarbonization; however, large-scale deployment requires integrated optimization of site selection, electrolyzer operation, and energy system design. This study presents an integrated framework combining GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis, an electrochemical alkaline electrolyzer model benchmarked against literature experimental data, and multi-objective optimization to evaluate off-grid, desalination-supported green hydrogen production systems. title: A scenario-based estimate of sediment organic carbon storage in Posidonia oceanica meadows of the Croatian Adriatic
abstract: Coastal vegetated ecosystems are increasingly recognised for their role in long-term carbon sequestration, yet spatially explicit estimates of sediment organic carbon (C org ) stocks remain unavailable for many Mediterranean regions. In the Adriatic Sea, no region-specific sediment carbon core data currently exist, limiting regional blue carbon assessments and their integration into ecosystem-based management. This study provides a scenario-based estimate of the potential sediment C org stocks in P. oceanica meadows in the Croatian Adriatic. Study-level sediment C org stocks (0–1 m depth) were

title: GIS-Based Geospatial Assessment of Net Land Surface Change for Identifying Erosion-Accretion Hotspots Along the Padma River in Bangladesh
abstract: Erosion is a continuous natural process that reshapes Earth’s surface. It causes geohazards, loss of fertile lands, and has detrimental effects on the environment. This study provides an extensive analysis of erosion and accretion patterns over decades along both banks of the Padma River, the main distributary of the Ganges. Satellite images from Landsat and Sentinel were processed in ArcGIS to extract and compare banklines using a 5 km river-reach framework to identify net land surface change and erosion-accretion hotspots. title: Sustainability put to the test: environment and regional spatial planning in Chilean public policy (1994–2021)
abstract: This article reconstructs and analyzes the evolution of sustainability in regional-scale spatial planning in Chile between 1994 and 2021. It identifies four phases of normative evolution, from the first legal frameworks to the incorporation of Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) and recent policies, using a qualitative–quantitative mixed design that combines content analysis of 11 instruments with exploratory visualization through MDS and clustering and inferential testing through PERMANOVA. title: Benchmarking Dimensionality Reduction Methods for Livestock Transcriptomic Data: A Comparative Analysis of Visualization, Clustering, and Classification Performance
abstract: Dimensionality reduction methods play a critical role in the analysis and visualization of high-dimensional transcriptomic datasets. In this study, the clustering and classification performances of Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Kernel Principal Component Analysis (Kernel PCA), t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE), and Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) were compared using two independent livestock microarray datasets (GSE20552 and GSE24560) obtained from the GEO database. The performance of the methods was evaluated using Silhouette score, Davies–Bouldin

title: CoSAG-nf: A Scalable Nextflow Pipeline for Co-assembly, Optimization, and Interactive Visualization of High-Throughput Single-Cell Genomes
abstract: MOTIVATION: Single-cell amplified genomes (SAGs) are crucial for resolving intra-population microbial heterogeneity and accurately understanding the metabolic potential of microbial dark matter populations. However, SAGs generated through multiple displacement amplification (MDA) of genomic DNA from single cells with single-copy chromosomes are highly fragmented and prone to contamination, severely hindering high-quality genome reconstruction and functional analysis, which greatly limits their scientific utility. title: Sense of Place and Customary Legitimacy in Marine Protected Area Co‐Management: Evidence From Beloi Village, Atauro Island, Timor‐Leste
abstract: ABSTRACT Marine protected areas increasingly depend on social legitimacy, customary authority and community participation, yet the interaction between sense of place and conservation behaviour remains insufficiently understood in small‐island settings. This study examined how place attachment, place dependence, place identity, perceived Tara Bandu effectiveness and co‐management satisfaction were associated with conservation behaviour in Beloi Village, Atauro Island, Timor‐Leste. title: From Principle to Practice: A Pragmatic Pathway for Ecosystem-Based Fisheries Management in a Data-limited RFMO
abstract: The Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA) is legally mandated through its founding agreement to implement an Ecosystem Approach to Fisheries Management (EAFM). However, like many Regional Fisheries Management Organizations (RFMOs), translating this principle into effective practice poses significant challenges, particularly in data-limited environments. This viewpoint paper traces SIOFA’s pragmatic journey in operationalizing EAFM. journal: Journal of Northwest Atlantic Fishery Science

title: Investigation on the Steady‑state of Gas–liquid Two-phase Swirling Flow Differential Pressure Based on Visualization Experiments
abstract: Unreliable radial differential pressure (RDP) measurements in gas–liquid two-phase flow are caused by variable flow patterns. To address this challenge, an approach based on active swirl regulation is reported to stabilize flow patterns and improve RDP measurement accuracy. Using an indoor visualization experimental system, the variations and underlying mechanisms of axial differential pressure (ADP) and RDP with gas and liquid flow under the action of a vane-type swirler were investigated. Luoyang Institute of Science and Technology

title: Delineation of groundwater potential zones using analytical hierarchy process and GIS in Bhilangana Block of Tehri Garhwal District, Uttarakhand, India
abstract: Groundwater is one of the most reliable freshwater resources globally, but overexploitation has led to declining water tables, deteriorating water quality, and increased water scarcity. These problems have raised serious questions about how sustainable groundwater management can be achieved. In recent times, geospatial techniques and the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) have been increasingly applied to assess groundwater availability. title: Assessing Forest Resource Depletion and Rural Livelihood Sustainability in Ovia Southwest, Nigeria using Remote Sensing, GIS, and Qualitative Socio-Economic Data
abstract: Forest resources are fundamental to rural livelihoods in sub-Saharan Africa, yet rapid land-use change threatens their sustainability. This study assessed forest cover change, available forest resources, socio-economic drivers of household dependence, and community perceptions of forest contributions to socio-economic development in Ovia Southwest LGA., Edo State, Nigeria. A mixed-methods approach was used to integrate remote sensing and GIS analysis of Landsat imagery (1987–2024), a household survey (n = 390), factor analysis, multiple regression, and chi-square tests. title: Spatio-Temporal Mapping and Analysis of Surface-Water Dynamics in Kopa Dam, Niger State, Nigeria, Using Sentinel-2 Level-2A and GIS Techniques
abstract: Surface-water extent provides a spatial measure of reservoir condition and supports water-resource monitoring where field observations are limited. This study assessed the spatio-temporal dynamics of surface water in Kopa Dam, Niger State, Nigeria, from January 2022 to January 2026 using Sentinel-2 Level-2A imagery and the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI). One image was selected for January of each year to maintain seasonal consistency. MNDWI was calculated using the green band (B03) and shortwave infrared band (B11), with B11 resampled to 10 m. title: From Disruption to Recovery: A Social Big Data Analysis of Sport Tourism Discourse During and After COVID-19
abstract: This study investigates how online discourse on sport tourism was structured during the COVID-19 pandemic and reshaped as tourism entered a period of recovery and restructuring. The analysis covered two three-year periods: 1 July 2020–30 June 2023, representing the pandemic and early recovery period, and 1 July 2023–30 June 2026, representing the post-pandemic recovery and restructuring period. Unstructured online texts related to sport tourism were collected and processed through text cleaning, morphological analysis, and stop-word removal. abstract: Considerable isotopic variation between Earth and major chondritic materials implies a possible fractionation in the early differentiate stage of the Earth. However, it is challenging to study isotopic fractionation at the high pressures relevant to the deep Earth due to the lack of natural samples. title: PLACE-BASED WELLNESS TOURISM ARCHITECTURE AT THE DEAD SEA: ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCES, SPATIAL SYSTEMS, AND OPERATIONAL SUSTAINABILITY
abstract: Wellness and health tourism has experienced significant global growth, driven by increasing demand for integrated therapeutic experiences that combine natural resources, environmental context, architecture, and interior design. The Dead Sea is one of the world’s most prominent wellness destinations due to its exceptional climatic and mineral properties. However, hotel architecture in the region often continues to follow conventional hospitality models that emphasize general leisure amenities rather than spatially integrated therapeutic systems rooted in the specificity of place. title: Pemodelan spasial tingkat kerawanan banjir rob di Benua Kayong, Kabupaten Ketapang Kalimantan Barat
abstract: Abstrak. abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, the dynamic behaviors of the generalized (3 + )‐dimensional Kadomtsev‐Petviashvili equation, an important mathematical model for nonlinear wave propagation, are examined through interaction solutions. Using interaction solutions such as breather, two‐wave, and lump periodic solutions, the interactions between the solitary wave solutions of the equation and their dynamic characteristics are analyzed in detail. title: Environmental forcing of winter spawning grounds on the abundance trend of Pacific saury (Cololabis saira) in the Northwest Pacific
abstract: Pacific saury (Cololabis saira) is a highly migratory pelagic fish with a short lifespan, whose recruitment is highly sensitive to environmental fluctuations. This study investigated the drivers of recruitment by establishing a statistical relationship between winter spawning conditions and fishery-dependent abundance indices from 2013 to 2023. Specifically, we hypothesize that winter spawning habitat conditions pre-determine year-class strength by jointly regulating parental spawning success and the survival of eggs and larvae throughout their early life history. title: Phylogeographic epidemiology of Dabie bandavirus in East Asia: divergent transmission networks and genotype‑linked clinical severity
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus (SFTSV), exhibits geographically decoupled incidence and fatality patterns across East Asia. We aimed to elucidate the distinct ecological drivers and phylogeographic dynamics underlying this inland-coastal epidemiological divergence. title: Acoustic assessment of industrial noise generated by operational installations in the RA1K refinery, Skikda (Algeria)
abstract: Industrial noise pollution poses significant occupational and environmental challenges in large petrochemical plants. This study presents an acoustic assessment and GIS-based spatial modelling of noise in the RA1K refinery, Skikda (Algeria). Field measurements using an A-weighted sound level meter were used to determine LAeq (equivalent continuous sound pressure level), LAmax (maximum sound pressure level), and LAmin (minimum sound pressure level) at multiple monitoring locations. title: Reproductive Biology of Bombay Duck (Harpadon nehereus) as a Basis for Sustainable Management in the Malacca Strait
abstract: The Bombay duck (Harpadon nehereus), a common bycatch species found in various coastal fisheries, has experienced a global population decline. Studies on its reproductive biology, distinguishing between males and females, are still limited, particularly in the Strait of Malacca. This study aimed to investigate sexual dimorphism in the reproductive biology of H. nehereus, including body length distribution, length-weight relationship, growth pattern and coefficient, condition factor (K), hepatosomatic index (HSI), sex ratio, and gonadal maturity stage (GMS). title: Population genomics, demography, and circum-Baltic connectivity of Early Medieval southwestern Finland
abstract: BACKGROUND: Knowledge of Early Medieval Finland (1050-1250 CE) relies primarily on archaeological evidence, as contemporary sources are scarce. The available evidence indicates two distinct cultural-economic zones: coastal and inland. Using newly generated genomic data from 34 ancient individuals alongside modern Finnish genomes, we characterise Late Iron Age and Early Medieval ancestry in southwestern Finland, reconstruct demographic patterns, and place individuals within a circum-Baltic relatedness network. title: Land cover transformations in northern Algeria from 2001 to 2021: A MODIS-based spatiotemporal analysis
abstract: Land use/land cover (LULC) changes in northern Algeria from 2001 to 2021 were investigated in this research. The assessment utilized the MODIS MCD12Q1 dataset combined with Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques. Substantial landscape transformations were highlighted by the findings. Forests (+47.52%), shrublands (+17.65%), wetlands (+58.64%), and natural vegetation (+465.72%) experienced notable growth, whereas a drop of −14.13% was documented for barren lands by the end of study period. title: The marine drug plitidepsin alleviates osteoporosis in estrogen-deficient mice by suppressing ROS-mediated NRF2/HO-1 signaling and osteoclast formation
abstract: Abstract Marine-derived compounds represent an important source of innovative therapeutics owing to their structural diversity and broad bioactivity; however, their potential in osteoporosis therapy remains insufficiently explored. This study investigated the effects of plitidepsin (Pli), a marine-origin cyclic peptide, on osteoclast differentiation and bone loss associated with estrogen deficiency. title: Widespread declines of formerly common species reshape local assemblages over time
abstract: Abstract Despite dramatic human-driven changes across ecosystems, local-scale aggregate biodiversity metrics are often surprisingly stable, even as communities experience substantial reorganization of species identities and relative abundances. While rare species are often thought to be more vulnerable to these changes, emerging evidence suggests that common species may experience disproportionately greater declines. title: Synergistic regulation of soil water and salt through mud blanket mulching and raised fields improves rainfed winter wheat yield on coastal saline-alkali land
abstract: Soil salinization induced by shallow saline groundwater severely limits rain-fed winter wheat yield in the Bohai Rim coastal region. Although mulching effectively suppresses salt accumulation, the interactive effect of mulching type and groundwater depth has not been clearly defined, and alternatives to plastic film are urgently required. title: Assessment of the Current Sanitary and Technical Condition of Irrigation Reservoirs in Azerbaijan
abstract: The article presents a comprehensive assessment of the current sanitary and technical condition of irrigation reservoirs in Azerbaijan, analyzing the operational characteristics of hydraulic structures, the level of technical deterioration, and the primary risk factors affecting their safe operation. The study aims to determine the condition of reservoirs vital to irrigation systems, identify factors influencing operational reliability, and evaluate the applicability of modern monitoring and management approaches. title: Spot the difference: Turbidity‐driven plasticity and variation in spotted grunter ( Pomadasys commersonnii ) spot patterns
abstract: Animal body markings such as spots, stripes and patterns play important roles in camouflage and visual communication. This study investigated phenotypic plasticity in the spot patterns of spotted grunter Pomadasys commersonnii, an estuarine-dependent haemulid species. First, an aquarium experiment (n = 24) examined plasticity in spot patterns under contrasting turbidity conditions. title: A conceptual nexus framework integrating mangrove management with water energy and food planning in Hamata Egypt
abstract: Abstract Remote coastal settlements in Egypt face interconnected water, energy, food, and ecosystem pressures that are often addressed through fragmented sectoral approaches. Existing Water–Energy–Food (WEF) nexus studies increasingly emphasize governance, while mangrove research generally focuses on ecosystem services rather than cross-sector resource planning. title: Instance segmentation model applied to automated palynofacies area-ratio quantification analysis for black shales of T-OAE
abstract: For the purpose of this study, an instance segmentation pipeline based on the YOLOv26 model was used for automated detection, classification, visualization, and quantitative analysis of palynofacies in black shales from the Toarcian Oceanic Anoxic Event (T-OAE). institutions: Ankara Atatürk Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi

title: Surveillance of Mytella strigata using eDNA and local ecological knowledge: implications for management and alternative feed use
abstract: The brackish-water mussel Mytella strigata, native to Central and South America, has recently spread to Asian waters, raising concerns for aquaculture and biodiversity. This study presents a regional assessment along India’s southwest coast, integrating local ecological knowledge (LEK), environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring, and nutritional analysis. title: Targeted gene expression analysis of Streptococcus mutans interaction with oral epithelial cells in a co-culture model
abstract: ABSTRACT Streptococcus mutans is recognized as the principal etiological agent of dental caries and has also been implicated in systemic diseases such as bacterial endocarditis and inflammatory bowel disorders. Its pathogenicity is strongly associated with virulence traits, including quorum sensing, biofilm formation, and oxidative stress response. abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the in vitro inhibitory activity of different Angelica dahurica-Ligusticum sinense extracts (ethanolic, aqueous, and cold-pressed) against planktonic cells and biofilms of Malassezia furfur. METHODS: Ultra-performance liquid chromatography (UPLC) was used to quantify the major constituents. title: Spatial turnover and bioregional structure of reptile assemblages across Türkiye
abstract: Türkiye represents one of the most important biogeographic transition areas in the Mediterranean Basin, linking Mediterranean, Euro-Siberian, and Irano-Turanian biotas. Owing to its complex topography, climatic heterogeneity, and geological history, the country harbors exceptionally diverse reptile assemblages. However, large-scale quantitative analyses of reptile community structure across Türkiye remain limited. title: Climate change impacts and resilience pathways in somalia through a systematic review
abstract: Somalia is among the most climate-vulnerable countries worldwide, characterized by predominantly arid and semi-arid regions increasingly affected by recurrent droughts, irregular precipitation, rising temperatures, land degradation, and water scarcity, all of which compromise livelihoods, food security, and socio-economic stability. title: Effect of processing and germination on the nutritional and bioactive properties of black amaranth ( Amaranthus hybridus ) cultivated over 2,700 m above sea level in Apurimac
abstract: Black amaranth (Amaranthus hybridus), an Andean pseudocereal, was evaluated to assess the effects of germination, roasting, and cooking on its nutritional profile, protein structure (SDS‒PAGE and FTIR), color, polyphenol content, antioxidant capacity (DPPH and ABTS), and flavonoids. title: Pronounced megafaunal community transition driven by polymetallic nodule cover in the Northwest Pacific abyss
abstract: Polymetallic nodules provide essential hard substrata for benthic fauna and are widely assumed to enhance biodiversity on abyssal plains. Yet, our understanding of how nodule cover shapes megafaunal communities remains limited and largely restricted to low nodule cover conditions. Using a large image dataset from a nodule-rich abyssal basin in the northwest Pacific (NWP), we characterized megafaunal communities and quantitatively assessed their responses across a broad gradient of nodule cover. title: DNA metabarcoding illuminates nestling diet of the at-risk Western Purple Martin ( Progne subis arboricola )
abstract: The Western Purple Martin (Progne subis arboricola) is an aerial insectivore of conservation concern throughout the Pacific Northwest in the continental USA. In contrast to the widely studied eastern subspecies (Progne subis subis), there is a paucity of information on Western Purple Martin life history and ecology. Aside from anecdotal observations, there is no information on prey use or diet of the Western Purple Martin. title: Biocontrol potential and genomic analysis of novel lytic bacteriophage CABI-SEA 2302 against multidrug-resistant avian pathogenic Escherichia coli associated with colibacillosis
abstract: Multidrug-resistant avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (MDR-APEC) causes critically high first-week mortality in chickens, resulting in substantial economic losses in the global poultry industry. This study aimed to isolate and characterize a novel bacteriophage as an effective safe alternative for the control of colibacillosis. A lytic bacteriophage CABI-SEA 2302 was obtained from E. coli lesion samples collected from commercial poultry farms. title: Impact of Urbanization on Agriculture and Wetland Management in Makurdi LGA of Benue State, Nigeria
abstract: Wetlands are among the most productive ecosystems, providing essential ecological, hydrological, and socio-economic services, including flood regulation, groundwater recharge, water purification, biodiversity conservation, and agricultural support. However, rapid urbanization has accelerated the conversion of wetlands to built-up areas and agricultural land, threatening their ecological integrity. This study assessed the impact of urbanization on agriculture and wetland management in Makurdi Local Government Area, Benue State, over a twenty-year period (2004–2024). title: Microplastics, much more than water contaminants: Environmental trajectory and the state of particles at exposure
abstract: Microplastics were initially recognized and investigated primarily as aquatic contaminants, but they are now known to circulate among atmospheric, terrestrial, freshwater, and marine environments. Their significance therefore extends beyond their occurrence in individual environmental compartments. title: First report on morphometrics, length–weight relationship, feeding habit, and diet composition of Trichopodus trichopterus from Tra Su, An Giang, Vietnam
abstract: Abstract This study aimed to provide preliminary biological data on Trichopodus trichopterus (Pallas, 1770), an ecologically and economically essential freshwater species in the Mekong Delta, focusing on its external morphology, growth pattern, feeding habit, and diet composition. Specimens were collected from Tra Su (An Giang Province) in March 2025 and analyzed in the laboratory. title: Using a trait-based framework to characterize farmed seaweeds and guide selection of new candidates
abstract: Abstract Seaweed aquaculture could meet the “triple bottom line” of environmental, social, and economic sustainability. However, while seaweeds in nature are incredibly diverse, only eight species are responsible for >95% of production, leaving untapped potential. We use a trait-based framework to identify candidate seaweed species for commercial production. title: Bacterial extracellular vesicles as players in biofilm dynamics and community interactions
abstract: The ability to use vesicles to deliver cargo safely across distance is a valuable strategy that appears to be universal across all life. The ability of prokaryotes to accomplish this is a relatively new idea, but one that is expanding rapidly. In this review, we will describe what bacterial extracellular vesicles (bEVs) are and where they come from. title: SeaMamba: Frequency-Stabilized Selective State-Space Multiscale Detection for SAR Ships in Complex Maritime Scenes
abstract: Ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery remains challenging because near-shore clutter, coherent speckle noise, dense scattering responses, and large target-scale variations often obscure vessel boundaries and weaken small-ship signatures. Although single-stage detectors provide efficient inference, their predominantly local convolutional modeling and fixed multiscale fusion strategies are insufficient for capturing long-range sea-surface context and adaptively emphasizing discriminative ship responses. title: AN INTEGRATED ASSESSMENT OF GROUNDWATER PHYSICOCHEMICAL QUALITY AND LAND USE/LAND COVER DYNAMICS IN THE PENNA RIVER BASIN, YSR KADAPA DISTRICT, INDIA
abstract: Groundwater is a critical component of water security in the semi-arid landscapes of southern India, where seasonal recharge, geology, agriculture and changing land cover can jointly influence water chemistry. This study presents an integrated assessment of groundwater physicochemical characteristics and land use/land cover (LULC) dynamics in the Penna River Basin within YSR Kadapa District, Andhra Pradesh, using the study framework and results developed during the 2022–2026 assessment period. title: Subdued surface expression of deep cave collapse
abstract: Cave systems can be difficult to recognise where karst landforms are subdued or overprinted with other landscape processes. Subtle linear depressions on carbonate platforms are commonly interpreted as fluvial or tectonic landforms, but may also mark collapse above underlying cave systems. We test this on the Nullarbor Plain, southern Australia, a stable >200,000 km² carbonate platform exposed for >14 Myr. title: Geopolitical Risk and Economic Uncertainty in Small Open Economies: Rethinking Resilience in the Caribbean
abstract: The global economic system is undergoing profound transformation, shaped by heightened uncertainty, intensifying geopolitical tensions, economic fragmentation and enduring structural vulnerabilities. Small Island Developing States, particularly those in the Caribbean, are disproportionately exposed to these shifts because of their economic openness, narrow production bases, high import dependence, limited fiscal space and vulnerability to climate-related shocks. Yet within this turbulence lies an opportunity to redefine economic relations, strengthen resilience and diversify pathways to growth
journal: Journal of Economics and Development Studies

title: Long-term diatom response to anthropogenic stressors in a Neotropical lake
abstract: Understanding tropical lake ecosystem responses to anthropogenic disturbance over long timescales is critical for assessing resistance, resilience, and regime shifts; however, such perspectives are rare in the Neotropics. We combined paleolimnological, limnological, and remote-sensing approaches to evaluate the response of a shallow tropical maar lake in the Sierra de Los Tuxtlas (eastern Mexico) to deforestation-driven disturbance over the last ~200 years, with emphasis on ecosystem trajectories following peak impact in the late twentieth century. title: From vulnerability to resilience: Understanding social responses to climate-induced hazards in peri-urban and natural resources-dependent communities – The case of Tanga City in Tanzania
abstract: Over the past two decades, climate change (CC) has been and continues to be considered among the greatest challenges of our time. Its escalating risks are increasingly evident and more intense, particularly in natural resources-dependent and rapidly growing communities of sub-Saharan Africa. This study examined the interplay of climate-induced hazards, social vulnerability, and adaptation strategies used among communities in peri-urban areas of Tanga City in Tanzania. title: Development of a unique multiagency fish tracking collaborative in California
abstract: Abstract In California’s Central Valley, a unique science collaborative built around a shared telemetry network has been developed to track and understand the factors affecting the survival and movement of anadromous species such as salmonids and sturgeons throughout their migration to and from the ocean. The Interagency Telemetry Advisory Group (ITAG) gathers scientists from state and federal natural resource management agencies, universities, and consulting companies that work collaboratively to maintain this science program. title: Spatial Analysis of Groundwater Quality and Its Suitability for Drinking Purpose in SARGODHA City
abstract: Groundwater is the principal source of drinking water for Sargodha Tehsil, Punjab, Pakistan, but its quality is increasingly influenced by urbanization, agricultural activities, and changing land-use practices. This study aimed to provide a comprehensive spatial assessment of groundwater quality, evaluate its suitability for drinking, and identify areas vulnerable to potential health risks. abstract: Abstract A unique aquaculture practice for masu salmon ( Oncorhynchus masou masou ) has been developed in Miyazaki Prefecture, Japan, in which fish are transferred from seawater (SW) to freshwater (FW) following the SW culture period to extend the shipment season through summer. abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of an ethnopedagogy-based pop-up book on the beginning reading skills of second-grade students at SDN Padike III. This research was motivated by students’ low beginning reading skills and the limited use of contextual learning media. Previous studies have shown that pop-up books have been widely used to support students’ interest, learning outcomes, and reading skills; however, few studies have specifically integrated local culture into beginning reading instruction. title: Bibliometric Analysis of CRM Practices and Their Descendants: Impact on Business Outcomes and Strategic Development
abstract: The current research The current research performs a bibliometric analysis of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) practices and their offspring, looking at their contributions to business performance and strategic formation. Based on data obtained from the Scopus database, it provides an extensive view of the scholarly environment, identifying primary trends, popular studies, and upcoming themes in CRM. title: Impact chain driven data management for multi-risk analysis at urban scale
abstract: Urban areas are increasingly exposed to complex multi-hazard dynamics, where interacting events amplify risk across interconnected physical and socio-economic systems. Despite advances in risk assessment, existing approaches often remain hazard-specific, data-intensive, or limited in their ability to integrate diverse vulnerability dimensions. This study addresses these limitations by proposing a data-driven, interoperable multi-risk framework based on the impact chain approach. abstract: Drylands are highly vulnerable to salt accumulation, particularly near shrinking inland water bodies where strong evaporation, shallow groundwater, and terrain interact. To quantify this process, 39 surface samples (0–20 cm) were collected from a 94.18 km² belt surrounding Chaiwopu Lake, and nine indicators—ESP, pH, slope, aspect, distance to the lake, groundwater-level decline, Simpson’s diversity index, vegetation coverage, and elevation—were integrated into a composite index. title: Hydraulicity in Organic Polymers Enabled by Hydrophobization Upon Water‐Triggered Curing of Hydrophilic Chains
abstract: Water-curing capability of cementitious materials, commonly known as hydraulicity, is key to their widespread use through simply mixing powder with water to form desired robust structures. However, hydraulicity has been difficult to achieve for organic materials due to the lack of a strategy for wet curing while ensuring water resistance after curing. Here, we report unprecedented hydraulicity in an organic polymer enabled by an unusual water-induced polarity inversion, in which the reaction of a hydrophilic polymer with water induces hydrophobization via sol-gel reaction of silatrane. title: Do Himalayan-style mountains lie under the Antarctic ice: Implication for the Gondwana Supermountains, the rise of oxygen and the Cambrian explosion?
abstract: Analyses of detrital zircons from Antarctica show that its tectonics were dominated by Himalayan-style mountains, the roots of which now underlie the ice sheet. These mountains formed during the amalgamation of Gondwana and when the Antarctic data are added to the global river zircon database and appropriately weighted, it is apparent that the mountains, which formed by the amalgamation of Gondwana, were our planet’s dominant mountain-forming event. title: Enhanced production of phomapyrrolidone a through culture-condition optimization and morphological regulation in Didymella sp. FATR0054
abstract: Phomapyrrolidone A (Ppd A) is a hirsutellone-type macrocyclic alkaloid derived from marine fungi, exhibiting significant activity against triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, its low fermentation yield has limited further drug development. This study established a systematic optimization strategy integrating medium optimization, mycelial morphology regulation, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to enhance Ppd A production by the marine-derived filamentous fungus Didymella sp. title: Regional Typology of Maritime Business Profiles Using Subsector Presence and Regional MSME Scale in West Nusa Tenggara
abstract: Background: Small-scale maritime enterprises are central to blue-economy development, but fragmented sectoral statistics limit comparable regional profiling and do not support direct inference of business concentration. Objective: This study aims to develop a regional typology of maritime business profiles in West Nusa Tenggara using recorded subsector presence and the general regional MSME scale context. abstract: Sediment samples were collected and analysed for microplastic concentrations and identification in the Almendares River, both upstream and at the river mouth, and in Havana Harbour. Microplastic particles (45 μm to 5 mm) isolated by density separation were identified using microFourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (μFT-IR), and found concentrations ranging from 24 to 9989 items kg −1 d.w. title: Improving preschool children’s understanding of water pollution through experiential learning
abstract: Water pollution is a major environmental challenge with important implications for sustainability, public health, and environmental education. This study explored how an experiential learning program was associated with preschool children’s understanding of water pollution in a developmentally appropriate way. The study was conducted over a two-week period in a public kindergarten in Greece and involved 18 children aged 4 to 6 years. The intervention was integrated into the regular curriculum and engaged children in observation, experimentation, guided discussion, artistic expression, and inte

title: Household Survey and Geospatial Analysis of Urban Land Use Changes in Uyo Capital City, Akwa Ibom State
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive assessment of urban expansion in Uyo Capital City from 1986 to 2024, utilizing remote sensing, GIS, and socio-economic analysis. The findings reveal substantial land use/land cover transformations, particularly the decline in forest cover and agricultural land, and a significant increase in built-up areas. NDVI analysis confirmed a notable reduction in vegetation due to infrastructural development. title: Spatio-Temporal Dynamics and Variability of Rainfall in North-Western Rajasthan, India (1991–2024)
abstract: In this research, the spatial and temporal distribution of annual rainfall in North-Western Rajasthan is studied between 1991 and 2024 based on the Climate Hazards InfraRed Precipitation with Station (CHIRPS) v2.0 rainfall data and GIS technology. Annual rainfall data was analyzed through QGIS and Microsoft Excel was used for tabulating and plotting of statistical graphics. Spatial distribution of rainfall maps of years 1991 and 2024, rainfall change map, and temporal graph of rainfall were created. title: Multivariate analysis of land use/land cover (LULC) effects on water quality in the Lower Mara River catchment
abstract: ABSTRACT The Lower Mara River catchment is increasingly subjected to anthropogenic pressure due to land-use/land-cover (LULC) changes, which significantly influence river water quality. This study assessed the effects of LULC on water quality in the Lower Mara River catchment. Water samples were collected from 12 sampling stations during February, August, and December 2025 and analysed for nine physicochemical and biological parameters. title: Distribution and preservation of Kimberella quadrata from the Ediacara Member, South Australia
abstract: The fossil Kimberella quadrata is one of the most morphologically complex members of the soft-bodied Ediacara Biota. Kimberella and its trace fossil, Kimberichnus teruzzii, are largely known from the White Sea region of Russia, where Kimberella occurs abundantly. Kimberella occurs rarely in the Flinders Ranges area of South Australia, previously identified almost exclusively from float material. title: Interactions Between Micro- and Nano plastics and Engineered Nanoparticles in Wastewater and Receiving Environments: Implications for Treatment Performance, Transport Pathways, and Ecotoxicity
abstract: Microplastics (MPs), nanoplastics (NPs), and engineered nanoparticles (ENPs) are increasingly recognized as interconnected contaminants in wastewater treatment systems and receiving environments. This review examines their occurrence, interactions, treatment performance, transport pathways, persistence, and ecotoxicological implications, with emphasis on evidence from primary studies. title: Travel Motivations and Destination Attributes in Online Tourist Reviews: A Qualitative Study of Cittaslow Demre, Antalya
abstract: This study examines how visitors describe their travel motivations, destination experiences, and practical concerns in online reviews of Demre, Antalya. The researchers organized 210 unique TripAdvisor reviews, posted between 1 January 2021 and 1 July 2026 across five attraction groups, in a structured analytical matrix; stated visits range from 2020 to 2026. Demre’s Cittaslow status is treated as a contemporary destination-management context rather than as an explanation for reviews that largely pre-date certification.
