title: Synergistic configurations of livelihood capital drive pastoralist well-being: evidence from Tibetan Plateau, China
abstract: Grassland governance has shifted from a primary focus on ecological restoration toward greater attention to pastoralists’ well-being. Against this background, subjective well-being (SWB) has become a core indicator for assessing livelihood outcomes in pastoral regions. Using survey data from 163 pastoral households in Sunan Yugur Autonomous County on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau, this study applies fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to identify multiple pathways through which livelihood capital configurations generate high SWB. title: New Orleans and the Illegal Transatlantic Slave Trade, 1857–1861
abstract: This study explores the role of New Orleans in the illegal transatlantic slave trade between 1857 and 1861. It argues that the city’s growing involvement in this trade was connected to broader debates and attempts to reopen the transatlantic slave trade in Louisiana, which had been prohibited since 1808. title: Framework for retrofitting municipal wastewater treatment plants for enhanced resilience under failures and inflow variability
abstract: Resilience of wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) is critical for mitigating human impacts on aquatic ecosystems and enhancing environmental sustainability. However, WWTPs are typically designed on the basis of economic considerations, often neglecting system response to failures and disturbances. This work presents a systematic methodology for retrofitting WWTPs that explicitly accounts for both uncertainty in wastewater inflow and expected and unexpected events that may result in equipment failures. abstract: The assessment of heavy metals in plant species is crucial for understanding environmental health and potential risks to human health. This study focuses on the determination of heavy metals specifically lead, chromium, nickel, and manganese in the leaves of five selected plant species: Boswellia odorata, Thaumatococcus daniellii, Anogeissus leiocarpus, Erythrina senegalensis, and Cochlospermum tinctorium. title: The PAXT connection is a modifier of rare codon-enriched protein expression
abstract: Abstract Synonymous codons occur at unequal rates in the coding genome, with those represented least often termed ‘rare.’ Rare codon-enriched genes typically exhibit poor expression due to reduced transcription, mRNA stability, export, and translation. However, there are an increasing number of examples whereby rare codon-enriched genes are paradoxically highly expressed, suggestive of mechanisms to overcome the poor expression imposed by rare codons. title: From Energy Poverty to off-grid Smart Energy: Measured Household Air Quality and Willingness to Pay in Skardu, Gilgit-Baltistan
abstract: Gilgit-Baltistan lies at the periphery of Pakistan's electricity network, and in Skardu the consequences are acute. The town sits at 2,228 m, receives no piped natural gas, and endures a heating season of four to five months in which night temperatures fall between −10 and −20 °C. More than 80% of households therefore burn wood, dung cakes, crop residue, kerosene, coal, or plastic waste for warmth and cooking. abstract: This study evaluated the effects of different pretreatment methods on the phytochemical composition and amino acid profile of “Nyama Asabo” (Diplazium esculentum) to determine the most effective processing method for preserving its nutritional quality in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. Fresh leaves of D. esculentum (300 g each) were subjected to oven drying at 60°C, steam blanching at 70°C for 2 minutes, hot water blanching at 70°C for 2 minutes and hot water blanching with 2.5% sodium bicarbonate at 70°C for 2 minutes, while fresh leaves served as the control. title: Modernized cosmogony: enduring hierarchies and the co-optation of public administration reform in Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates the persistent barriers to democratic accountability within Indonesian public administration by elucidating the evolving cultural logic termed modernized cosmogony. Drawing on historical institutionalism and critical realism-informed research, the research reveals how inherited sacred hierarchies, rooted in pre-colonial cosmologies, have dynamically adapted to withstand colonial, authoritarian, and democratic reforms. title: Audit Quality and Financial Reporting Quality of Listed Insurance Companies in Nigeria
abstract: The integrity of audit opinions regarding financial reports has been a matter of concern since the Enron accounting scandal in 2001 and the subsequent financial crisis that affected numerous organizations, despite the issuance of clean audit opinions by auditors over the years. Consequently, this study investigated the effects of audit quality on the financial reporting quality of listed insurance companies in Nigeria from 2014 to 2023. title: Airborne microplastic exposure and urinary oxidative damage biomarkers in populations living in traffic-congested areas
abstract: Airborne microplastics (MP) have emerged as a growing environmental and human health concern globally. This study aimed to investigate associations between exposure to traffic-related airborne MP and oxidative damage among residents living in different traffic-congested areas in Bangkok, Thailand. Ambient and personal air samples were collected from low-, medium-, and high-traffic areas. abstract: Vietnam completed its national satellite positioning network, VNGEONET, at the end of 2019, and in September 2024 moved the service from free trial access to a priced public utility. Both steps were justified on productivity grounds, yet no published study has quantified how much surveying productivity the network can plausibly deliver, or under what conditions the new access charges leave users better off. title: Effects of Helleborus thibetanus extract, a novel plant-derived molluscicide on Oncomelania hupensis, the intermediate host of Schistosoma japonicum
abstract: The snail, Oncomelania hupensis, is the only intermediate host of Schistosoma japonicum. Thus, snail control is one of the most rapid and effective strategies for disrupting schistosomiasis transmission. In this study, 125 botanical extracts were screened for molluscicidal activity, leading to the selection of the extract of Helleborus thibetanus (EHT) for further evaluation. abstract: Abstract Air pollution remains a major environmental and public-health concern, especially in urban and peri-urban regions where emissions, land use, and seasonal meteorology interact. Although GI is often proposed as a strategy to improve air quality, its effects are highly context-dependent and difficult to isolate. This study examined the association between vegetation greenness, represented by NDVI, and monthly concentrations of particulate matter (PM 10 and PM 2.5 ), and NO 2 in the MRC and MRP, São Paulo State, Brazil, from 2019 to 2025. abstract: An important question in evolutionary biology is how polyploidization generates raw material for phenotypic diversification. abstract: European Ash (Fraxinus excelsior) is a keystone tree species, whose populations are being decimated by ash dieback disease (ADB) - better characterisation of genetic variants associated with low susceptibility to the disease is needed. Here, we develop a F. excelsior pangenome to more fully capture sequence variability within this species compared with a linear reference genome, using a geographically diverse set of fifty F. excelsior samples. title: Ecotoxicity of bauxite residue leachates during amendment-assisted revegetation: Multi-organ oxidative and genotoxic effects and gut microbiota shifts in zebrafish
abstract: Vegetation restoration is increasingly applied to mitigate environmental risks from bauxite residue disposal areas; however, how amendment-assisted revegetation alters leachate chemistry and affects aquatic organisms remains unclear. In this study, separate groups of adult zebrafish (Danio rerio) were exposed for 96 h to leachates collected after 30, 90, and 150 days of restoration. abstract: Introduction and Objective.Rainwater harvesting systems (RWHS) are an important element of sustainable water management in urbanized areas, by supporting retention and adaptation to climate change.The widespread use of RWHS, however, is limited due to concerns about the microbiological purity of the water.The aim of the review is to illustrate the current state of knowledge regarding microbiological hazards and methods of their assessment in the rainwater of RWHS. title: Intelligent analysis and interpretation of coffee production of Koraput district of Eastern India
abstract: Coffee has become an important cash crop for tribal farmers in the highlands of Koraput district in Odisha, Eastern India. Its production, however, varies widely from year to year, which makes planning and support difficult for district agencies. This study analyses twenty years of block-level coffee records (ten administrative blocks, 2006 to 2025) from Koraput district and asks a practical question: can the productivity type of a block in a given year be discovered without labels, and can that type then be used to predict whether the block will record a high-production year? abstract: Formwork work is a critical component in reinforced concrete construction because it affects structural quality, execution duration, and overall project cost. Rumex abyssinicus is an important plant species used in Ethiopian traditional medicine, and this study aims to conduct a phytochemical analysis of root extracts of R. abyssinicus and determine its antimicrobial activity. abstract: The ownership of commercial airports is increasingly essential for national competitiveness and regional economic development. In Italy, historically, tight control by the state permitted the implementation of long-term development plans and ensured that the needs of local communities were addressed, but today, there are very few airports, and among the larger ones, almost none, without an equity share held by the private sector. abstract: Radium-226 (226Ra) is mobilized following the disturbance of ore bodies containing uranium-238. abstract: Spatially confined biofilms generate distinct extracellular microenvironments that may shape host immune responses, yet their effects on macrophage function remain poorly defined. abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines the cultural and intellectual history of the Chinese “slave girl” in Progressive Era California. abstract: The use of nitrogen (N) fertilizer in maize production is constrained by scarcity, low use efficiency, and high costs. abstract: The reuse of treated wastewater (TWW) in agriculture represents a promising strategy to alleviate freshwater scarcity, although the occurrence of pharmaceuticals (PhACs) raises concerns regarding their fate and potential transfer within the soil–plant system. abstract: Abstract Rapid land-use change and climate change increase the need for quantitative, region-wide assessments of current status across many plant species. abstract: Executive function develops rapidly in early childhood and predicts later success in life, yet its neurobiological correlates during this period are not yet well characterised. abstract: Data visualisation is often used to communicate insights and influence behaviour, particularly in relation to socio-ecological challenges. abstract: Deep foundation is one of the structural components where ensuring pile integrity is essential to achieve the required strength. Then, the soil mixed with marble dust was cured for 7 days before the testing. abstract: Abstract Biological soil crusts – photosynthetic communities of cyanobacteria, lichens, and/or mosses living on soil surfaces – represent about 12% of the global land surface, yet their role in climate mitigation remains uncertain. Here we address this knowledge gap by integrating multiscale remote sensing techniques within a unique long-term climate manipulation experiment. abstract: Paracetamol is a widely used analgesic and antipyretic agent; however, its use is limited by minimal anti-inflammatory activity and the risk of hepatotoxicity from prolonged oral use or in acute overdose. To address these limitations, four novel phosphorylated paracetamol analogs (2a-2d) were synthesized via a UV-radical methodology and evaluated through integrated in silico, in vitro, and in vivo for anti-inflammatory dermal approaches. abstract: The study was conducted to determine the food safety knowledge, attitude and practices of road-side vendors of ready to eat grilled catfish in Awka metropolis, Anambra state, Nigeria. Cross-sectional survey was adopted in selecting a sample of vendors. This sample was derived from 20 entities randomly selected from four predetermined towns that were considered to have high concentration of these operators. abstract: This study designs, develops, and evaluates the performance of a low-power, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) based, IP68 protection-rated, multi-station smart irrigation control unit for agricultural irrigation applications. The system is built on an STM32F103 microcontroller-based electronic control board and can manage 6 independent irrigation stations. title: Belowground microbial stewardship underpins sustainable agroecosystem management
abstract: Below every cultivated field lies a civilization of unimaginable complexity. A single gram of productive agricultural soil harbors upwards of a billion bacterial cells, several kilometers of fungal hyphae, and a faunal community spanning nematodes, protozoa, mites and collembolans, all bound together in trophic relationships that have been taking shape for hundreds of millions of years. abstract: Abstract This study evaluates for the first time the sustainability of photocatalytic hydrogen production in China utilizing a 26-faced polyhedron SrTiO3/Rh/Co/Cr photocatalyst. Life cycle assessment and costing are used to estimate the impacts and levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH). These are compared via multicriteria decision analysis with alternative solar-driven hydrogen technologies (water electrolysis, photoelectrochemical, and thermochemical), as well as with conventional methods (steam methane reforming and coal gasification). title: Allanblackia and Soybean Bakery Fat Impact on Baking Performance of Bread
abstract: Physicochemical features of Allanblackia and Soybean bakery fat and the impact of on baking performance of bread in terms of loaf volume, weight, height and oven spring was investigated. Outcome was compared with the commercial equivalent. title: Duckweed (Wolffia globosa, Wolffia arrhiza, and Lemna minor) as novel therapeutic food for acute malnutrition and famine alleviation in low- and middle-income countries and humanitarian crisis settings
abstract: Acute malnutrition remains a leading cause of under-five mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly in humanitarian crisis settings where conventional therapeutic food supply chains are frequently disrupted. There is an urgent need for locally cultivable, affordable, and nutritionally adequate alternatives to imported ready-to-use therapeutic foods (RUTFs). abstract: Dietary fucoidan, a sulfated polysaccharide derived from brown seaweed, has attracted increasing interest for its potential to influence gut microbial and metabolic responses. abstract: Safe drinking water remains essential for public health, particularly in developing regions where sachet water is widely consumed. This study assessed the physicochemical properties, bacteriological quality, antibiotic resistance, heavy metal contamination, and potential health risks of 8) selected sachet water samples. title: Environmental drivers of body size plasticity and their consequences for reproductive fitness in Anopheles coluzzii
abstract: Malaria is a life-threatening infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites and transmitted to humans primarily through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. Sub-Saharan Africa bears the greatest global burden of malaria, with members of the Anopheles gambiae complex, including Anopheles coluzzii, serving as important malaria vectors in the region. abstract: This study aims to explore the regulatory mechanism of Semiliquidambar cathayensis extract on the immune stress induced by Aeromonas hydrophila in Misgurnus anguillicaudatus . Through transcriptomics and 16S rRNA sequencing techniques, the changes in gene expression profiles of M. anguillicaudatus muscle tissues and the structure of the intestinal microbiota were analyzed separately. abstract: Indonesia's Islamic Religious Colleges (Perguruan Tinggi Keagamaan Islam, PTKI) have institutionalised Sufism and Psychotherapy as formal academic disciplines. title: LN-PMUT ultrasonic transducer enables instantaneous blood pressure reduction via renal hilar implantation
abstract: Blood pressure (BP) is a fundamental vital sign, yet no implantable device for BP modulation is currently available. Here, we present a miniaturized ultrasound probe based on lead-free lithium niobate (LN) piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) technology. The device features a dual-electrode design offering enhanced emission sensitivity and acoustic output, while maintaining a compact size (3×3 mm 2 , 3 mg), wide bandwidth (∼32%), and 2.5 MHz resonant frequency. abstract: Tuning protein expression in non-model organisms is often constrained by the lack of validated genetic parts and predictive design tools. Translational tuning through the modulation of upstream untranslated regions (5'-UTRs) offers a potentially organism-agnostic route, but existing methods typically rely on mechanistic assumptions, prior knowledge that may not be available in non-model contexts, or the screening of sequence libraries. abstract: While most previous studies on Hermetia illucens larvae in poultry nutrition have focused mainly on productive performance and the replacement of conventional protein sources, limited information is available on the dose-dependent effects of whole dried larvae on metabolic and blood indices in laying hens. The objective of this research was to examine the effects of graded dietary levels of dried Hermetia illucens larvae (DHIL; 5%, 10%, and 15%) in White Leghorn laying hens on liver enzymes, kidney parameters, lipid profile, and hematological indices. abstract: Soil salinisation has become a global environmental problem, seriously threatening the stability and sustainable development of regional ecosystems. As a key tree species for the ecological restoration of saline‒alkali lands, investigating the root-associated microorganisms of Elaeagnus angustifolia L. provides an important approach to addressing this challenge. abstract: Abstract The aim of the study is to clarify the association between heavy metal exposure and drug-induced liver injury (DILI) in patients with drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB), and to provide new epidemiological evidence for the prevention and treatment of DILI. In this study we utilized a 1:2 matched nested case–control study design based on a follow-up cohort of DR-TB patients at Hunan Provincial Chest Hospital from September 2021 to November 2024. abstract: ABSTRACT The Mesostoinae are a poorly understood braconid subfamily with unresolved morphological challenges and a complex taxonomic history. This study provides insight into the biodiversity of this subfamily on Kangaroo Island (KI), South Australia. Specimens were curated from existing collection material for DNA extraction and sequencing of the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I gene. abstract: AI literacy has been theorised as a developmental, transdisciplinary capability. In contrast to this, Australian regulation appears to govern generative AI principally through academic integrity and award value, and its differential impact across student cohorts is largely still under-examined. We combine a survey of 462 students at an Australian university with its academic-integrity case records for 2022–2026. abstract: Abstract Low-level ethanol blending in gasoline may reduce petroleum dependence in humid-tropical economies, but deployment requires evidence on fuel handling, storage stability, material compatibility, emissions, and feedstock supply. abstract: Community-managed seasonal tank irrigation systems in South Asia's dry zones face increasing climate-induced production risks, yet systematic prioritisation of climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practices through integrated stakeholder frameworks remains limited. abstract: Despite substantial investment in technical safeguards, employees continue to fall for phishing emails at high rates, and the cognitive decision-making processes that drive this susceptibility remain comparatively understudied relative to technical countermeasures. The present research addresses this gap by applying the tripartite model of dual-process theory and prospect theory to examine cognitive responses to phishing and legitimate emails. abstract: Objective: To critically examine the scientific structure, thematic evolution, and emerging monitoring and mitigation strategies of microbial biodeterioration in diesel, biodiesel, and diesel–biodiesel storage systems. This retrospective study investigated the epidemiology and molecular characteristics of RSV in Taiwan from 2018 to 2024 using data from the National Community Virus Surveillance System, which encompassed the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic period. abstract: Abstract Eggplant holds a significant place in the human diet due to its nutritional value. Given its extensive cultivation across various regions of Iran and the widespread use of pesticides, monitoring these residues is essential for safeguarding public health. Accordingly, this study was conducted to identify and assess pesticide risks in eggplant and surrounding soil. abstract: This study aims to compensate for the absence of a system for ranking university libraries. abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. abstract: Vegetable retanning modifies the surface, mass-retention and initial color-difference characteristics of wet-blue leather, but dosage selection is still commonly based on practical experience rather than quantitative process descriptors. abstract: This study compares characteristics and implications for sustainable resource management of supergene and primary mineral deposits. Supergene deposits, formed through weathering and oxidation near the Earth’s surface, represent a significant source of critical and industrial metals. abstract: This policy brief synthesizes scientific evidence on the ecology, structure, and natural dynamics of North-European (boreal and hemiboreal) old-growth forests (OGF), and provides clear, operational, science-based recommendations for implementing the European Commission’s OGF indicators in this region. abstract: Background Withania somnifera , commonly known as ashwagandha, is a widely used herbal remedy with reported anxiolytic and adaptogenic properties. Despite its growing use globally and regionally, comprehensive public understanding of its pharmacological benefits, safety, and potential risks remains limited within the Saudi Arabian context. abstract: Bambara groundnut ( Vigna subterranea ) is a resilient indigenous African legume with potential for improving food and nutrition security in semi-arid environments. abstract: In recent years, edible coatings and films have emerged as sustainable postharvest technologies to preserve the quality and freshness of fruits and vegetables and extend their shelf life, thereby reducing the use of conventional plastic packaging. title: Positive ion mass spectrometry enables simplified radiocarbon analysis
abstract: Abstract Radiocarbon ( 14 C) analysis underpins research and regulation across archaeology, Earth system science, the life sciences, and bio-content verification, yet remains constrained by reliance on accelerator mass spectrometry (AMS). Although AMS delivers the sensitivity required to measure natural 14 C abundances, it is built around a single technological paradigm — negative-ion source coupled to high-energy acceleration — that limits automation, throughput, and integration with mainstream analytical workflows. title: Color patterns as a model for connecting developmental mechanisms to phenotypic evolution
abstract: Vertebrate color patterns are experimentally accessible and ecologically relevant traits, making them excellent models for studying how diversity arises during development and evolution. Advances in developmental biology, pattern quantification, and broad phylogenetic sampling now offer an opportunity to investigate how pattern development and evolution influence each other. To facilitate this crosstalk, we propose a conceptual framework connecting pattern development with its diversification through two key developmental principles: self-organization and instruction. title: Harmonic impact of LPG-to-electric cooking substitution on Indian low-voltage networks and a hybrid GWO–DE tuned active-filter mitigation
abstract: A constraint on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) supply through the Strait of Hormuz, the corridor through which the majority of India’s imported LPG is routed, would induce a substitution of LPG-based domestic cooking by electric alternatives. The present study evaluates the low-voltage (LV) distribution-side power-quality consequences of such a substitution through a scenario-based simulation study. title: Diversity and Unity in the European Union
abstract: Two diversities are operative in the EU: the traditional diversity between member states, and the more recent minority-related diversity whose proper site is within member states. This article traces the EU-level evolution of minority-related diversity, whose legal-political focus expanded from old (national) to new (immigrant) minorities. It looks at “interculturalism” and “diversity” as normative follow-ups to a notionally discarded “multiculturalism,” reviewing their manifestations in the EU. And it addresses two seemingly contradictory campaigns recently launched by the European Commission

title: An integrated framework for evaluating nano-enabled agro-inputs: linking environmental fate, exposure and field translation for sustainable crop protection
abstract: Nano-enabled agro-inputs (NEAs) include intrinsically active nanomaterials and nanoscale systems that deliver pesticidal molecules, nucleic acids, biological control agents, nutrients, plant signals or defence elicitors. Their evaluation remains fragmented because studies use inconsistent dose metrics, delivery routes, biological endpoints and reporting standards, which limits comparison and obscures environmental and agronomic relevance. title: Bitlis Front and Mustafa Kemal Pasha's Commandership of 16th Army Corps during the First World War
abstract: Following the defeat at Sarıkamış on the Eastern Front during the First World War, the front was virtually left to its fate. The fall of Erzurum to Russian forces on 18 February 1916, and the subsequent expansion of operations toward Iraq and the Mediterranean, finally alerted the Ministry of War to the seriousness of the situation. It was decided to reinforce the 3rd Army with units of the newly formed 2nd Army in Thrace.Among the divisions dispatched was the 5th Infantry Division, a unit distinguished in the Gallipoli campaign. title: Hypouricemic effect and mechanism of chitooligosaccharide‐ionic water in hyperuricemic mice
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Hyperuricemia is a prevalent metabolic disorder associated with excessive uric acid (UA) accumulation, oxidative stress, renal dysfunction and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Chitooligosaccharide (COS) possesses antioxidant and microbiota‐regulating properties; however, the potential of mineral ion‐enriched COS formulations against hyperuricemia remains unclear. title: Climate Change–Associated Modulation of Phytochemical Composition and Antimicrobial Potential in Medicinal Plants of the East African Region: A Review of Evidence
abstract: Medicinal plants remain important components of healthcare systems in East Africa, where indigenous knowledge has supported their use for generations. Their therapeutic value is largely associated with secondary metabolites whose biosynthesis and accumulation are influenced by environmental conditions. Climate change may therefore affect medicinal plants not only shifts in productivity but also through alterations in the quantity and composition of bioactive constituents. title: Transfer learning-based fault diagnosis of wind turbine high-speed shaft bearings using CWRU pretraining and public run-to-failure data
abstract: Fault diagnosis of wind turbine high-speed shaft bearings (HSSBs) is hindered by the distribution gap between laboratory data and field signals, and by the lack of labeled run-to-failure recordings. This study proposes a three-stage transfer learning framework to address both problems. Stage 1 pretrains a lightweight convolutional backbone with a frequency-domain attention module (FAM) on the CWRU bearing dataset. title: Biochar mitigates dimethylarsenate-stimulated methane emissions mediated by DOM-microbe interactions in paddy soils
abstract: Introduction Paddy soils represent key biogeochemical interfaces linking arsenic (As) transformation and carbon (C) cycling. Dimethylarsenate (DMAs), a widespread organoarsenic contaminant in rice paddies, can alter methane (CH 4 ) dynamics, but the underlying mechanisms based on dissolved organic matter (DOM)-microbe interaction and the mitigation potential of biochar still remained insufficiently understood. title: The R plasmid pRAS2 in the fish pathogen Aeromonas salmonicida is a global mediator of antibiotic resistance in aquaculture and can be used by pRAS3 for mobilization
abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) mediated by conjugative plasmids is a major driver of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dissemination in aquatic environments. In Aeromonas salmonicida , plasmid-mediated HGT is largely driven by the pRAS plasmid family. Here we present genomic and experimental characterization of pRAS2 from A. salmonicida strain 1682/92 and demonstrate its role in helper-dependent mobilization of the co-resident pRAS3. title: Prevalence of chronic respiratory disease symptoms and associated occupational risk factors among certified silicosis patients of Rajasthan
abstract: Background Silicosis is an irreversible, fibrotic occupational lung disease caused by the chronic inhalation of respirable crystalline silica dust, and persists as a significant source of morbidity among sandstone quarry workers in Rajasthan, India. Despite the prevalence of silicosis, there has been no comprehensive assessment of the symptom load and occupational risk factors of Chronic Respiratory Symptoms among certified silicosis patients in the Balesar sandstone area. title: What is this sophistication thing anyway?
abstract: Abstract Following Dewar (2019), ‘reduction’ and ‘sophistication’ are supposed to be two different ways of articulating the shared content of symmetry-related models of physical theories. And yet: there does not exist in the literature a maximally clear, maximally general statement as to what the distinction between reduction and sophistication amounts to. title: De novo assembly and characterization of the complete chloroplast genome of Amorphophallus myosuroides Hett. & A. Galloway 2006
abstract: The genus Amorphophallus exhibits high species diversity but poorly resolved phylogeny due to phenotypic plasticity and convergence. Amorphophallus myosuroides, with unique silvery leaf markings, lacked complete plastome data, leaving its phylogenetic placement uncertain. We sequenced and assembled its first chloroplast genome using PacBio HiFi sequencing. The circular genome is 171,894 bp in length contains 128 genes, including the trans-splicing gene rps12. title: Individual periovulatory ovarian responses associated with pregnancy outcome following an Ovsynch protocol in Peranakan Ongole cows
abstract: Introduction Although ovulation synchronization protocols effectively control the timing of ovulation, pregnancy success remains highly variable among individual cows. The periovulatory ovarian responses associated with subsequent pregnancy outcome following synchronization remain poorly characterized in Bos indicus beef cattle. Therefore, this exploratory longitudinal study characterized individual ovarian sonographic and hormonal responses during an Ovsynch synchronization protocol and evaluated associations with pregnancy outcome in Peranakan Ongole cows. title: The urinary and vaginal microbiota in postmenopausal women with and without overactive bladder
abstract: Overactive bladder (OAB) is a common condition, particularly prevalent in women after menopause. Previous studies suggest that OAB is related to an altered urinary microbiota, indicating a potential microbial etiological component. However, establishing a solid association between the microbiota and OAB has been obscured by use of heterogenous study populations with broad variations in age and menopausal status, both factors known to influence the composition of the urinary and vaginal microbiota. title: A Multiplatform Chemical Perspective on Coffee Identity: Interplay Between Origin, Cultivar, and Fermentation Time
abstract: Abstract Green coffee bean chemistry is shaped by the geographic origin, plant genetics, and post-harvest processing, but their relative contributions across complementary chemical layers, within a single, tightly controlled context, remain comparatively underexplored. We applied a multiplatform strategy utilizing ICP-based multielement profiling, UHPLC-HRMS/MS polyphenolic analysis, 1 H NMR metabolomics to investigate the contributions of farm, cultivar, and fermentation time of green coffee. title: Chronic Methanol Exposure as a Potential Environmental Trigger of Behçet’s Disease: A Hypothesis
abstract: Behçet’s disease (BD) is a chronic, relapsing multisystem inflammatory disorder with a distinctive geographic distribution along the ancient Silk Road. Although genetic susceptibility—particularly HLA-B*51—is well established, genetic factors alone cannot explain the marked regional clustering or migration effects observed in BD. In this hypothesis-driven review, we propose that chronic low-level methanol exposure represents a plausible and previously underrecognized environmental contributor to BD pathogenesis. journal: International Journal of Medical and Biomedical Studies

title: Polystyrene microplastics exposure impairs skeletal muscle development by disrupting the gut-muscle axis in Hu sheep
abstract: Microplastic pollution is an increasing concern in livestock production. Skeletal muscle development is fundamental to animal growth and meat production, but whether microplastic exposure impairs skeletal muscle in ruminants and whether intestinal injury contributes to this process remain poorly understood. Hu sheep were orally exposed to 50-μm polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs; 75 mg/animal/day) for 8 weeks. title: Simulating the host niche: balancing complexity and control in the experimental evolution of antibiotic resistance and pathoadaptation
abstract: The 'ESKAPE' pathogens cause the majority of antibiotic-resistant infections in humans, with associated mortality expected to surpass that of cancer by 2050. Outbreak strains of these pathogens often demonstrate a remarkable ability to establish infection and easily acquire novel antimicrobial resistance mechanisms. Because the expression of virulence factors and antimicrobial resistance genes often imposes a fitness cost, successful host-adapted strains must evolve without compromising their ability to colonize the niches found in the human body. title: Water-regulated processing window of soil–cement–epoxy hybrid binders for cohesive soil interface applications
abstract: This study investigates a water-regulated soil–cement–epoxy hybrid binder developed for cohesive silty clay interface applications. The work aims to identify a preliminary processing window that provides adequate workability, dimensional stability, and soil-contact continuity under moisture-sensitive conditions relevant to bored-pile construction. A laboratory-based iterative mixture-screening approach was conducted using fixed proportions of soil, cement, and epoxy while varying water dosage and epoxy resin-to-hardener ratio. title: Natural radionuclide occurrence and ingestion dose in foodstuffs from a Uranium Province, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Radiological assessment of dietary intake is a key component of environmental surveillance in areas characterized by enhanced natural radioactivity. In this context, the Lagoa Real Uranium Province, a strategic mineral region in Bahia, Brazil, presents a complex geogenic setting that demands a detailed understanding of radionuclide occurrence in foodstuffs. title: Analysis of Strategies to Improve the Financial Feasibility of the Rantauprapat–Kisaran Toll Road Section
abstract: The Rantauprapat–Kisaran Toll Road is a strategic part of the Trans-Sumatra corridor that supports connectivity and regional economic development in North Sumatra, Indonesia. However, the baseline financial analysis indicates that the project is not financially feasible, with a Financial Internal Rate of Return (FIRR) of 8.351%, a negative Net Present Value (NPV) of IDR 3,971 billion, and a Payback Period (PP) of 15.95 years. abstract: Objectif : Evaluer la qualité de l'eau de boisson et les pratiques domestiques de conservation dans l'aire de Santé Musumba afin d'identifier les risques de contamination de la source à la consommation. Méthodologie : Une étude quantitative, descriptive transversale prospective a été menée de février à juillet 2026 auprès de 384 ménages sélectionnés par échantillonnage aléatoire systématique. title: Next-generation nanomedicine: Bridging tumor biology with individualized drug delivery
abstract: Introduction: Nanomedicine has made a significant impact in the field of oncology, with many nanosized systems reaching the market and clinical trials. These novel drug delivery systems often respond to biological triggers and temporarily target tissues, enhancing the therapeutic index of chemotherapeutics. Despite these advances, including stimuli-responsive and targeting ligand-decorated nanosystems, the therapeutic results have not yet fulfilled expectations. title: Pushing the Boundaries: Studies on Consumers and Food Demand in the Journal of Agricultural Economics
abstract: ABSTRACT We summarize the development of consumer economics and food demand in the Journal of Agricultural Economics over the past 100 years. Even from an early stage, the role of marketing agricultural products in a thriving agricultural sector was recognized within the works published in the Journal. Early papers focused on the demand for specific commodities and consumer trends more generally. title: Role of ZnO and TiO2 nanomaterials in the removal of toxic trace elements from contaminated water: A review
abstract: Persistent Organic Pollutants (POP) and trace elements are important contaminants in global water quality management because of their toxicity, non-biodegradability, and bioaccumulation potential. Contaminants are not easily removed, especially when present at low concentrations and in complex natural water situations, where traditional treatment operations may be less effective. title: A probabilistic framework for modeling chloride‐induced corrosion and related load‐deformation behaviour of reinforced concrete
abstract: Abstract Chloride‐exposed reinforced‐concrete structures often suffer localized corrosion, so corrosion initiation time and average steel loss are poor indicators of structural performance. This paper presents a spatially resolved, proof‐of‐concept framework that couples diffusion‐based chloride ingress and initiation with a localized morphology model and maps the resulting deterioration field to structural damage descriptors for non‐linear finite element analysis. title: Time and Free Trade Agreements: Implications for the AfCFTA
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how free trade agreements (FTAs) can boost economic growth by increasing trade, with clear implications for the African Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA). Our main finding is that in general, the effects of FTAs are delayed by at least 3 years on average for intra‐African trade. The results make the case for timely implementation of the agreement's tariff policies, as well as the investment plans to reduce barriers to trade and logistics. abstract: Abstract We present new results from ambient noise tomography and azimuthal anisotropy analysis of the DOMERAPI data set to investigate crustal structure beneath the Merapi‐Merbabu‐Telomoyo region in central Java. The 3D shear‐wave velocity (Vs) model reveals a prominent high‐Vs anomaly extending from south of Merapi through Merbabu to Telomoyo, aligned with the Merapi‐Merbabu Fault. title: The Limits of Incumbent Blame Games in Times of Crisis: Experimental Evidence from Electoral Autocracy
abstract: Abstract This study investigates how blame-attributing crisis frames influence support for incumbents in an electoral authoritarian context, focusing on Türkiye. It asks how, to what extent, and under what conditions incumbents’ blame frames shape public attitudes toward the government. The study examines four crisis types (i.e., global warming , earthquake , economic collapse , and pandemic ) and compares the effects of religious , conspiratorial , and scientific framing across these contexts. title: Comprehensive analysis method of key risk factors in the subway operation accident by complex network and accident data
abstract: With the continuous expansion of subway systems in China, the operational systems of subway have become increasingly complex, leading to a rise in risk factors. In the event of an accident, these risks can significantly impact the safety and health of individuals, and pose a direct threat to the reliability, social stability, and economic sustainability of subway systems. title: IS Aba1‐ mediated crp‐osmC amplification enhances host‐associated fitness in Acinetobacter baumannii
abstract: Abstract Acinetobacter baumannii is a pathogen, highly adaptable to both hospital‐ and host‐associated environments. Understanding the genetic mechanisms underlying its adaptability is critical for controlling its persistence. Our study identified the crp‐osmC gene cluster, flanked by IS Aba1 elements, as a significant genetic structure undergoing amplification in A. baumannii . title: Peptide‐Enabled Nanoplatforms for Malaria and Leishmaniasis: From Intracellular Targeting to Translational Diagnostic Perspectives
abstract: Malaria and leishmaniasis continue to impose a substantial health burden, while current therapeutic and diagnostic strategies remain limited by toxicity, prolonged regimens, drug resistance, and restricted field applicability. This review examines recent advances in peptide-enabled nanoplatforms for both diseases, with emphasis on intracellular targeting, drug delivery, and diagnostic innovation. abstract: This study employed ultrasound-assisted enzymatic extraction combined with response surface optimization to determine the optimal extraction parameters, achieving a polysaccharide yield of 21.73 %. Kinetic analysis based on Fick's second law revealed that the GP extraction procedure is a non-spontaneous, endothermic reaction and elucidated its mass transfer kinetics. GP is a furan-type polysaccharide formed by D-glucose units linked via α-glycosidic bonds. abstract: Background The neonatal mycobiome remains an underexplored component of early-life microbial ecology. Although fungi may contribute to immune maturation and host–microbe interactions, fungal DNA profiles across maternal and neonatal body sites are poorly characterized. This exploratory pilot study aimed to characterize fungal DNA profiles across multiple maternal and neonatal biological compartments during early life. title: Nurses’ knowledge, attitudes, practices, and educational needs regarding frailty: a multicenter cross-sectional survey in southwestern China
abstract: Background Population aging has made frailty a major public health concern. Frailty is potentially reversible when identified and managed early, and nurses are well positioned to deliver such care; however, nurses’ frailty-related competencies vary considerably, and evidence remains scarce in southwestern China, where the aging burden is disproportionately high. We therefore conducted a multicenter study to assess nurses’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding frailty, explore their associated factors, and clarify their educational needs. title: Lineage-resolved lifetime modelling reveals potential quiescence and synchronization among MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells
abstract: This study presents evidence of a previously unrecognised structured organisation of untreated cancer cell lineages and suggests an unexpected sensitivity to subtle experimental perturbations that is not readily explained by standard population models. These conclusions are based on exploratory analyses of cell-tracking data from untreated MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells cultured under standard conditions. title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and kidney disease: Genetic associations and computational prioritization of candidate toxicogenomic pathways
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental pollutants with bioaccumulation potential, but their associations with kidney diseases remain incompletely understood. This study integrated Mendelian randomization and computational toxicology to examine associations between genetically predicted circulating PFAS levels and kidney disease outcomes and to prioritize candidate toxicogenomic pathway themes. title: Molybdenum as a context-dependent lever for crop nitrogen use efficiency: a review
abstract: Molybdenum (Mo), an essential cofactor for nitrate reductase and nitrogenase, has demonstrated variable crop responses across soil conditions, crop species, application methods, and environmental stress factors. We conducted a Scopus-based scoping review and evidence mapping of studies published from 2015 to 2025 that evaluated Mo effects on NUE-related agronomic, physiological, biochemical, and symbiotic outcomes. abstract: Reference evapotranspiration (ETO) is a fundamental component of irrigation scheduling, estimation of crop water requirements, and sustainable water-resource management, particularly in semi-arid regions where water resources are limited. This study evaluated the performance of four empirical ETO estimation methods (Blaney–Criddle, Hargreaves, Radiation, and Modified Penman) against the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith method in the Ziway area of the Central Rift Valley, Ethiopia. abstract: This study, based on fieldwork conducted as part of the “Kızıldağ National Park Long-Term Development Revision Plan” and an evaluation of previous literature studies, presents the flora and floristic characteristics of Kızıldağ National Park. Therefore, continuous monitoring potentially provides critical insights about the impact of extreme condition exposure on the fitness to fly of military pilots. abstract: Vascular graft transplantation is an important strategy for treating advanced cardiovascular diseases, restoring blood flow, and replacing diseased vessels. However, currently used autologous and synthetic vascular grafts still face several limitations, including limited availability of autologous vessels, thrombosis, intimal hyperplasia, infection, insufficient endothelialization, mechanical mismatch, and unsatisfactory long-term patency of small-diameter vascular grafts, which restrict their further clinical application. title: A comprehensive review of sewage sludge valorization for resource recovery and sustainable agriculture use
abstract: Abstract The swift intensification of urbanization and industrialization has resulted in the generation of over 53 million tonnes (dry solids) of sewage sludge/year globally, posing major environmental and management challenges. Sewage sludge (SS), a solid or semi-solid output from sewage treatment plants, may mostly be utilized in agriculture as organic fertilizer and enhancing nutrient turnover and soil organic matter through reuse. title: Research advances in red ginseng polysaccharides: preparation, structural characteristics and immunomodulatory effect
abstract: Red ginseng is a processed product of ginseng through steaming. Its polysaccharides differ in structure and biological activity from those of ginseng. Red ginseng polysaccharides are mostly acidic polysaccharides and have various biological activities. It is worth noting that its immunomodulatory effect has become an important area of research. abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Air pollution remains a global public health and climate challenge, causing millions of premature deaths annually and disproportionately affecting marginalised communities. abstract: Abstract Reliable prediction of groundwater recharge from rainfall is crucial to water management but is scientifically challenging. Previous studies have demonstrated that caves, mines, and tunnels provide useful “windows” for observing rainfall recharge timing and thresholds (i.e., amount of rainfall in a given time period causing a change in dripping from the void ceiling). abstract: Background The growing global environmental concerns and market demands have intensified the search for alternatives to petroleum-based packaging. As health and ecological impacts move to the center of attention, natural fibers derived from plant, animal, and mineral sources have emerged as viable substitutes, owing to their biodegradability, renewability, and minimal environmental footprint. abstract: The biofilms of Mycobacterium Tuberculosis (Mtb) use extracellular DNA (eDNA) as a protective structural scaffold that shields resident bacteria from host immunity and antibiotics, promoting persistent infection. abstract: Introduction Continuous flooding in paddy ( Oryza sativa L.) cultivation challenges sustainable agriculture and food security amid climate change. abstract: Abstract Candida albicans biofilms represent a clinical challenge due to their protective extracellular matrix and the resistance to conventional antifungals. abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of global mortality and disability, exhibiting marked sexual dimorphism in incidence, severity, and functional outcomes. abstract: Abstract Medicinal flora represents an essential source of bioactive substances for both conventional and contemporary medicine; nevertheless, excessive extraction of non-renewable parts such as roots, bark, and heartwood has led to significant reductions in wild populations, especially among endemic and slow-growing species. abstract: Thunbergia laurifolia Lindl. (TL), commonly known as the blue trumpet vine or rang jued in Thai, is traditionally used in Thai medicine as an herbal tea for the treatment of poisoning. abstract: Since October 7, 2023, protests related to the Israel-Hamas conflict have occurred at colleges and universities across the United States. abstract: Introduction Eleutherococcus senticosus (Rupr. & Maxim.) Maxim. is an important medicinal shrub with increasing demand for its wild resources. abstract: Wutou decoction (WTD) is a traditional remedy in Chinese medicine for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). However, its active ingredients are complex, and how it counteracts RA is still not clear. abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a major microvascular complication of diabetes, with renal lipid deposition being a key pathogenic driver. abstract: The prevalence of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is rising, with adverse maternal–fetal outcomes. title: Turbulent gravitational wakes

Specifically, we show that a localized boundary deformation acting on a boosted black brane generates a wake whose boundary dynamics exhibit the formation of coherent vortical structures that are advected downstream by the background flow. title: Investigation of magnetic-field effects on photomultiplier tubes for the first Large-Sized Telescope of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory
abstract: Photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) are widely used in imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes. Their response can depend on the telescope pointing direction through changes in their orientation relative to the geomagnetic field. Such a dependence was indicated during the calibration campaign of the CTAO LST-1. In this work, the LST-1 calibration data are analyzed to quantify the gain dependence in terms of the geomagnetic field, and dedicated laboratory measurements are performed to test the hypothesis that the observed dependence originates from magnetic-field effects. title: Mind the Gap: How SBOM Specification Ambiguities Lead to Divergent Software Bills of Materials. An Empirical Tool Study
abstract: Software Bill of Materials (SBOMs) will become mandatory starting in December 2027 under the European Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) [8]. Although previous studies have highlighted significant differences among SBOM generators, the reasons for these discrepancies remain unknown, as does whether they stem from implementation errors or deliberate design choices. In this paper, we evaluate three widely used SBOM generators across more than 3,000 JavaScript and Rust projects, using a groundtruth baseline derived from dependency lockfiles. title: A Critical Assessment of Nigeria’s Legal and Institutional Framework for Ocean and Coastal Governance
abstract: Nigeria possessed extensive maritime endowments, including an 850-kilometre coastline and an Exclusive Economic Zone of over 200 nautical miles, holding an untapped blue economy potential estimated at 296 billion USD. However, the sustainable exploitation of these marine and coastal resources was severely hindered by a fragmented, multicephalous, and reactive legal and institutional framework. title: ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE THROUGH INDIGENOUS OCEAN GOVERNANCE AND CUSTOMARY MARINE TENURE
abstract: Environmental justice has become one of the defining principles of modern international environmental law, traditionally focusing on the equitable distribution of environmental benefits and burdens, public participation in environmental decision-making, and protection against environmental discrimination. Although these objectives remain fundamental, they are no longer sufficient to address contemporary environmental challenges, including climate change, marine biodiversity loss, ocean warming, sea-level rise, marine pollution, and the increasing exploitation of marine resources, all of which

title: Diagnostic assessment of Marine Protected Area performance using the Social-Ecological System framework in coastal Bangladesh
abstract: Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) are important instruments to safeguard biodiversity and human well-being. In Bangladesh, previous MPA-related studies have focused on MPA zoning, Hilsa sanctuary, fisheries co-management, or community livelihood issues. Only limited empirical research has examined MPAs by integrating governance, actor-level, livelihood, and environmental dimensions within a single diagnostic framework, leaving a clear gap in MPA assessment in Bangladesh. title: Sea Surface Roughness Trends Estimation using Power Waveforms of BeiDou MEO Satellite Reflected Signals
abstract: The sea surface is a crucial climate regulator and the boundary where air and water interact. It fuels global weather systems and tempers climate change by absorbing heat and carbon dioxide, while its microscopic marine life generates a major portion of Earth's breathable oxygen. Sea surface roughness monitoring is essential for assessing ocean conditions and improving sea-state and marine weather forecasting. title: Climate Pressure and Labor Vulnerability in Colombian Caribbean Coastal Cities: Open-Data Evidence from Barranquilla, Cartagena, Santa Marta, and Riohacha
abstract: This study examines the association between coastal climate pressure and labor market vulnerability in four Colombian Caribbean cities: Barranquilla, Cartagena, Santa Marta, and Riohacha. Using open-access secondary sources from DANE, IDEAM, UNGRD, INVEMAR, and DNP, the study constructs a 48-observation city-quarter analytical panel and estimates city and period fixed-effects models, distributed-lag specifications, and an event study design. title: Physical-layer security of underwater wireless optical communication systems under non-line-of-sight eavesdropping
abstract: Abstract This work investigates physical-layer security of underwater wireless optical communication (UWOC) systems under covert non-line-of-sight (NLOS) eavesdropping caused by scattered photons. A first-order single-scattering model is developed for the near-transmitter NLOS eavesdropping link by incorporating seawater absorption, scattering, beam divergence, receiver field of view, and Eve’s geometry. title: Model-Free Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control Integrated with Linear Extended State Observer for Ocean Ship Course Control Based on Ultra-Local Model
abstract: In maritime navigation, precise and stable ship course control is critical for operational efficiency and maritime safety, yet it is severely challenged by unpredictable marine disturbances (e.g., waves, wind, and currents) that consist of slowly varying and stochastic components. Traditional control methods, though effective under specific operating conditions, exhibit limited adaptability to the nonlinear, time-varying characteristics of marine systems and inherent dependence on accurate ship mathematical models, which easily leads to suboptimal performance and elevated navigation risks, esp
journal: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

title: The first GBIF dataset on the distribution of fish assemblage in inland and transitional waters of Sicily (Central Mediterranean Basin)
abstract: Mediterranean inland and transitional waters are fragile ecosystems currently facing rapid biodiversity loss due to anthropogenic pressures and climate change. In Sicily, the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea, knowledge of ichthyofaunal assemblages of these ecosystems has remained fragmented, sporadic, and largely confined to "grey" literature for long. The present paper presents a dataset built with the aim to fill this gap. The dataset aggregates 808 occurrence records from 108 water bodies and localities, spanning a 50-year period (1976–2025). Data were recovered from diverse sources,

title: Biodiversity of the abyssal and hadal zone in the Nova Canton Trough (Central Pacific Ocean; 2751–7989 m): a visual inventory
abstract: Comprehensive biodiversity inventories of abyssal and hadal ecosystems remain rare due to the financial and logistical challenges associated with operating in the deepest parts of the ocean. However, deep-sea exploration programmes are increasingly generating extensive video datasets offering new opportunities to document biodiversity across broad depth ranges. The process was performed with different rotational speeds (1000, 1100 and 1200 rpm) and transverse speeds (40, 50 and 60 mm/min). title: Between Print and Public in Indian Ocean Africa: The Diasporic Publics of the Zanzibar Protectorate
abstract: Abstract This article discerns commonalities and distinctions between Zanzibar’s printed publics and other publics that emerged around the Indian Ocean between the 1860s and 1930s. Problematizing the concept of public, it traces the development of discrete publics in Arabic, Indian languages, and to a lesser degree Swahili as the diasporic triumphed over the local. title: High school science fair: Characterizing student communication and presentation practices and their association with SEF outcomes
abstract: Obtaining, Evaluating, and Communicating Information is one of the eight Science and Engineering Practices in the National Research Council framework that underlies Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS). Scientific inquiry requires evaluation and communication of research findings. These skills are part of scientific inquiry itself. The goal of this study was to characterize the communication practices students used during Science and Engineering Fairs (SEFs). title: Determinants of CSA Adoption in Coastal Bangladesh: An Application of Structural Path Analysis
abstract: Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) is widely promoted to reconcile productivity, resilience, and emissions goals among smallholder farmers, yet adoption of capital-intensive CSA technologies remains low and uneven in climate-vulnerable coastal agriculture. This study examines socio-demographic, institutional, and behavioral determinants of CSA adoption among farming households in selected coastal districts of Bangladesh. abstract: Introduction: The conservation of Indonesia's coastal environment is highly dependent on the role of customary law communities that uphold local wisdom. Purposes of the Research: This study aims to analyze the implementation and role of the customary law community of Negeri Haya in preserving the coastal environment through the practice of Sasi in response to the mining activities of Waragonda Minerals Pratama Ltd. title: Employee fairness perceptions through social dialogue and proactive communication: evidence from Moroccan organisations
abstract: Employees’ fairness perceptions have become increasingly important in contemporary human resource management (HRM) because they are closely associated with employee well-being, workplace relationships and organisational effectiveness. Although organisational justice has received considerable attention as a framework for understanding employees’ fairness perceptions, limited evidence explains how participatory, communicative and regulatory organisational mechanisms are jointly associated with these perceptions, particularly in emerging organisational contexts. title: CWAS: A Dense Passive-Source Seismic Survey to Image Northwestern Australia
abstract: Abstract Northwestern Australia preserves a complex record of Precambrian craton formation and passive-margin evolution, yet its lithospheric structure remains poorly constrained because of thick sedimentary cover and sparse seismic observations. To address this gap, the China–Western Australia Seismic Survey was conducted between 2017 and 2019 by the Institute of Geology and Geophysics, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Macquarie University, and the Geological Survey of Western Australia. title: Upscale Hotel Markets in Vietnam’s Coastal Tourism Cities: Supply, Demand and the Risk of Overbuilding
abstract: Vietnam’s coastal destinations absorbed the largest share of hotel investment during the country’s post-pandemic tourism recovery, and by the third quarter of 2025 they held roughly 60 per cent of a national midscale-to-luxury stock of more than 192,000 rooms. This paper asks whether the upscale room supply now under construction in those destinations can be absorbed by plausible demand growth, and it develops a transparent method for answering that question when only published aggregates are available. title: The paradoxes of adaptation to climate change in Central Asia
abstract: Central Asia is widely recognized as a global ‘hotbed’ of climate change (CC), yet effective adaptation is hindered by systemic contradictions. Despite the region's high vulnerability to CC it remains a significant scientific "blind spot" in global research on its impacts. title: Common Heritage of Mankind: The Evolution of the Concept and Its Significance in Contemporary International Law
abstract: The study examines the concept of the common heritage of mankind (CHM) and its role in contemporary international law. The historical context of the development of this concept is analyzed, its development since the mid-20th century and the reasons for its support by developing countries advocating for a new international economic order are traced. abstract: Abstract Sophia de Mello Breyner Andresen is among the most celebrated of Portuguese poets, yet the eight literary fairy tales gathered in English as The Girl from the Sea and Other Stories (2020), first published separately in Portuguese from 1958 onwards, have rarely been read for their form. This essay reads the collection, together with the separately published Saga , as Kunstmärchen, fairy tales composed by a named author who deliberately reworks an inherited tradition. title: The Impact of Montara Compensation on Business Sustainability and The Potential for Increased Profitability Amongst Small-Scale Fishermen in Rote Ndao
abstract: This study aims to analyse the extent to which the Montara compensation has impacted the business sustainability and increased profitability of small-scale fishermen in Rote Ndao Regency. Previous research on oil spills has generally focused on direct economic losses and the fairness of compensation but has not examined how compensation translates into business sustainability and long-term profitability. title: Emerging research for the effective co-management of small-scale fisheries
abstract: Small-scale fisheries account for 40% of global fish catch, employ 90% of the world's fishers, and play a pivotal role in food security, poverty reduction, and sustainable resource utilisation for a substantial portion of humanity. Fisheries co-management is now widely considered to be the most appropriate, fair, and effective form of governance for small-scale fisheries. While fisheries co-management will continue to grow, its implementation does not guarantee positive impacts for food security, nutrition, livelihoods, or biodiversity. title: Invisible Pollution, Inadequate Law: Rethinking Civil Liability for Non-Persistent Oil Spills in International Maritime Law
abstract: Non-persistent oil spills, involving substances such as gasoline, kerosene, and jet fuel, pose acute yet under-recognized threats to marine ecosystems due to their rapid dissipation and toxic effects. Despite existing international liability frameworks—principally the International Maritime Organization’s (IMO) Civil Liability Convention (CLC) 1969 and the International Oil Pollution Compensation (IOPC) Fund Conventions—the treatment of non-persistent oil remains legally and ecologically inadequate. title: Data-driven Bayesian analysis of port-call bottlenecks and turnaround time at the ship–shore interface in crude oil tanker operations
abstract: Ship consumption during port periods, main and auxiliary engine usage, cargo handling operations, and waiting times contribute significantly to ship-related emissions. Despite increasing regulatory pressure regarding carbon emissions, the assessment of ships' energy efficiency and performance during port calls remains limited. The study aims to identify the main bottlenecks and drivers of turnaround time at the ship–shore interface as a proxy indicator with implications for ship energy efficiency by examining the entire process from ship arrival until the commencement of the sea passage. abstract: Large unmanned cargo airships may support heavy-lift logistics in regions without runway infrastructure, but payload release produces a rapid buoyancy surplus and changes the vehicle mass properties. This study develops a simulation framework coupling six-degree-of-freedom variable-property flight dynamics, an active seawater ballast system, and constrained ballast-flow allocation. title: Product environmental footprint assessment of cultivated sugar kelp: A step toward Product Environmental Footprint category rules for cultivated seaweed
abstract: Harmonised environmental assessment is essential for integrating algae and seaweed products into EU sustainability policies, including the Green Deal and the forthcoming Green Claims framework. Yet, no Product Environmental Footprint Category Rules (PEFCR) currently exist for cultivated macroalgae, creating a major methodological gap for a fast-growing biomass sector. title: SAFERCOAT project: Sustainable coatings for a safer, circular future
abstract: SAFERCOAT project: Sustainable coatings for a safer, circular future The Horizon Europe project is developing sustainable coating solutions for demanding applications, such as maritime, aeronautical, and cultural heritage protection. COATINGS are everywhere in modern life. They protect ships from corrosion caused by chlorides in seawater, shield aircraft components from extreme conditions, and help preserve cultural heritage objects for future generations. title: Blue Cities, Green Laws: Legal Models for Urban Climate Resilience in the Global South
abstract: Blue cities are cities that plan themselves around water rather than against it: rainwater is stored, recycled and reused, streets and parks are given permeable surfaces, wetlands and lakes are protected and restored, and coastal settlements are defended by mangrove belts and flood-resistant construction. Rivers, lakes, drainage, drinking water supply, sewage and storm water are treated as one interconnected system, and nature-based solutions such as rain gardens, bioswales and urban forests are preferred to concrete drains that push water downstream. title: Dissemination of Sustainable Whiteleg Shrimp Farming Practices for GEDSI Groups in Dadap Village, Sambelia, East Lombok
abstract: GEDSI groups in coastal areas still face limited access to information, training, technology, and decision-making in productive economic activities, including whiteleg shrimp farming. This community service activity aimed to improve the knowledge and understanding of GEDSI groups in Dadap Village, Sambelia District, East Lombok Regency, regarding sustainable, inclusive, and environmentally friendly whiteleg shrimp farming practices. title: Integrating Biobanking Into Conservation Practice: The Development and Impact of the EAZA Biobank
abstract: Zoological biobanks are becoming essential tools in conservation, offering a means to preserve genetic material and support in situ population management amid accelerating biodiversity loss. With rapid advances in genomics, cryopreservation, and assisted reproduction technologies, biobanks enable a proactive approach to providing insurance against genetic erosion and facilitating future research, supplementation, and genetic rescue. title: Call for Survey Responses: Understanding Dataset Publication Trends in Aquatic Sciences
abstract: As journals increasingly mandate public data deposition, researchers in the aquatic sciences depend on information about best practices for data sharing. Datasets are now required or expected by many journals. Specifically, upon the acceptance of an article, authors are now often expected to have the data corresponding to the article uploaded as a dataset with its own digital object identifier (DOI) in a publicly accessible data repository. title: Improving landcover data governance in developing countries
abstract: Recent advances in open-access satellite imagery and processing tools have accelerated the production of national-scale landcover (LC) maps for land use planning and ecological monitoring. While such technological democratisation has expanded analytical capacity, it has also generated a new governance challenge: the coexistence of multiple, independently produced LC datasets without institutional coordination or custodianship. abstract: Against the backdrop of the in-depth advancement of the Silk Road Economic Belt initiative, environmental protection in the overseas investment of Chinese enterprises has increasingly attracted the attention of the international community. From the perspective of international environmental law governance, this paper systematically examines the basic principles that should be established for the environmental legal system of the Silk Road Economic Belt. title: Regulatory capture in Italian port authorities: the case of terminal concessions in Genoa and Trieste
abstract: Ports are central to global trade, with 80–90% of traded goods transported by sea. Since the 1990s, liberalization has brought increasing convergence in port governance, with port authorities assuming the role of independent agencies responsible for managing port space through public tenders. Despite their importance, port authorities have received little attention from the perspective of regulatory politics. This exploratory study addresses that gap by focusing on the Italian case. title: Sources and environmental impacts of Kura River pollution under anthropogenic pressures in Azerbaijan
abstract: The Kura River is Azerbaijan’s principal river system and supports drinking-water supply, irrigation, hydropower, fisheries and riverine ecosystems. At the same time, its transboundary character and intensive human use make it vulnerable to multiple forms of pollution. This study examines the principal anthropogenic sources of Kura River pollution and their environmental implications by integrating two independently prepared research dossiers with a targeted review of scientific and institutional literature. title: Measurement in the Ultimatum and Dictator Games: Construct validity, standardization and the problem of coordination
abstract: The ultimatum game (UG) and the dictator game (DG) are two of the most prominent tools in experimental and behavioural social sciences. Originally designed to study bargaining behaviour and decision-making in economics, these simple yet versatile scripts have come to be viewed by many as reliable instruments for measuring prosocial preferences, such as altruism, generosity, or sensitivity to social norms. abstract: Background and objective. Griffonia simplicifolia is a woody vine found in the secondary forests of West and Central Africa. Its seeds are an important source of 5-hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP), a precursor of serotonin, and contain an oil rich in linoleic acid. Traditional knowledge and uses of this oil remain poorly documented. This study aims to document the ethnobotanical knowledge relating to the species in Togo, with a particular focus on the seed oil. abstract: Global warming is no longer merely an environmental or atmospheric phenomenon; it is an increasingly profound anthropological challenge affecting human health, livelihoods, migration, settlement, food systems, cultural practices, social institutions and relations between humans and the environment. abstract: Introduction: India is undergoing a significant digital health transformation, propelled by initiatives like the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM). title: Evaluating the Livelihood Impact of Tourism Revenue Sharing Funded Projects in Communities Around Musanze District, Rwanda
abstract: Tourism Revenue Sharing (TRS) is a policy mechanism with a pivotal role to promote community development and conservation around protected areas in Rwanda. While the TRS programme has invested heavily in social infrastructure and community projects, there is a lack of empirical evidence on the impact of TRS on the livelihoods of households. title: Health-Seeking Behaviour of Buruli Ulcer Patients in Rural Areas with Water Bodies in Rivers State
abstract: Buruli ulcer (BU) remains a neglected tropical disease that disproportionately affects populations living in rural communities with frequent exposure to aquatic environments. Despite its debilitating physical, social, and economic consequences, evidence on the health-seeking behaviour of affected individuals remains limited in many endemic areas of Nigeria. Most of our business and management literature continues to rely on traditional, anthropocentric, leadership and strategy theories as a route to change without considering the embedded, systemic, heterogeneous, and future-orientated nature of the problem. title: Recentering Resource‐Based Livelihoods: Prosperity Beyond Extractivism and Pastoralism
abstract: This research note, informed by qualitative fieldwork with resource harvesters in Nova Scotia, explores the effect of economic change and ecological crisis, the outcomes of rural development strategies, and demographic shifts that have shaped the province's rural areas in recent years. It argues that our present moment is ripe with opportunities for a renewed sociological attention on livelihoods in this region, which should take as its focus the relationship that people, communities, and government have with their physical environment. title: Look-up tables for complex refractive index correction of particle sizes measured by common research-grade optical particle counters
abstract: Optical particle counters (OPCs) are widely used to measure the aerosol particle number size distribution over a large size range encompassing sub- and super-micron diameters. The measurement principle of OPCs is based on the dependence of light scattering on particle size. However, this dependence is not monotonic at all sizes as light scattering also depends on the particle composition (i.e., the complex refractive index, m ) and morphology. title: Estimating Rice Transplanting Dates and Projected Shifts under Climate Change in Japan with the Use of Sentinel‐1 Imagery and CMIP6 Scenarios
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the impact of climate change on rice transplanting timings in Japan, focusing on Hyogo and Niigata Prefectures. Using time‐series Sentinel‐1 SAR imagery, we identified transplanting dates based on the sharp decrease in backscatter coefficients during the ponding period. The estimation was validated against survey data from agricultural corporations and cooperatives, yielding a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 9.8 days for Hyogo and 6.2 days for Niigata. title: An Exploratory Accounting Approach for Balancing Environmental Impacts of Point and Diffuse Sources in Nitrogen Trading
abstract: Nutrient trading between point and diffuse sources of nutrients offers an integrated watershed nutrient management approach to achieve nutrient reduction goals that benefit both the terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. This market-based approach requires quantification of the environmental impacts of nutrients derived from different sources. This environmental impact depends on the forms, concentrations, loads, transport, and processing of nutrients within waterways. title: Ratio of different bacterial genera in oral biofilm in polar researchers during an Antarctic summer-season expedition 2026 to James Ross Island
abstract: Short- and long-term stays in Antarctica may induce microbiome changes in oral cavity. In our study, pre- and post-Antarctic expedition oral microbiome were analysed in the participants of Czech Antarctic expedition 2026. Saliva samples were taken from the expedition members before (Day 0, January 16th, 2026), during, and after (Day 62, March 20th, 2026) the Czech Antarctic Expedition to Mendel station, James Ross, Island.
