title: Behavioral Insights for Sustainable Living: Evaluating Household Waste Management Behavior for a Green Economy in Bali
abstract: The rapid growth of tourism and urban activities has significantly increased household waste generation in Bali, while existing waste management systems face persistent capacity and behavioral challenges. Although socio-economic determinants of waste behavior have been widely examined, empirical studies that explicitly link household sustainability perceptions to community-based waste management mechanisms, including TPS3R, remain limited. This study aims to fill this gap by analyzing how environmental, health, and economic perceptions influence households’ assessment of the importance of TPS3

title: Enlightening the Anthropocene: reconsidering anthropocentrism for environmental education
abstract: Abstract This paper argues that the Anthropocene must be understood not primarily as a geological epoch but as an epistemic and ethical condition in which human action becomes inseparably entangled with natural and technological processes. In this hybrid world of “third nature,” the most urgent challenge is a pervasive misrecognition of humanity’s own role in shaping planetary systems. title: Oil Pollution and Environmental Challenges in the Niger Delta Region of Nigeria: The Way Forward
abstract: Over the years the Niger Delta (ND) region of Nigeria has been known for environmental pollution. This pollution has been attributed to the activities of Multi-National Oil Companies (MNOCs) operating in the region, the activities of these organisations cause contamination of the soil surface and ground water, atmospheric air (gas flaring), increased deforestation as well as the economic loss. The inability of the government to curb these problems have led to conflict between communities in ND and many of MNOCs. title: Reflections on Creative Responses to Archival Collections in PARADISEC
abstract: The Pacific and Regional Archive for Digital Sources in Endangered Cultures (PARADISEC) is a digital archive of some of the many small cultures and languages of the world, particularly from the Pacific region. The article reflects on a collaborative outreach project involving the creative response of a group of Papua New Guinean people to archival collections held in PARADISEC. The project demonstrates how reciprocity, long-term relationships and the valuing of Indigenous knowledge holders can invigorate cultural practices, adding value and meaning to the archive. title: Serve yourself: a digital engagement framework for automatic text recognition
abstract: With digital scanners for heritage material becoming increasingly accessible, libraries require guidance to locally implement such technologies. Clear assessments as to technical affordances, potential disruptions and overheads are needed, especially if libraries are to harness such technologies for greater digital engagement. This paper focuses on scanners aligned to Automatic Text Recognition: the AI-enabled process of converting images-of-manuscripts into machine-readable text. title: Congenital and Rheumatic Heart Disease in the South Pacific: An Urgent Need for a Regional Cardiac Surgery Center
abstract: The island nations of the South Pacific are home to more than 3 million Polynesians and Melanesians. There is a high birthrate and unique susceptibility to rheumatic fever which together have led to a large and increasing population of children and young adults with both congenital and rheumatic heart disease. Wide geographic dispersal has resulted in major challenges in both diagnosis and management of these patients. title: Place, identity, and adaptation: conceptual insights from elementary science education initiatives in rural Hawaiʻi, Maine, and Montana
abstract: Rural elementary science education presents a wide array of opportunities to provide connection between classroom learning and lived experiences. While existing curricula support teachers in connecting NGSS-aligned scientific sensemaking to the cultural, ecological, and political dimensions of the communities they serve, few frameworks integrate authentic rural educator perspectives and experiences. abstract: Object detection at the edge requires a difficult balance among detection accuracy, deterministic latency, memory bandwidth, and energy consumption. Existing binarized accelerators replace multipliers with XNOR and population-count logic, but many designs use a fixed binary datapath or select precision only at the layer level, limiting their ability to protect accuracy-sensitive channels while fully exploiting low-bit parallelism. title: Critical modelling of socioscientific issues: fostering critical scientific literacy in Latin America
abstract: Abstract This paper advances a research-informed framework for conceptualising modelling-based instruction as a means of fostering critical scientific literacies through socioscientific issues (SSI). Drawing on the SSI research movement and Vision III of scientific literacy, we conceptualise critical modelling as a situated, collective, and deliberative practice that integrates disciplinary reasoning with ethical, political, environmental, and cultural dimensions of knowledge. title: ICT development and maritime transport CO2 emissions: evidence from cross-country panel data
abstract: Maritime transport is a vital pillar of global trade, while its CO 2 emissions have become an increasingly pressing concern. ICT development may provide a new perspective for maritime decarbonization. Using cross-country panel data for 111 countries from 2019 to 2023, this study examines the impact of national ICT development on maritime transport CO 2 emissions and further investigates the nonlinear role of maritime transport scale. title: Mapping the Architecture of Community Involvement in Traditional Craft Village Tourism: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: The intersection of traditional craft villages and tourism has emerged as a critical domain for both rural revitalization and cultural heritage preservation. While tourism acts as an economic catalyst, unchecked development frequently leads to cultural commodification and the marginalization of local artisans. Consequently, community involvement is recognized as an essential structural mechanism for sustainable tourism. This study presents a systematic bibliometric analysis of 731 Scopus articles published between 2015 and 2025 to map the evolutionary trajectory of this academic domain. Using

title: Safeguarding Vietnamese Traditional Musical Instruments in the Digital Era: A Cultural Management Perspective
abstract: Safeguarding Vietnamese traditional musical instruments in the digital era requires management of more than physical objects or isolated digital files; the relevant unit is a living heritage ecosystem comprising instruments, sound, skills, knowledge, context, and communities of practice. Objective: This study examines how digital technologies can support the safeguarding of Vietnamese traditional musical instruments and develops a cultural management framework for linking digital resources with living heritage continuity. Methods: A structured narrative review was combined with policy analysis
journal: Journal of Social Science and Human Research Studies

title: Curating Ružake gila
abstract: Ružake gila is a trilingual digital exhibition in German, English and Lovari Romani dedicated to the life and songs of Ruža Nikolić-Lakatos (1945–2022), a prominent performer of Lovari Romani music in Austria. The exhibition is the result of a project at the Music and Minorities Research Center at the University of Music and Performing Arts Vienna (MDW). title: The Persistent Fragmentation of Gulf Foreign Aid: Bilateralism and the Limits of Regional Humanitarian Coordination
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines why Gulf foreign aid has remained predominantly bilateral and fragmented since its emergence in the 1960s, despite the establishment of regional institutions, recurring regional crises and repeated calls for greater coordination. Bilateralism has been a persistent and defining feature of Gulf aid, and no effective regional humanitarian coordination mechanism has emerged even as Gulf donors have expanded and professionalised their aid institutions. title: Indigenous led biodiversity litigation in the extractives context
abstract: Litigation focusing on advancing Indigenous Peoples’ rights, or provision of remedy where these rights have been impacted, often relies on a combination of legal frameworks and principles across international environmental law, international human rights law, biodiversity law and national indigenous rights law. This is apparent in the extractives context where Indigenous Peoples have sought to challenge the continued violations and a constant lack of recognition of their rights, whilst also simultaneously advancing the protection of biodiversity. abstract: Recent political assaults on natural resource management, scientific integrity, and historical memory by the United States’ current administration have exposed some of the brittle foundations of “America’s best idea” within place‑based conservation. Incremental fixes and a return to the status quo will not suffice to save our nation’s parks and protected areas (PPAs). title: Neurorights in the Age of Neurotechnology and Digital Health. Are New Rights Necessary to Protect the Mind?
abstract: The present paper is concerned with the ongoing debate on neurorights from the standpoint of legal philosophy. The fundamental question is whether these rights should be understood as a reinterpretation of existing fundamental rights or as a distinct emerging legal category. Methodologically, the paper combines conceptual analysis, comparative law and the study of international soft law instruments in order to assess the legal status and practical function of neurorights. title: Climate action and sustainable development: equity, justice and inclusion in developed vs. developing economies
abstract: Purpose This article introduces a special issue volume on climate action and sustainable development, with a central focus on equity, justice and inclusion (EJI). It examines how climate impacts and policy responses intersect with gender, labour and governance systems, applying an adaptation–maladaptation lens to identify challenges and opportunities for equitable and inclusive climate action. title: Clinical safety and tolerability of repeated high-fluence 405 nm blue light exposure in chronic wounds
abstract: ABSTRACT Antimicrobial blue light requires substantially higher fluences than conventional photobiomodulation to achieve antibacterial effects, but concerns regarding tissue toxicity have limited its clinical translation for chronic wounds. The objective of this phase I clinical trial was to evaluate whether repeated high-fluences antimicrobial blue light could be delivered safely to chronic wounds. title: The Paradox of Confidence: Competitive Mediation of Teaching Self-Efficacy in the Emotional Intelligence and Classroom Incivility Relationship
abstract: This study investigates the interrelationships among Emotional Intelligence (EI), Teaching Self-Efficacy (TSE) and Classroom Incivility Management (CIM) among university faculty members in Gujarat, India. The primary objective is to examine whether teaching self-efficacy functions as a competitive mediator in the EI-CIM relationship, potentially revealing a paradox where heightened self-efficacy may unexpectedly diminish incivility management effectiveness. title: Core microbiomes as a potential fingerprinting method of Western USA dust sources
abstract: Introduction Changing frequency and intensity of dust emissions impacts ecosystems and human health. Dust carries microbes, nutrients, heavy metals, and other materials that may change environmental biogeochemistry at deposition sites. Identifying dust sources provides key information on where and when mitigation strategies should be employed. However, commonly used geochemical or isotopic tracers are often not capable of distinguishing between geographic regions. title: From Traditional Practice to Professional Training: Vietnamese Instruments in Higher Education
abstract: Background : Higher education training in Vietnamese instruments must safeguard community-embedded performance knowledge while responding to new professional demands. Objective: This study identifies the tensions arising in the transition from traditional practice to professional training and proposes a curriculum framework for Vietnam. Methods: Qualitative document analysis was combined with an integrative review. title: Who Benefits from the Circular Economy? A Systematic Scoping Review of Social Economy Actors, Livelihoods, and Policy in the Global South
abstract: Abstract The circular economy (CE) has gained substantial policy traction, yet its social dimensions — particularly the roles, contributions, and vulnerabilities of social economy actors in the Global South—remain insufficiently mapped. This systematic scoping review examines how waste-pickers, cooperatives, social enterprises, and informal sector workers are positioned within CE transitions, adopting a multi-level analytical framework spanning micro-level livelihood outcomes, meso-level institutional and governance mechanisms, and macro-level CE system performance. title: Divergent fertility responses to cyclones and floods: a mixed-methods study from rural Bangladesh
abstract: Over the past decade, Bangladesh has experienced substantial demographic change alongside increasing climate-related disruption. This study examines the links between extreme climatic events and fertility among married Bangladeshi women of childbearing age who already have children, focusing on how cyclones and floods relate to fertility behaviour in cyclone- and flood-prone villages. A mixed-methods design was used, drawing on 544 household surveys, 74 in-depth interviews with women, 10 focus group discussions with men, and 8 key informant interviews. title: Coupled drought–land use dynamics and agricultural resilience in mainland Southeast Asia
abstract: Abstract Drought is initiated by climatic anomalies, but its development and consequences often unfold as a coupled socio-ecological process shaped by interactions among land use, water infrastructure, resource management, and governance. This coupling is particularly pronounced in Mainland Southeast Asia (MSEA), where strong monsoon dependence, rapid land-system transformation, expanding hydraulic infrastructure, and intensive water use influence how climatic water deficits propagate through hydrological, agricultural, and livelihood systems. title: A multi‐objective decision‐analysis framework for addressing human–wildlife conflicts
abstract: The costs and frequency of negative interactions between people and wildlife (that is, human–wildlife conflict or HWC) are increasing globally and hindering conservation efforts. Practitioners are challenged to manage wildlife populations and consider human health and livelihoods simultaneously. Principles and tools of conservation decision‐making can help relevant parties navigate the complexities, uncertainties, and difficult trade‐offs involved in managing HWC. journal: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment

title: Killing Nature to Save It: Conservation Science, Biotechnology, and Ethical Extermination
abstract: There is a deep tension within conservation: The field aims to protect the well-being of flora, fauna, and ecosystems, but often goes about doing this by mass-killing invasive animals. Into this picture comes biotechnology, a field of research that engages with modifying the fundamental building blocks of life. Biotech, and in particular suppression gene-drives, seem to promise win-win solutions that allow us to painlessly and gently remove invasive species from ecosystems. title: Mapping justice claims for solar geoengineering
abstract: Solar geoengineering is a set of controversial emerging technologies that seek to cool the planet by reflecting sunlight. These technologies may be able to reduce the worst impacts of climate change by lowering global temperatures temporarily. They also come with great risks, including as related to technological lock in and mitigation deterrence, among others. Balancing these potential risks and benefits demands a careful interrogation of justice and ethics. Unlike many scholars who assert a clear justice landscape, we argue here that the terrain is complicated, nuanced, and not fully mapped.

title: Reproductive hesitation in the Norwegian petrostate
abstract: This article responds to calls for critical engagement with the entangled politics of reproduction, population, and climate breakdown by exploring analytical avenues that refuse both the individualization of responsibility and the logics of population. Taking as our empirical point of departure Andy Lautrup’s ethnographic engagement with the eco-reproductive considerations of young climate activists fighting to end oil production in Stavanger, Norway, we ask what it means to hesitate about one’s reproductive future from a position of privilege and complicity within the Norwegian petrostate, an

abstract: This technical paper forms part of The Economic and Fiscal Implications of Alberta Separation, a broader analysis undertaken by the School of Public Policy. Its development reflects the contributions of a wide project team, including authors, reviewers, editors, research assistants and other research personnel, technical specialists, and the integration and production team. title: Research Trends in Eco-Friendly Construction Materials (2015–2025): A Bibliometric Review
abstract: This study presents a bibliometric review of research on “eco-friendly construction materials” and “green building materials” published between 2015 and 2025. abstract: The total emissions generated during the manufacturing, use, and disposal of aerospace materials and selected components were evaluated and compared using a cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment (LCA) of structural aircraft materials. Initially, the potential of lightweight composite materials to reduce aviation-related emissions was investigated by comparing plates made from Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy, carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP), and basalt fiber-reinforced polymer (BFRP). abstract: El artículo refleja los resultados de un estudio que tuvo como objetivo sistematizar la producción científica sobre estándares de representación documental, es decir, de normas de descripción, de modelos conceptuales y de esquemas de metadatos en el ámbito de las ciencias de la información entre 2013 y junio de 2024. title: Genome Microbiology at 20 Years: Who We Are and Where We Are Going
abstract: The International Symposium "Microbial Growth and Behavior: From Bench to Nature" was held as part of the annual meeting of the Society for Genome Microbiology, Japan. This session was designed to highlight challenges in modern microbiology: how to connect molecular insights obtained from laboratory model systems with the dynamic and complex responses of microbes in natural environments.

title: Corridor statecraft: connectivity without integration in the Horn of Africa
abstract: The Horn of Africa is frequently framed as an emerging frontier of infrastructure-led transformation, yet this narrative obscures a deeper structural contradiction: the expansion of transport corridors has not produced corresponding regional integration. This article advances the concept of Corridor Statecraft to explain how infrastructure in the Horn functions as a geopolitical instrument through which states and external actors organize selective connectivity, shape economic dependency, and reconfigure regional order. abstract: Kansalaistiede on lähestymistapa, joka tuo kansalaiset aktiivisina toimijoina osaksi tieteellistä tutkimusta. Kehittyvät kansalaistieteen menetelmät tarjoavat merkittäviä uusia mahdollisuuksia vaikuttavalle hyvinvoinnin tutkimukselle. title: Green synthesized Mn-Doped MgO multifunctional nanoparticles: from bioactive action to dye degradation
abstract: This study reports the green synthesis of Colocasia esculenta leaf extract-mediated manganese-doped magnesium oxide nanoparticles (Mn-doped MgO NPs) and evaluates their photocatalytic, antibacterial, cytotoxic, and reusability performance. The novelty of the work lies in the use of C. esculenta leaf extract as a natural stabilizing/reducing agent for preparing Mn-doped MgO NPs and in correlating Mn incorporation with structural, optical, and biological activities. title: TOURISM RESOURCES CONFLICTS IN PROTECTED AREAS: A CASE STUDY OF THE MAKULEKE CONTRACTUAL NATIONAL PARK
abstract: Protected areas increasingly depend on tourism to support biodiversity conservation and local development; however, conflicts over governance, resource access, and benefit-sharing continue to challenge sustainability outcomes. The Makuleke Contractual National Park (MCNP) in South Africa, established through a landmark land restitution agreement, provides a valuable context for examining the relationship between co-management and tourism-resource conflict. title: Planning Cultural Exchange Across Borders
abstract: Cross-border spatial development poses distinct challenges where differing planning cultures and paradigms meet at national borders, a reality that is particularly evident in the Greater Region. We present an innovative, intercultural planning game developed by the UniGR-CBS Spatial Planning Working Group, which serves as a science-policy interface with a dual purpose: it functions as a data collection methodology drawing on discourse analysis of stakeholder reasoning, and as a training format for spatial planners in cross-border contexts. title: Portable Web Applications: Feasibility, Limitations, and Applications of Flash Drive Deployment
abstract: Traditional enterprise web applications rely on centralized, cloud-hosted client-server architectures that assume continuous broadband connectivity, DNS resolution, and administrative access on the local host for runtime execution. In infrastructural edge-deployment zones, post-disaster humanitarian settings, high-security isolated networks, and digital-divide educational institutions, this centralized paradigm runs into severe operational barriers. abstract: After more than two decades of development, China has remained the world’s largest online retail market for 13 consecutive years, achieving a remarkable transformation from “the world’s factory” to “the world’s shopping center” and leading the development of the global e-commerce industry. However, the current development of China’s retail e-commerce is confronted with numerous difficulties and has entered a bottleneck. abstract: In a context of increasing political polarization, ideological bias poses a challenge to evidence-based reasoning and the evaluation of factual information. However, its systematic study is hindered by the lack of reliable and valid measurement tools and by the frequent conflation of ideological bias with ideological stance. Addressing this gap, we introduce the Ideological Bias Expression (IBE) scale, a novel measure grounded in signal detection theory that disentangles discrimination accuracy from ideological bias in individuals' evaluations of evidence. abstract: ABSTRACT Autonomous soft actuators are essential for untethered intelligent robotic systems. However, achieving energy‐efficient operation and long‐term shape retention in solid‐state platforms remains a significant challenge, as most conventional systems rely on continuous power input or complex fluidic architectures. abstract: This study examines the relationship between competence, education level, and service employee performance at DPMPTSP Serang City. A quantitative approach was applied involving 87 employees selected through a saturated sampling technique. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS. Competence in this study includes training, work experience, knowledge, communication, and work environment as important aspects supporting employees’ ability to perform service-related tasks. title: Network science reveals the structure and lasting impact of the Roman road system
abstract: Ancient infrastructure can leave lasting imprints on modern settlement patterns and mobility. The Roman road network connected vast regions of Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East, and is often mentioned as an example of such long-term impact. Yet its structural characteristics remain largely unquantified. Here we present a high spatial resolution quantitative exploratory analysis of the Roman Empire's road system, enabled by our creation of a spatially detailed Empire-wide dataset. abstract: Flexible satellite structures with lightweight solar panels are naturally prone to structural vibrations caused by attitude maneuvers, continuous environmental disturbances and deformation during deployment. abstract: Despite growing interest in bat–virus interactions, experimental infection studies (EIS) remain taxonomically and geographically restricted, limiting inference about bat immunology and zoonotic risk. title: Would-be Émigrés: Navigating the Academic Job Market Under Fascism
abstract: Abstract What defines an émigré scholar? Drawing on personal correspondence between members of the Unity of Science movement, this article emphasizes the contingency of the category by reconstructing the social and material conditions that shaped academic life under fascism. When scholars became refugees, they had to find ways to move their knowledge with them. Antisemitic discrimination restricted their access to libraries, conferences, and publishing contracts: the very things they needed to continue their work and secure jobs abroad. Would-be émigrés attempted to compensate by relying on th

title: Effectiveness of emergency nutrition program for toddlers after Mount Semeru eruption in Lumajang: CIPPO evaluation
abstract: Malnutrition in toddlers remains a public health concern in Indonesia. East Java reports a relatively high prevalence of wasting (7.2%), while Lumajang Regency recorded a severe wasting prevalence of 6.9% in 2022, exceeding WHO public health thresholds and increasing from the previous year. The 2021 eruption of Mount Semeru disrupted food systems and limited access to health and nutrition services, increasing nutritional risks among affected toddlers. This study evaluated the effectiveness of an emergency nutrition program for toddlers in Lumajang Regency, using the CIPPO model. This evaluativ
publisher: Jurusan Gizi Politeknik Kesehatan Kemenkes Aceh

title: Research-Related Competence, Productivity, and Culture among Secondary Mathematics Teachers in the Schools Division of Dagupan City
abstract: This study examined the relationship among research-related competence, research productivity, and research culture of secondary mathematics teachers in the Schools Division Office of Dagupan City. The inquiry was guided by Shulman’s Pedagogical Content Knowledge, Bandura’s Social Cognitive Theory, and the Framework Design Integration Model (FDIM), which emphasize the integration of knowledge, practice, and institutional support in teacher research. A descriptive–correlational design was employed, involving twenty-three mathematics teachers with prior action research experience. Data were coll
journal: International Journal of Research on Multidisciplinary Studies

title: Language shifts as a catalyst for social and educational cohesion in multilingual societies
abstract: Although the Indonesian New Capital City, or Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN), is a potential living laboratory of a multilingual society, studies investigating the extent to which language shift conditions stimulate educational cohesion remain limited. To fill this gap, this research aims to investigate language shifts at schools in IKN to achieve equitable education. The participants were teachers and high school students who lived in three subdistricts of IKN (Sepaku, Penajam Pasir Utara, and Muara Jawa). We conducted eight interviews and two classroom observations to capture the participants’ ling

title: Tracing the development of primary students' expressed sustainability conceptions through SDG-based classroom action research
abstract: This qualitative classroom action research study traced the development of primary school students' expressed sustainability conceptions during an 8-week interdisciplinary process based on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Participants were 31 fourth-grade students (aged 9–10) in one intact classroom of a public primary school in Istanbul, Türkiye. Instruction comprised 24 class periods of 40 min across eight weekly action research cycles; the second author taught all lessons while the first author observed every session. Data comprised pre- and post-instruction conception tasks, learn

title: Derechos humanos frente a la automatización de las decisiones públicas: revisión bibliográfica
abstract: La automatización de las decisiones públicas mediante sistemas de inteligencia artificial plantea riesgos relevantes para la protección de los derechos humanos, especialmente cuando sus resultados inciden en derechos, obligaciones o acceso a servicios públicos. El estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar las implicaciones jurídicas de estas tecnologías y las principales garantías aplicables frente a sus riesgos. Se desarrolló una investigación cualitativa, documental y descriptivo-analítica, basada en una revisión bibliográfica de 13 artículos científicos publicados entre 2021 y 2026. Los hallazgos
journal: Journal of Multidisciplinary Novel Journeys & Explorations

title: Water resources in Spain: addressing challenges to water security
abstract: Successfully addressing and resolving water challenges, in a global context where the vectors of population growth, urbanisation, climate change and globalisation are at work, is a key element to foster sustainable development and achieve an improvement in the quality of life of societies and people. It is essential that water is on the political agenda and that many actors play their role properly, with the appropriate governance. The Sustainable Development Goals are not always synergistic among them, and SDG 6 on water interacts with a number of other SDGs. Understanding this is essential t

title: Governing green enabling megaprojects: reconciling transformative risk-taking with megaproject delivery discipline
abstract: This paper introduces green enabling megaprojects (GEMs) to characterize an increasingly important class of infrastructure for climate change mitigation. GEMs are large-scale green infrastructure projects whose primary value lies in enabling broader socio-technical transformation through subsequent adoption, diffusion, and scaling. GEMs sit at the intersection of two distinct literatures and governance imperatives: mission-oriented innovation policy (MOIP), which emphasizes public-sector transformative risk-taking under deep uncertainty, and megaproject management (MPM), which emphasizes megap

title: Techno-Economic Assessment of LOHC-Based Hydrogen Export from Australia to Japan
abstract: Abstract This study develops a corridor-specific techno-economic framework for LOHC-based hydrogen export from Australia to Japan and applies it to four representative carrier systems: toluene/methylcyclohexane (TOL/MCH), dibenzyltoluene/perhydrodibenzyltoluene (H0-DBT/H18-DBT), N-ethylcarbazole/perhydro-N-ethylcarbazole (H0-NEC/H12-NEC), and benzene/cyclohexane (BZ/CH). The framework integrates carrier-specific process simulation, maritime logistics, regional cost assumptions, heat-supply options, and deployability factors within a unified hydrogen-to-hydrogen supply chain boundary. The resul
institutions: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

title: Evaluating geoscience campaigns in the conservation of water resources in the Western Region, Ghana
abstract: The Western Region of Ghana faces persistent water resource issues due to pollution, illegal mining, unsustainable land use, and degrading ecological integrity, public health, and livelihoods. Though geoscience-based water conservation campaigns have been initiated to remedy these issues, limited empirical data exist on their effectiveness in encouraging the conservation of water. This study assessed the impacts of these geoscience-based water conservation campaigns on water resource conservation in the area by evaluating their approaches, stakeholder involvement, and conservation results. A m
journal: JOURNAL OF GEOETHICS AND SOCIAL GEOSCIENCES

title: Mineralogical characteristics and soil behaviour of lime-stabilised dredged sediment from Sengguruh Reservoir for sustainable fill applications
abstract: Severe sedimentation in the Sengguruh Reservoir has reduced its effective storage capacity to approximately 24% of the original value, creating persistent dredging and spoil bank management problems. This study aimed to evaluate the potential reuse of dredged spoil bank sediment as sustainable fill material through lime stabilisation. Natural sediments and sediments treated with 10% and 15% calcium oxide on a dry weight basis were evaluated experimentally. Laboratory testing included specific gravity, grain-size distribution, Atterberg limits, soil classification based on USCS (unified soil cl
journal: Journal of Water and Land Development

title: Edadismo invisible: voces y experiencias en la atención hospitalaria
abstract: El objetivo fue analizar la presencia de prácticas edadistas en la atención sanitaria en el Pius Hospital de Valls (Tarragona), explorando cómo el trato, el lenguaje y las dinámicas asistenciales reflejan posibles actitudes discriminatorias hacia los pacientes mayores. Se examinó la influencia del contexto sociocultural y profesional en su manifestación y en la calidad del cuidado. Se adoptó un enfoque cualitativo descriptivo de carácter exploratorio, basado en entrevistas semiestructuradas a diez profesionales sanitarios. La recogida de datos se realizó entre abril y junio de 2025 y se analiz

title: Hybrid quantum-inspired secure and energy-efficient framework for wireless sensor networks using quantum key distribution and optimization techniques
abstract: Abstract Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) require secure and energy-efficient communication because sensor nodes operate with limited battery power, constrained communication range, and high vulnerability to interception, spoofing, and malicious forwarding. Existing methods usually optimize security, clustering, or routing independently, which reduces overall network efficiency under dense and adversarial conditions. To address this limitation, this work proposes a hybrid framework named BB84-CFG-OOA, which integrates BB84-inspired Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) for secure session key establish
institutions: Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science

title: Functional memory of drought affects leaf chemical defenses and microbial interactions in aspen
abstract: Abstract Drought is an increasingly important driver of tree mortality, but its long-term impacts on trait expression remain poorly understood. Leaves are a key interface at which trees respond to abiotic stress, and foliar traits such as chemical defenses and microbial communities may play an important role in determining post-drought resilience. Here, we tested whether prior-year drought leaves a persistent imprint on leaf traits in Populus tremuloides. Using a three-year common garden experiment with controlled water limitation, we measured two major classes of defensive phenolics—salicinoi
institutions: The University of Texas at Austin

title: Inteligencia artificial en educación superior: transformación sociotecnológica y desafíos éticos-regulatorios
abstract: Este ensayo reflexivo de corte documental examina la evolución histórica, los fundamentos técnicos y las implicaciones socioeducativas de la inteligencia artificial (IA), con énfasis en educación superior. Se parte de la trayectoria de la IA desde sus bases formales y hitos fundacionales hasta su consolidación contemporánea mediante aprendizaje automático, redes neuronales y aprendizaje profundo. A continuación, se analiza la incorporación de la IA en educación, confrontando la promesa de personalización y analítica del aprendizaje con críticas sobre tecnocratización, reducción del aprendizaje

title: Modeling determinants of women’s decision-making autonomy on agriculture and household matters in rural Ethiopia: a mixed effects beta regression tree analysis
abstract: Despite existing research on women's decision-making autonomy (WDMA), there remains a significant gap in understanding the complex factors influencing women's autonomy. This study investigated the determinants of WDMA in agriculture and household matters in rural Ethiopia. The study used data from nine rural districts in the Oromia and the former Southern Nations Nationalities and Peoples region in Ethiopia. A mixed effects beta regression tree model was used to identify variables impacting WDMA across diverse participant segments. The analysis incorporated various fixed effects, including fam

title: Graph-guided MADQN based handover strategy for LEO satellite networks
abstract: In low earth orbit satellite networks, the high orbital velocity of satellites causes frequent communication link handovers, which adversely affects user service quality and the efficiency of network resource management. To maintain communication continuity, an effective handover strategy is required. Traditional handover strategies are typically based on fixed decision rules, which makes it difficult to balance handover frequency, signal quality, and network load balancing. Reinforcement learning based methods, while capable of adapting to dynamic network conditions, suffer from low training

title: Spatiotemporal autocorrelation of landslides in neighborhoods of Recife, Brazil (2015–2024) based on the Moran and Lisa index
abstract: This study analyzes the spatiotemporal dynamics of landslide occurrences in neighborhoods of the municipality of Recife (PE), from 2015 to 2024, using spatial analysis techniques based on the Global Moran’s Index and Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA). Official data from the Recife Civil Defense, as well as landslide susceptibility maps prepared by CPRM and municipal monitoring information, were used. The analyses were performed in a Python environment, with the support of geoprocessing and spatial statistics tools. The results highlight the persistent presence of positive spatial

title: A Writer’s Universe: John Updike on Physics and Astronomy
abstract: Abstract Among the many twentieth-century authors who have been inspired by developments in science, the American novelist and poet John Updike stands out as a fascinating example. Interested in science and its history, he was well informed by his reading of popular science books and journals. From where did he get his information? How did scientists respond to his literary works referring to science, if at all? This paper offers a critical survey of Updike’s science-related writings from the mid-1950s to his death in 2009. Rather than adopting a literary-critical approach, its focus is on the

title: Adjudication Where Negotiation Is Required: Community Initiation in Taiwan's Renewable Energy Siting
abstract: ABSTRACT Renewable energy projects continue to fail at the local level despite enjoying broad public support and successive rounds of participatory reform. This article asks what institutional pattern produces this persistent gap and what kind of response would address it. Drawing on qualitative interviews with 10 actors across resident, developer, consultant, local government, and civil society positions, alongside procedural analysis of two decades of wind energy disputes in Penghu, Taiwan, the study traces how the architecture of the country's Environmental Impact Assessment generates confl

title: Shirking Responsibility and Accountability: Racial Capitalism, Biculturalism and the Ethics of the Crusaders Super Rugby Franchise’s Rebranding
abstract: This article examines the Crusaders Super Rugby franchise’s partial rebranding after the 15 March 2019 Christchurch mosque attacks as a case study in how sport reproduces settler/invader colonialism, racial capitalism and white possessive power in Aotearoa New Zealand. While the attacks prompted public scrutiny of the franchise’s name, medieval crusading symbolism and pre-match performance culture, New Zealand Rugby and the Crusaders retained the “Crusaders” name and substituted the horseman logo with koru-inspired branding. Drawing on Aileen Moreton-Robinson’s theorisation of the white posses

title: Modeling the pathway from transformational leadership to innovative work behavior via AI readiness: advancing SDG 4 and SDG 8 in Indonesian higher education
abstract: Drawing on a cross-sectional survey of 250 lecturers and administrative staff from Indonesian higher education institutions (HEIs), this study examined the statistical relationships among transformational leadership, AI readiness, and innovative work behavior (IWB) using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings showed that transformational leadership was positively associated with AI readiness (β = 0.654, p < 0.001) and IWB (β = 0.322, p < 0.001), while AI readiness was positively associated with IWB (β = 0.451, p < 0.001). The indirect effect of transformatio

title: Robustness Evaluation of Hyperspectral Image Classification Models Using Degradation-Aware Metrics
abstract: Hyperspectral image classification studies are generally evaluated on clean benchmark datasets and often report high-accuracy values. However, because real sensor data can be affected by different degradations, such as Gaussian, impulse, stripe, dead-line, and mixed noise, clean-data performance alone may be insufficient to explain the reliability of models under practical conditions. In this study, SVM, k-NN, 1D-CNN, 2D-CNN, 3D-CNN, Hybrid CNN, Dense CNN, and a transformer-based model were evaluated on the Indian Pines, Pavia University, and Salinas datasets under controlled noise scenarios.
journal: Black Sea Journal of Engineering and Science

title: Arab nationalism and historicity in the 1980s novel: Haydar Haydar’s Walīma li-aʿshāb al-baḥr and Rachid Boudjedra’s Maʿrakat al-Zuqāq
abstract: Two 1980s novels from the Maghreb and Mashreq, respectively – Algerian writer Rachid Boudjedra's Maʿrakat al-Zuqāq (Battle of the Strait, 1986) and Syrian writer Haydar Haydar's Walīma li-aʿshāb al-baḥr (Banquet for Seaweed, 1983) - offer formal and thematic critiques of a regime of historicity that they link to Arab nationalist states after decolonization. Using François Hartog's regimes of historicity, this essay reads these modernist novels as sites of delayed processing for the thwarted hopes of progressive, anti-colonial emancipation. title: Assessment of Household Water Security in Makurdi Town, Benue State, Nigeria
abstract: Makurdi town is contending with many water related issues that impede efforts targeted at achieving water security for the growing population. Water security is a multidimensional concept that seeks to address the array of issues related to water. Previous studies in Nigeria and Makurdi in particular, employ a methodology for water security assessment that merely accounts for water access or water scarcity, thereby limiting the scope of the concept. This study employed a modified framework to holistically determine the water security status of households in Makurdi town. Data was gathered via
journal: International journal of sustainable rural development.

title: Improvement of chaotic maps for k-NN classification using Lévy-flight whale optimization: multiple dataset comparison
abstract: Metaheuristic feature selection is frequently used to improve distance-based classification on tabular datasets, yet the empirical value of adding chaotic dynamics to already enhanced optimizers remains unclear. This paper presents a controlled multi-dataset benchmark of a binary Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) feature selector combined with Lévy-flight refinement and a k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) classifier. title: STRATEGI PENINGKATAN KEPUASAN DAN LOYALITAS PELANGGAN MELALUI KUALITAS PELAYANAN DI PT. SAHABAT PUTRA SERAYU DIENG
abstract: Kualitas layanan diakui sebagai determinan utama kinerja perusahaan pariwisata, berbagai studi menunjukkan bahwa terdapat kesenjangan antara ekspektasi wisatawan dan persepsi layanan yang diterima, terutama pada dimensi bukti fisik, keandalan, dan daya tanggap layanan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kepuasan dan loyalitas pelanggan melalui peningkatan kualitas pelayanan di PT. Sahabat Putra Serayu Dieng dengan menggunakan pendekatan SERVQUAL. journal: Business Preneur Jurnal Ilmu Administrasi Bisnis

title: TOURISM SITUATION IN THAILAND AND APPROPRIATE STRATEGIC ADJUSTMENTS
abstract: Tourism serves as a vital engine for the Thai economy, contributing significantly to national wealth; however, persistent disparities exist in income distribution between primary and secondary provinces. This study aims to analyze the current tourism situation in Thailand and identify appropriate strategic adjustments to enhance the industry’s resilience and sustainability. By evaluating the concentration of visitors and revenue, the research seeks to provide a roadmap for more equitable economic growth through tourism. This research utilizes secondary time-series data from 2012 to 2023 obtain

title: Delivering sustainable food: exploring college students’ willingness to pay for carbon labels in China via a choice experiment
abstract: The rapid expansion of online food delivery has intensified concerns about packaging waste and carbon emissions, making sustainable consumption an increasingly important component of the sector’s low-carbon transition. Whether environmental information disclosure can shift consumers’ choices toward lower-carbon alternatives is therefore an important issue for improving the sustainability of digital food-delivery platforms. title: Professional legitimacy in Swedish wildlife management: frontline bureaucrats in a gendered governance landscape
abstract: Swedish wildlife management is characterized by multi-level governance, stakeholder conflict, and strong cultural ties to hunting. In this contested arena, frontline wildlife officers play a central role in mediating between state authority and local interests, making professional legitimacy a critical institutional resource. journal: Journal of Environmental Planning and Management

title: Hydrogen from pine wood waste via pyrolysis and autothermal steam reforming: technoeconomic and environmental performance of single and co-production pathways
abstract: Biomass-based hydrogen production represents a promising pathway to reduce the environmental impacts associated with fossil-based hydrogen. In thermochemical pathways, biomass is typically converted into intermediate streams such as bio-oil prior to hydrogen production. However, in bio-oil reforming processes, a key unresolved question is whether hydrogen production should prioritize complete conversion of the pyrolysis liquid or selective upgrading of its aqueous fraction, recovering the organic fraction as a fuel co-product. title: About the influence of the use of geometric altimetry on cruise flight efficiency under nominal operations
abstract: Abstract The introduction of global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) generally enables the use of the geometric altitude for altimetry instead of the currently used barometric altitudes, which is indeed a simple and robust method for altimetry but is also subject to various measurement errors. By using geometric instead of barometric altimetry, a more efficient airspace design is be expected. title: The population dynamics in China: understanding the role of spread and backwash effect
abstract: Considering the declining population growth and increasing intra-provincial migration in China, the population issue becomes crucial for the sustainable development of the Chinese economy. We utilize data of 2010 and 2020 China Census to study the impact of the “spread-backwash” effects of large cities on county-level population dynamics over the past decade and investigate the potential mechanisms. title: Navigating Organisational Change in the Australian Public Service: Demographic Shifts and Leadership Perception
abstract: Organisational cultural change driven by demographic shifts is affecting employee perceptions of leadership roles within the Australian Public Service (APS). Despite longstanding diversity challenges, the APS has implemented policies to increase female employees’ representation in senior roles. This study examines the demographic composition and perceptions of Senior Executive Service (SES) leaders in the APS from 2018 to 2024, using APS census data (N = 127,262) and ordinary least squares (OLS) regression to analyse relationships among age, gender, and perceived leadership effectiveness. title: TEXTUAL INDICATORS OF CHARACTER IN SHAKESPEARE’S RICHARD iii
abstract: William Shakespeare is renowned in English and world literature for his masterful ly crafted characters. In this paper we will explore all textual indicators of characterization in William Shakespeare’s play Richard III, used for the construction of Richard`s character, based on the method proposed by the classical narratology theorist Shlomith Rimmon-Kenan in her study Narrative fiction (1983). title: INFLUENCE OF BIOCLIMATIC CONDITIONS ON REPORTED UNCOMPLICATED AND SEVERE MALARIA CASES IN THE SECOND DISTRICT OF COTONOU, BENIN
abstract: Malaria remains a major public health concern in Benin, and its seasonal pattern may be influenced by local climate. This study examined associations between bioclimatic conditions and reported uncomplicated and severe malaria cases in the second district of Cotonou. Monthly temperature, relative humidity and rainfall data for 1995-2024 were obtained from Météo-Bénin, while monthly malaria data for 2005-2024 were obtained from the Littoral Departmental Health Directorate. title: Temporal heterogeneity differential learning method for advanced equipment multi-timeseries measurements forecasting
abstract: Abstract Accurate modeling of multi-timeseries measurements (MTM) is the key to remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of advanced equipment. Existing approaches mostly model the MTM of different equipment stages on the uniform and fixed way, weak the differential learning ability based on the degree of degeneration information, which decreases the RUL prediction accuracy. Facing the gap, temporal heterogeneity differential learning (THDL) method is proposed for equipment RUL prediction based on MTM, which mainly consists of two key submodules. institutions: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

title: Organizational Culture as a Driver of Employee Performance: The Mediating Effects of Job Satisfaction and Motivation
abstract: This article examines the effect of organizational culture on worker performance through worker motivation and job satisfaction. The research used a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional strategy. Primary data were collected from 291 employees across various organizations using a structured questionnaire. Each construct was measured with a five-point Likert scale, and the measurement scales were adapted from previous reliable studies. title: New Insights Into the Three‐Dimensional Mechanics of the Flagellar Beat Cycle
abstract: Advances in imaging at the molecular scale have provided greater detail concerning the three-dimensional structure of the ciliary/flagellar axoneme. Additionally, it has recently been confirmed that electrostatic forces regulate the dynein-tubulin interaction at the microtubule binding domain (MTBD) of dynein, and at the junction of the nexin-dynein regulatory complex (N-DRC) with the adjacent outer doublet. title: Listening to the mountain: oral history, biocultural heritage, and sustainability transitions in Serra da Estrela
abstract: This article draws on a corpus of oral history interviews collected in Serra da Estrela, Portugal, to examine how community memory, territorial knowledge, and lived relationships with the mountain contribute to understanding socio-ecological change and rethinking sustainability in a context of climate disruption. Focusing on territory already recognized as a UNESCO Global Geopark and currently proposed for inscription as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, the study explores how oral testimony illuminates the biocultural dimensions of sustainability and the contribution of the Social Sciences and Huma

title: Análisis informétrico del impacto social en la producción científica de Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Colombia y México (2016–2024)
abstract: En el contexto de los debates recientes sobre la función social de la ciencia, el impacto social ha adquirido una presencia creciente como categoría discursiva en la evaluación de la ciencia, especialmente en América Latina. Este artículo analiza, desde un enfoque informétrico, la manera en que el impacto social es tematizado en la literatura científica producida en Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Colombia y México durante el periodo 2016–2024. title: Utilizing Architectural Design Strategies to Optimize Spatial Efficiency in A Proposed Convention and Exhibition Centre in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigates how architectural design strategies can optimise spatial efficiency in convention and exhibition centres, with application to a proposed facility in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. Convention centres are increasingly required to host simultaneous programmes (conferences, exhibitions, banquets, and civic events) and to support rapid changeovers; consequently, efficient spatial planning, clear circulation, and adaptability are critical to operational performance and user experience (Ovais Ansari, n.d.; Jude Barnaby & Igwegbe Uzodinma, 2024). journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

title: A Review of Sustainable Trade Practices and Employment in Uganda
abstract: The intersection of sustainable trade governance and labour-market outcomes has become a central concern for low-income, agriculture-dependent economies, yet the evidence base linking specific sustainable trade practices to employment changes in Uganda remains fragmented. This narrative review synthesises the available literature across five dimensions: voluntary sustainability certification schemes, environmental provisions in trade agreements, gender-differentiated employment outcomes, Aid for Trade and green trade facilitation, and skills development for sustainable production. journal: Ndejje University Journal Of Interdisciplinary Studies

title: Military Coup and Regional Integration in Africa: Themes, Trends and Threats to ECOWAS
abstract: West Africa in the past decade has witnessed an alarming resurgence of military coups. This article examines the implications of this coup wave for regional integration as it affects Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) using democratic theory as its framework. This article is predicated upon qualitative method of research, utilizing secondary sources of data collection from Journals, newspaper publications, online news outlets, official documents, etc. Anchored on the preceding methodology, we reviewed the literature on African coups and regional integration. journal: JOURNAL OF POLITICAL SCIENCE AND LEADERSHIP RESEARCH

title: The Negotiation of New Heights and Essence by Bakossi Traditional Authorities Under Colonial Rule
abstract: This paper aims to present the pride and prejudice of the Bakossi traditional authority in the south-west region of Cameroon. It shows how the imposition of colonial rule led to a systematic abuse and disregard for the local institutions that were so dear to the people. The Germans then British modified the political structures in which the traditional elite enjoyed a privileged position to their own advantage. title: The Spiritual Dimension of Palliative Care Patients and Their Caregivers in a Compassionate Community in Two Brazilian Favelas1: A Mixed-Methods Study
abstract: Spirituality is a key dimension of palliative care, contributing to well-being, supporting adjustment to illness, and serving as an important coping resource for patients and caregivers. In socially vulnerable settings, compassionate community initiatives may facilitate the integration of spiritual care and help mitigate the effects of limited access to health and social resources. title: Brazil’s Rare Earth Elements Landscape: From Geological Endowment to Mine-to-Magnet Integration—Operations, Resources, Bottlenecks, Market Prospects, and Research Gaps
abstract: Brazil has re-emerged as one of the most consequential rare-earth jurisdictions outside Asia, but geological scale alone does not determine whether it can capture strategic and economic value from rare earth elements (REEs). This structured critical review evaluates Brazil’s REE landscape from 2020 through 9 September 2026 using a mine-to-magnet framework that integrates geology, mineralogy, beneficiation, extraction, impurity control, separation, environmental performance, economics, policy, recycling, and downstream manufacturing. title: Research progress in the preparation of lactic acid from biomass by chemical catalytic process
abstract: Abstract Lactic acid (LA) is a versatile platform chemical widely used in food, pharmaceutical, and biodegradable plastic industries. While industrial LA production predominantly relies on fermentation, the chemo-catalytic conversion of renewable biomass-especially non-edible lignocellulosic feedstocks-has emerged as a promising alternative due to its potential for higher efficiency, lower environmental impact, and reduced competition with food resources. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in the chemo-catalytic production of lactic acid from biomass-derived sugars, glycerol

title: Violence at Peekskill! Paul Robeson, Anti-Communism, and Populist Fascism Among Veterans
abstract: In 1949, two riots rocked Paul Robeson concerts in Peekskill, New York. The riots were provoked by local veterans’ organizations and were not anomalous, as the American Legion and other groups intentionally targeted Robeson and his public appearances. Though scholars have examined the Peekskill riots and their relationship to Paul Robeson’s increased radicalism and his declining popularity, this article centers veterans’ organizing against Robeson as intentional, and the violence as unexceptional. title: Nexus Between Participation in Non-Formal Adult Education Programmes and Women’s Empowerment in Turkana County, Kenya
abstract: Education plays a critical role in promoting women’s empowerment, yet women in nomadic pastoralist communities in Kenya continue to face barriers such as poverty, cultural restrictions, early marriage, domestic responsibilities, and limited access to formal schooling. In Turkana County, these challenges contribute to low literacy levels and limit women’s economic participation, decision-making, and social and political engagement. abstract: Contemporary intellectual property (IP) governance remains strongly shaped by proprietary logics of exclusivity, control, and rights allocation, even as knowledge production becomes increasingly collaborative, cumulative, and digitally mediated. This study examines how the Knowledge Commons Framework can inform a stewardship-oriented reconceptualization of IP governance. title: Same event, different stories: a corpus-assisted critical discourse analysis of the 20th CPC National Congress in Chinese and US mainstream media
abstract: As China’s first major national congress in the post-pandemic era, the 20th CPC National Congress has considerable domestic and international influence. This study employs a corpus-assisted critical discourse analysis to investigate the divergent discursive constructions of the Congress across six mainstream Chinese and American media outlets. title: Techno-Convergence and Evidentiary Contemporaneity: Comparative Analysis of Application in Advanced Jurisdictions and Nigerian Criminal Justice System
abstract: The research assessed technological adoption and evidentiary reform in the Nigerian criminal justice system, comparing practices with the United States, United Kingdom and India. The study employed doctrinal and comparative analysis, reviewing statutory instruments, judicial decisions and institutional operations across the Nigeria Police Force, Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, Nigerian Correctional Service and the Judiciary. abstract: Purpose This study investigates how digital traceability systems operate as inter-organisational information systems (IOS) enabling information integration, visibility, and coordination across multi-tier fashion supply networks. Focusing on how firms build digital traceability infrastructures in anticipation of forthcoming regulatory requirements, the study examines the strategic, institutional, and operational drivers, socio-technical mechanisms, and traceability configurations that shape data integration and governance across organisational tiers. abstract: Where should one look for fungi in a bog? Historically, fungal diversity in peatlands has been studied primarily in peat itself – understandably, given that peat is the defining feature of these ecosystems – using methods such as sporocarp-based observations and microfungal culturing. These approaches suggested relatively modest richness. In this study, we asked whether that picture changes when we sample multiple contrasting substrates beyond peat. abstract: In Vietnam’s export-oriented economy, environmental law now operates at the intersection of domestic regulation, trade governance and corporate organization. This article develops developmental compliance capacity as a firm-level construct explaining how enterprises interpret green requirements, build routines and evidence, coordinate suppliers and, where organizational conditions permit, turn compliance into learning and upgrading. abstract: Ideal Halal ecotourism promotes Islamic values, economic growth, and the environmental sustainability needed to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). However, tourism development still largely focuses on economic goals and neglects socio-cultural and environmental aspects. Some post-mining areas, such as Perlang Village, Central Bangka, also face this issue, as they experienced ecological damage from tin mining activities. abstract: The dependable electrification of off-grid communities in Bangladesh continues to be a significant challenge, with the techno-economic feasibility of decentralized solar photovoltaic (PV) systems heavily impacted by the selection of solar tracking configurations and notable regional variations in irradiance. abstract: A review of Dougal McNeill's Forms of Freedom: Marxist Essays in New Zealand and Australian Literature, which questions what it means to think critically and imaginatively with the literary form.

abstract: This study investigates how epistemic hierarchies emerge and shift within families during informal, everyday science-related activities. Although informal science learning is increasingly recognized as important, limited research has examined how knowledge and authority are constructed and negotiated among family members in daily life. Using a dataset of self-recorded videos, audio recordings, interviews, and WhatsApp conversations collected over several months from three families, this study examines how family members take up and assign epistemic roles across different contexts. title: Analysis of Kinematic and Kinetic Parameters during Manual Load Lifting Using Markerless Motion Capture and Inverse Dynamics Method
abstract: Manual material handling activities continue to be a primary cause of musculoskeletal disorders in industrial environments. This study aimed to perform a biomechanical moment analysis of symmetric load lifting using kinematic data obtained via markerless motion capture technology without the use of physical sensors. abstract: This study describes a highly effective process innovation in power conversion architecture for Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) electric vehicle (EV) application, by integrating a photovoltaic (PV) system, a single-ended primary inductor converter (SEPIC), intelligent control techniques, and bidirectional energy transfer capability. abstract: Despite a global advocacy of the right to clean, healthy and sustainable environment, which strengthened the bond between environmental protection, sustainable development, social justice and human rights, a persistent gap has been observed towards environmental rights in the planning, conservation, restoration and institutional accountability.The paper develops a rights-based philosophy for environmental governance that integrates ecological integrity, environmental justice, community stewardship, participatory governance, institutional accountability, and sustainable development within a com

abstract: The Paudi Bhuiyan is one among the PVTGs of Odisha, predominantly inhabiting the bordering regions of Deogarh, Sundargarh, and Keonjhar districts. The deep-rooted cohabitation with nature over generations, the Paudi Bhuiyan community has developed a unique body of knowledge based on live experimentation on trial and error for healthcare practices. title: Examining weather impacts on urban travel demand in Nanjing, China during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Accurately characterizing variation in public transport demand is important for urban traffic management, especially when weather conditions and public-health disruptions jointly reshape travel patterns. Using monthly transportation statistics and weather observations for Nanjing, China, from February 2019 to December 2022, this study examines associations between weather conditions and passenger flow across buses, taxis, and the Rail Transit System (RTS) during the COVID-19 period. title: Dark Humor and 'Brainrot': The Hidden Power of Gen Z Laughter and Collective Identity Making
abstract: ‘Brainrot’ is a relatively new concept within fields such as anthropology, cognitive science, and psychology. It is generally defined as low-effort social media content associated with a range of negative consequences, including shortened attention spans and increasedanxiety. However, this article proposes an alternative understanding of brainrot rooted in its capacity to help Generation Z navigate and resist societal expectations, producing more generative and positive outcomes. title: Students’ Perception of Social Studies as a Tool for Curbing Social Vices in Plateau State, Nigeria
abstract: The study examined the influence of Students’ Perception of Social Studies as a Tool for Curbing Social Vices in Plateau State, Nigeria. The study raised three specific objectives and three research questions were answered. The study adopted the descriptive survey design and a sample of 3459 Junior Secondary II students selected from a population of 9193 using Yaro Yamane formula. title: Individualism Without Individuality: Friedrich Hayek and the Neoliberal Citizen
abstract: ABSTRACT Critics of neoliberalism increasingly examine its corrosive effects on democracy. Scholars often turn to Friedrich Hayek's political theory, arguing that it produces citizens who passively conform to spontaneous social orders. Yet insufficient attention has been paid to the normative conception of the human individual underlying his neoliberalism. This article demonstrates that Hayek's theory actively rejects individuality, understood as the cultivation and expression of one's distinct personal character. title: Full vector adaptive swarm decomposition and its application on damage identification of yaw bearings
abstract: Wind turbine yaw bearings play a critical role in power generation, and physical damage of these components directly incurs severe safety risks. To address the challenges of yaw bearing damage identification, a novel full vector adaptive swarm decomposition (FVASWD) method is proposed. title: Application and challenges of telephone‐assisted cardiopulmonary resuscitation combined with unmanned aerial vehicle‐mounted automated external defibrillator in out‐of‐hospital cardiac arrest
abstract: Abstract Background Out‐of‐hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a leading cause of death worldwide. Telephone‐assisted cardiopulmonary resuscitation (TCPR) and automated external defibrillators (AEDs) improve survival, but traditional emergency systems face delays due to traffic and geography. Objectives This narrative review examined the current application, technical challenges, and future potential of combining TCPR with unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)‐mounted AED systems in OHCA. title: From borders to courts: assembling pushback cases in a hostile transnational setting
abstract: Abstract This article examines the work of legal intermediaries in moving cases from the border to the court, focusing on pushbacks from Italy and Austria to Slovenia and along the Balkan corridor. It demonstrates that these practices occurred within a hostile transnational setting that, from the outset, dispersed and destabilized potential claimants, traces, and the litigation path. title: Birchers, Discordians, and Sex Education: The Libertarians in the Anaheim Sex-Ed Wars
abstract: Anaheim, California, was one of the first battlegrounds in the wars over sex education that started erupting in the 1960s. Hoiles on the anti-sex-education side of the debate and of Robert Anton Wilson and Robert Shea on the pro-sex-education side; it also describes how another radical libertarian, Ralph Raico, essentially synthesized the Hoiles and Wilson/Shea positions. abstract: Abstract Since the 19th century, numerous approaches have been developed to determine the relationship between Charles Darwin's theory of evolution and humans as cultural beings. All reductionist approaches, from Social Darwinism and its normative claims to Sociobiology and Memetics, have been subjected to considerable criticism, such as that of being subject to a naturalistic fallacy or assuming a simplifying and empirically untenable genetic or otherwise biological determinism. abstract: Cooperation among non-kin is sustained through repeated interactions and expectations of future reciprocity. The present study examined whether perceived similarity in reciprocity norms was associated with helping within established friendships and whether this association varied with helping cost. Participants were 255 Japanese adults who identified a same-gender friend living nearby and rated their perceived similarity to that friend in reciprocity norms, other moral concerns, physical appearance, tastes, and values. abstract: In January 2023, British Columbia (BC) implemented a three-year decriminalisation initiative, removing criminal sanctions for adults possessing up to 2.5 g of certain illegal drugs. abstract: This paper examines the challenges of environmental governance in Nigeria, where national frameworks like the Climate Change Act and the National Climate Change Policy face limitations in translating policy into practice due to weak institutional coordination, limited community engagement, and structural constraints. title: Nonlinear responses of net ecosystem productivity to heatwaves over the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau: insights from climate and vegetation
abstract: Global climate warming has intensified heatwave disasters over the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau (QTP), exerting persistent and far-reaching impacts on the regional carbon cycle, which has attracted extensive attention from the scientific community. abstract: Background Although Helicobacter pylori (Hp) infection is a major global public health challenge, clinically applicable tools for individualized risk stratification remain limited, particularly in geographically diverse and high-altitude populations. abstract: Slow- and controlled-release fertilizers (SRFs and CRFs) are increasingly used to improve nutrient-use efficiency and reduce nutrient losses, yet slower release does not inherently translate into superior field performance. abstract: This article examines how confessional normative frameworks shaped the regulation of financial transactions in early modern Germany through a comparison of the Jesuit theologian Gregorio de Valencia (1549–1603) and the Lutheran theologian Theodor Thumm (1586–1630). Both addressed the so-called five per cent contract, a financial arrangement designed to secure a fixed annual return while formally avoiding the prohibition of interest. abstract: The Covid pandemic was a pivotal episode in the evolution of the European Union's response to strategic disin-formation. This article deploys assemblage theory to advance a critical, interpretive understanding of truth contestation as an increasingly salient dimension of geopolitical conf lict – one in which foreign actors seek to undermine the epistemic foundations of rival political communities. abstract: Despite being carried out in India since 1951, cloud seeding, a weather modification technique that artificially induces rain to increase water supply, has not been thoroughly analysed with respect to its legality. Therefore, the main question this article addresses is whether cloud seeding is a lawful means of ensuring the right to water in India. abstract: Against the backdrop of reshuffled global economic governance and rising unilateralism, China and the EU, as two core global economies, share bilateral trade ties critical to world economic stability. In 2020, China proposed the dual-circulation new development strategy; meanwhile, the negotiation of the Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (CAI) between China and the EU was finalized, marking a breakthrough in cross-border institutional coordination. title: Genomic features, metabolism, and biotechnological applications of Candida tropicalis and other non-albicans Candida species
abstract: The production of bio-based products by yeasts from agroindustrial byproducts is a key strategy for advancing circular bioeconomy. abstract: Abstract This paper studies the macroeconomic impact of the Irish bank strike of 1966, which led to the closure of the major commercial banks for 3 months. abstract: The Gaza conflict, widely characterised as a genocide carried out by Israel, has challenged not only international norms of human rights and state conduct but also those of freedom of expression and democratic accountability within Commonwealth states and beyond. The Commonwealth hardly figured in the strikingly ineffectual international diplomacy that marked the two years after October 7th. The study used the partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) technique to analyse data from 312 bank practitioners. abstract: Smartphone-based human activity recognition (HAR) commonly relies on large sets of engineered time- and frequency-domain variables. abstract: August Wilson's Fences (1987 Pulitzer Prize), is one of his most notable works, distinguished by its profound human depth. By synthesising the strengths of existing models into a political economy framework, it is possible to better integrate the links, propose causal pathways, and more effectively incorporate relational theories of power and social class. abstract: A sustainable society within planetary limits requires structural changes. A right to care can be an important contribution for this transition. This article analyses how labour law could contribute to recognising and implementing a right to care. It focuses on individual rights to flexibility in the workplace. abstract: Failed states are a complex phenomenon with significant implications for global security, governance, and development. They destabilize regions, empower non-state actors, and increase transnational threats. abstract: Climate change is a major public health issue in the 21st century, and the links between climate change and health are increasingly becoming recognised by researchers and policy-makers. abstract: The accelerating reshaping of the global energy system and intensifying geopolitical competition have exposed the supply chains of energy production companies to complex risks. Traditional management paradigms urgently need to shift to a balance of efficiency and resilience. This paper focuses on energy production companies to systematically analyze their supply chain risk identification and resilience improvement paths. abstract: As linguistic landscape (LL) research has developed, analytical perspectives have expanded beyond descriptions of visible linguistic forms and content to encompass context, space, social meaning, language policy, sign production, and audience reception. abstract: ABSTRACT There is growing empirical evidence that “politics affects religion,” yet most of this work has been quantitative. abstract: The return of cultural artefacts taken during the colonial era seems to be a matter of course in our time. But what happens if the communities to whom these objects should be returned have for long ceased to exist and their successors are involved in a civil war? abstract: This paper examines how Chinua Achebe represents war and trauma in There Was a Country: A Personal History of Biafra through an integrated psychoanalytic and postmodern framework. abstract: This study investigates the behavioural and operational dynamics of a night-time demand-responsive transport (DRT) system in the alpine resort of Hakuba, Japan, within a digitally mediated service environment, with particular attention to the temporal and spatial patterns of seasonal tourism. abstract: Intense solar eruptions occasionally accelerate solar energetic particles (SEPs) and trigger ground-level enhancements (GLEs). This paper presents a domain ontology for magnetic materials, developed within the European Union funded Magnetic Multiscale Modelling Suite (MaMMoS) project and aligned with the Elementary Multiperspective Material Ontology (EMMO). abstract: SoftMobility is a Python library for modelling deformable assemblies of spheres in Stokes flows. abstract: Quantum computers can potentially solve large-scale combinatorial problems very efficiently when the problems are first converted into the quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) format. abstract: Interpreter agents built on machine translation (MT) increasingly mediate live conversation between people who do not share a language, yet we still evaluate them with metrics built for isolated sentences, which measure fidelity rather than whether communication succeeds. abstract: Reliable in situ observations of sea surface wind (SSW) in tropical cyclones (TCs) remain extremely limited because of the difficulty of operating conventional observing platforms under severe weather conditions.
