Shipping activities significantly affect local plastic loads and, to respond to this ongoing problem, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) is coordinating efforts to address plastic emissions from international shipping. abstract: This study investigates the occurrence, distribution, and ecological risks of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) in surface sediments collected from 17 stations in the Upper Gulf of Thailand (uGoT). abstract: The family Brassicaceae Burnett is one of the important families because of its position in nature and its economic status in human life. This family is represented by 3,628 species from 328 genera in the world. 248 species from 74 genera were identified in the Republic of Azerbaijan, and 165 species from 66 genera in the territory of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic. title: Orchidaceae Spirito-Sanctensis: A taxonomic and conservation synopsis of orchid diversity in the state of Espírito Santo, Brazil
abstract: The diversity of Orchidaceae in the state of Espírito Santo, southeastern Brazil, was reassessed 40 years after the last comprehensive survey conducted for the region. The study was based on the examination of herbarium specimens, a critical review of the literature, and targeted field expeditions carried out in different phytophysiognomies. A total of 730 taxa (728 species, one subspecies, and one variety) were documented, representing an increase of 130 taxa compared to the 600 previously recorded by Augusto Ruschi. abstract: The rise in global bacterial resistance has made the development of new therapies an urgent challenge, positioning Pseudomonas aeruginosa as a critical priority pathogen. In this context, phytotherapy stands out due to the wide diversity of bioactive compounds with antimicrobial potential. abstract: Abstract The recent Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise has raised global public health alarms due to its dangerous ability to person-to-person spread. Hantavirus infections primarily manifest as hemorrhagic fever with Eurasian renal syndrome (HFRS) and Americas hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), both characterized by endothelial manifestation. abstract: Abstract Background Arctic ecosystems are experiencing unprecedented warming, driving vegetation expansion into previously barren areas. Although Arctic greening is expected to alter biogeochemical cycles, how vegetation cover shapes soil microbial communities and their functional potential remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how vegetation cover structures bacterial and fungal communities across three soil depths (0–2, 5–10 and 30–50 cm) on remote Russian High-Arctic islands using soil DNA metabarcoding and functional prediction. abstract: Maritime transport adds to greenhouse gas emissions, but fishing boats under 100 GT are often overlooked, even though their fuel-heavy operations make diesel engines and generators run inefficiently at low loads. This study creates a resistance–solar energy-balance framework to evaluate the feasibility and fuel reduction potential of solar PV-assisted hybrid propulsion for a 30 GT fishing vessel in tropical waters. abstract: Context Narratives around declines and extinctions of critical weight range (CWR) mammals in Australia have focused on the dramatic impacts of invasive predators and habitat decline. For some species, human-wildlife conflict has had a greater impact than previously perceived. Aims We aim to explore the role of human-wildlife conflict in the decline of bandicoots in New South Wales (NSW). abstract: This paper investigates Western writings on Ottoman Algeria as more than mere historical documentation.The records left behind by consuls, diplomats, captives, clergymen, travelers and intelligence agents form a rich and diverse body of texts that, despite this diversity, converges on a single common purpose: gathering strategic intelligence that paved the way for the French invasion of Algeria in 1830.The research rests on four main axes: a typology of Western authors and their backgrounds; the writing techniques used by these authors and their sources of knowledge; the political, religious,

title: A 400‐Year Antarctic Ice‐Core Perchlorate Record Reveals Variability in Stratospheric Chlorine Chemistry
abstract: Abstract Perchlorate (ClO 4 − ) in polar ice preserves past chlorine oxidation chemistry; however, multi‐centennial Antarctic ClO 4 − records and the mechanisms controlling their variability remain poorly constrained. Here, we present the first 400‐year (1616−2016) ClO 4 − record from an Antarctic ice core, revealing two regimes separated around 1980. Before 1980, ClO 4 − variability is primarily controlled by natural drivers. title: Free Space Optics: Present Applications and Emerging Future Challenges
abstract: Free Space Optics (FSO) is a communication method that uses open space as the medium between transceivers, which must be in line of sight (LOS) for successful optical signal transmission. The medium can be air, outer space, or a vacuum. This system is suitable for communication in various environments and offers advantages like high bandwidth and no need for spectrum licensing. However, FSO performance depends on atmospheric conditions, as factors such as rain, fog, haze, physical obstructions, scattering, and turbulence can affect transmission. abstract: Selecting preserving parameters is key to deep fidelity coring and cost reduction. For achieving cost-effective fidelity coring under the dominant controlling factors, first, this study employed local outlier factor algorithm to screen homogeneous samples. title: A new species of Zonites Montfort, 1810 from the Aegean (Chtapodia, Greece): islet endemic and critically endangered
abstract: The species Zonites whittakeri n. sp. (Zonitidae) is described from two islets off Mykonos Island (Cyclades, Aegean, Greece). A small population of the species persists on the islet of Chtapodia, whereas only subfossil shells were recovered from Tragonisi islet, suggesting that the species is locally extinct. title: Global Black Speculative Collage
abstract: Abstract Since the turn of this century, artists of African descent have worked to refract the relation between Black Studies and African Studies, often blurring the lines between these two fields. Braiding together the speculative mode and the practice of collage, Chino Amobi’s 2017 electronic music album Paradiso and Wangechi Mutu’s 2014 multimedia painting series Nguva na Nyoka cultivate opacity, otherworldliness, fragmentation, and disorder. title: From Anthropocentrism to Hydrocentric Ethics: A Qur’anic Reading of QS. Al-Anbiya’ [21]:30 and the Global Water Crisis
abstract: The global water crisis raises fundamental questions about how human relationships with water should be understood beyond its treatment as an economic resource. This study examines QS. Al-Anbiyā’ [21]:30 and related Qur’anic passages to develop a water-centered ethical perspective in response to contemporary ecological challenges. title: Topography of the High Country, Ancient Spatial Transformation of Eastern Anatolia from Uruatri to Armenia
abstract: This article examines how the topography of Eastern Anatolia was described, named and given meaning in ancient sources, arguing that its mountains, valleys and river systems functioned less as a physical backdrop than as an active component of political strategy, imperial ideology and the construction of local identity and memory. The discussion runs from the Uruatri and Nairi confederations through the Kingdom of Urartu to the Persian-Achaemenid, Hellenic and Roman periods. title: Four new species and new distributional records for Australian caddisflies in the genus Ecnomus McLachlan (Trichoptera: Ecnomidae)
abstract: A recent surge in collection of fresh caddisfly material for molecular studies resulted in the discovery of four new species of Ecnomus, the first since a major review of Australian members of the genus by Cartwright in 1990. Three of the new species are from north-eastern Queensland: E. giblini sp. nov., E. lesteri sp. nov. and E. mundyi sp. nov., the latter resulting from recognition that E. apiculatus Cartwright, 1990 comprises two distinct species. The fourth new species, E. barwonensis sp. nov., also derives from a split from another species, the very similar E. continentalis Ulmer, 1916.

title: Between Segregation and Permeability: The VOC’s Spatial Dilemma in Zeelandia Facing External Actors and Intervening Groups (1624–1662)
abstract: Abstract This study re-evaluates the “dual city” model through the case of the VOC’s Zeelandia in the seventeenth century. It argues that the settlement’s spatial order was crucially shaped not only by Dutch-indigenous relations but also by an external force: Chinese pirate-merchant confederations. This Chinese intermediary group, forming the socio-economic core, fostered a colonial dynamic of simultaneous dependence and distrust. title: From one tree to the canopy: an evolutionary design trajectory for tethered robotics in forest environments
abstract: Forest robotics has largely evolved along a ground-first and flight-dominant trajectory, treating the canopy as a region to observe or briefly access rather than a habitat to inhabit. In this Perspective, we propose an alternative canopy-first framework in which robots operate through anchoring, suspension, and tension-mediated interaction with the environment. title: The Stability‐Instability Paradox and the Evolving Balance of Terror in the Middle East
abstract: Abstract In launching its war on Iran, Washington has committed a grave mistake by allowing a weakened Islamic Republic to reconstitute a regional balance of terror. This article shows how the Cold War‐era stability‐instability paradox has been restored in a new form, creating an equilibrium that discourages open warfare while reducing the advantages Israel and the United States had gained over Iran during the previous two years. abstract: Obese tourists represent a growing yet underexamined market segment whose decision-making processes remain insufficiently understood within tourism development research. This study investigates the psychological and experiential factors shaping obese tourists’ travel intentions by integrating social identity and complexity theories. abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become increasingly important in surveillance, environmental monitoring, mapping, and scientific research, where flight stability and control performance are essential for safe and reliable operation. This study focuses on the modeling and stability analysis of an Aerosonde UAV using a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) control approach. title: Policy responses to overtourism
abstract: Overtourism has emerged as one of the most debated challenges affecting major tourist destinations, with Italy frequently cited as a prominent case. This paper examines the policy responses to overtourism in Italy, focusing on how institutional arrangements, interest groups, and public discourse shape the management of tourism growth. Drawing on existing literature and emblematic cases - most notably Venice and Florence - the study argues that overtourism cannot be understood solely as the outcome of excessive visitor numbers. title: WARDING OFF A ROMAN INVASION IN AETHIOPIA (UPPER NUBIA) WITH TALL ELEPHANT TALES? REVISITING PLINY, NATURALIS HISTORIA 6.186
abstract: Abstract It has recently been suggested that the Romans baulked at the idea of expanding their empire beyond Egypt into Aethiopia (Upper Nubia) during the principate of Nero because they were tricked into thinking that a powerful army equipped with war elephants awaited them. This discussion aims to demonstrate that such a view, based on a minority reading of Pliny, HN 6.186 that plumps for 3,000 elephants once being stationed on the island of Meroë, is difficult to support on both textual and contextual grounds.

title: Facial emotional responses to visual representations of deprived experiences in ICE environments: an exploratory analog space mission case study
abstract: Isolated, confined, and extreme (ICE) environments, such as space analog habitats, expose individuals to prolonged sensory and social deprivation, posing risks to psychological well-being. This exploratory study examined whether visual representations of everyday experiences unavailable during isolation elicit measurable facial emotional responses in analog astronauts. title: Rethinking “Dead” Objects: Baya Pandang and the Cultural Lives of Iban Artifacts in Sarawak Museum Collections
abstract: Museums are among the most important institutions safeguarding indigenous cultural heritage. However, their colonial institutional origins have often obscured the original uses, values, and meanings that cultural materials hold for the indigenous communities who created and continue to claim them. This study examines three Iban cultural objects held in the Sarawak Museum that are widely assumed, within a Western museological frame, to have lost their significance once removed from their original cultural and social context. title: “Women of the Happy Life”: Prostitution, Public Morality, and Venereal Disease in US‐Occupied Nicaragua, 1912–33
abstract: ABSTRACT During the years of the US occupation (1912–33), Nicaragua's government legally regulated prostitution. Convinced of their objectives to protect society's moral and public health, politicians embarked on a long struggle to apprehend, quarantine, and segregate female prostitutes nationwide. Through a comparative analysis of these codes, this article discusses the language and changes in these regulations to examine the extent to which the broader context of US intervention shaped local perceptions and actions regarding non‐elite female sexuality. abstract: Introduction Commercial hypersonic point-to-point (P2P) travel promises intercontinental flights in under 90 min, yet viability depends on systems-level integration of advanced technologies and infrastructure. This paper addresses the critical question of whether such travel can be technically feasible, economically viable, and environmentally sustainable within the coming decades. abstract: Motorable roads have become such an essential part of the Himalaya that they are celebrated and prayed for. But who are the people who build them? The army, engineers, and the state are usually credited with the construction of high-altitude roads in India, but the road workers who often endure significant hardship while performing this labor have largely remained invisible in both national discourses and academic scholarship. abstract: River tourism has emerged as an important means of promoting sustainable regional development, especially in ecologically and culturally important destinations. However, increasing climatic variability, technological transformation, and growing community expectations pose significant challenges to the long-term sustainability of the river tourism system. This study explores the future of sustainable river tourism in the Brahmaputra River Basin, Assam, India, through a socio-ecological perspective informed by resilience theory and socio-ecological systems (SES) theory. abstract: Summary A growing body of evidence suggests that Nuragic Sardinia played a role, as yet poorly understood, in the metal trade between Scandinavia, Atlantic Europe, and the Mediterranean during the Bronze Age. title: Entwining sound, space and narratives. Sound design approaches in exhibitions
abstract: This article explores the evolution of exhibition design, focusing on the integration of sound as a key narrative and experiential element. In recent decades, technological advances and discoveries in neuroscience have influenced the design of exhibition spaces, transforming them into multimodal experiences that go beyond mere visual engagement. abstract: Antarctica remains one of the least explored regions of the world in terms of lichen diversity, and many remote localities still harbor undescribed taxa. abstract: Cooking emissions are increasingly important sources of organic aerosol in densely populated urban areas as clean-air actions reduce emissions from industrial activities and fossil-fuel combustion. title: Undisciplining service design: Towards a grammar of possibility
abstract: Despite its ambitions to transform service systems, service design has been critiqued for reproducing the status quo and normalizing others into dominant social expectations. To move away from the circulation of hegemonic structures, the service design discipline needs to be challenged. Drawing on queer theory, this paper explores how service design can be undisciplined to create a grammar of possibility for making service systems otherwise. title: Lichens and lichenicolous fungi of Prins Karls Forland (Svalbard Archipelago)
abstract: The paper presents data on lichens and lichenicolous fungi for Prins Karls Forland (NW of Svalbard archipelago). For the island, 283 species of lichens and 21 lichenicolous fungi have been identified to date. Seventy species of lichens and 17 lichenicolous fungi are listed for the first time for the study area, of which Arthonia epipolytropa, Gyalecta peziza, Lasiosphaeriopsis christiansenii, Porpidia rugosa, and Sclerococcum protothallinum are reported for the first time for the Svalbard archipelago. institutions: Komarov Botanical Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences

title: Rare and delicious: from monster to meal in Japanese gourmet fantasy manga
abstract: This study examines how gourmet fantasy manga, particularly Delicious in Dungeon and Campfire Cooking in Another World with My Absurd Skill, reconfigure monstrosity through the act of cooking and consumption. Drawing on textual, semiotic, and cultural hermeneutic analysis, the study argues that such transformations are not merely aesthetic, but grounded in deeper symbolic and cultural logics. The analysis identifies three key dimensions underlying this transformation. First, monsters are culturally and visually constructed through folkloric traditions and recognisable visual features. title: Personal health impacts of adventurous outdoor learning
abstract: Abstract This article examines the burgeoning field of study exploring links between health, wellbeing, and adventurous outdoor learning. Key terms (outdoor learning, adventure, nature, health, wellbeing, and wellness) are defined before delving into dimensions of wellbeing that contribute to human health, with specific outdoor learning components for meaningful development of these dimensions. The authors have varied backgrounds in outdoor learning and bring collective expertise in biochemistry, neurophysiology, indigenous healing, remote health promotion, ecohealth, and wellbeing. journal: Journal of Outdoor and Environmental Education
institutions: The University of Notre Dame Australia

title: From internal peace to the discourse of holy war: Tracing discursive continuities from the peace of god movement to the letters of Catherine of Siena
abstract: In medieval Latin Christendom, the discourse of peace was not confined to the mitigation of conflict and the prevention of war; rather, it developed into an ideological mechanism that oriented collective energies toward specific purposes. This study investigates how, in Medieval Western Europe, the discourse of peace, initially intended to bring violence to an end, gradually ceased to aim at its complete elimination and was transformed into a politico-religious mechanism that reordered and externalized violence. Within this framework, the study analyzes whether there exists an intellectual and

title: Behind the facades of Ctesiphon: an archaeometric study of stucco architectural decoration from the Sasanian and Early Islamic periods
abstract: Abstract Ctesiphon, the capital of the Sasanian Empire (ca. 224–651 CE), was a major center of political power and artistic production in Mesopotamia. Excavations conducted in the 1920s–30s by the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and the Metropolitan Museum of Art revealed an extensive corpus of stucco decorations from Sasanian and Early Islamic contexts. Their varied forms, decorative patterns, architectural contexts, and dates of production make these stuccos particularly valuable for comparative study. title: Two new species of the genus Eremiothrips Priesner (Thysanoptera, Thripidae) from Saudi Arabia
abstract: The genus Eremiothrips Priesner, which inhabits xeric environments, is studied. The male of E. brunneus (zur Strassen) is described for the first time. Two new species, E. tetraenae sp. nov . collected from Tetraena simplex and E. xerophilus sp. nov . from Tamarix sp., are also described. A key to the Eremiothrips species lacking drepanae on abdominal tergite IX is provided.

title: Insights into morpho-biochemical characterisation and β-ODAP profiling of diverse genotypes of grasspea
abstract: Grasspea (Lathyrus sativus L.) is a versatile, climate-resilient legume valued for its nutritional richness and low input requirements. However, the presence of the neurotoxin β-N-oxalyl-L-α, β-diaminopropionic acid (β-ODAP) has limited its popularity. The present study aimed to identify promising low-ODAP grasspea genotypes for rice-fallow ecosystems of the Gangetic Plains of India through comprehensive morpho-biochemical characterisation. Fifteen genotypes of diverse origin were evaluated in a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with 3 replications and observations were recorded from fiv
institutions: International Center for Agricultural Research in the Dry Areas

title: Updated checklist of non-psoroptidid Astigmata in China (Acariformes)
abstract: This paper presents a revised checklist cataloging 160 species across 61 genera in 17 families of non-psoroptidid Astigmata known to occur in China. Among these, eight species have been newly documented since the 2010 review, and a further nineteen previously overlooked species have now been incorporated. Furthermore, one erroneous record, Sancassania karnatakaensis (Krishna Rao & Ranganath), has been corrected by its removal. The updated binomial name, Chinese name, and detailed information regarding hosts, distribution, and other relevant data are provided for each species.

title: Distributed Agent-Based Scheduling of Smart Port Operations under Cost and Emissions Constraints
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a distributed, emission-aware scheduling framework for smart port energy management, designed to coordinate heterogeneous flexible electric loads under operational, economic, and environmental constraints. The proposed approach addresses the coordinated scheduling of refrigerated containers (reefers), plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs), and shore-to-ship power supply systems, with the objective of reducing total operational cost while satisfying asset-level constraints and ship-level and port-level emission limits. institutions: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

title: Colonial memories in landscapes and waterways: the vital materialism of troubling childhood histories
abstract: This article shares a postqualitative, new materialist approach to memory work and storytelling, foregrounding the entangled colonial histories embedded in water and landscape. With its life-giving properties, water is a vital matter through which we can rethink histories to connect with the more-than-human and decolonise ourselves. Using new materialism, we create a watery assemblage (images and text) to challenge our thinking around the colonial histories embedded in the waterscapes. title: From forbidden site to global attraction: Alula's narrative re-engineering
abstract: This paper examines the socio-political and religious transformations in Saudi Arabia's AlUla region, with a focus on Hegra. Once avoided for religious reasons, the site has been repurposed within Vision 2030. This study offers a systematic textual account of this narrative shift using Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) on three corpora: state documents (including the tourism website), media, and religious texts. journal: Annals of Tourism Research Empirical Insights

title: From Nahda to Naksa: Some Marxist Perspectives on the Arab National Question
abstract: This article examines the trajectory of Arab nationalism through a Marxist lens, analyzing its historical emergence, political ascendancy, and eventual decline. It posits the Palestinian question as central to the development of Arab nationalist consciousness and anti-imperialist struggle, arguing that the fragmentation of a unified Arab stance reflects broader geopolitical defeats and the consolidation of dependent capitalist relations. journal: Agrarian South Journal of Political Economy A triannual Journal of Agrarian South Network and CARES

title: A Perspective on the Historical Role and Future of Bactris Gasipaes as a Food Crop
abstract: Peach palm (Bactris gasipaes) is a domesticated perennial of the tropical Americas historically cultivated within Indigenous agroforestry systems. Interdisciplinary evidence indicates that it functioned as a staple in pre-Columbian Amazonia, embedded in diversified, human-managed forests. Despite its nutritional and agronomic potential, modern development efforts have not integrated it into contemporary food economies, largely due to a mismatch with prevailing models based on annual monocultures. title: Analysis of the current state and medium-term forecast of transport system development parameters up to 2028
abstract: The article presents an analysis of the dynamics of key indicators of the development of the Russian transportation industry in 2023–2025. It provides forecast values for the period up to 2028, taking into account current trends and exogenous macroeconomic parameters defined in the latest Forecast of the Social and Economic Development of the Russian Federation for 2026 and for the Planning Period of 2027 and 2028, as well as in other strategic documents.

title: Gleb Wataghin and his mission in Brazil: a memoir
abstract: Abstract This contribution, based on a talk delivered at the Workshop Ukrainian Contributions to Particle Physics: History and Prospects, offers a personal memoir of Gleb Wataghin (1899–1986) and his role in the institutional development of modern physics at the University of São Paulo and in Brazil. Born in what is now Ukraine and educated in Turin, Wataghin joined the newly created university in São Paulo in 1934, where he helped establish a physics department and research school. title: Global Sensitivity of Constraint Analysis method: Drag coefficient and Stall Speed selection for Small UAVs
abstract: The Constraint analysis method is applied in the early stages of aircraft conceptual design for determining preliminary sizing parameters such as wing loading and power loading. However, its application to small UAVs is challenged by uncertainties in several key input parameters, particularly those that require detailed geometric or aerodynamic information that is typically unavailable during the early design stages. title: Mongolian Loanwords in Kazakh: A Semantic and Cultural Analysis
abstract: This study provides a detailed analysis of Mongolic loanwords in Kazakh in terms of their historical origins, phonological and morphological adaptation, and semantic change. The main source of the research is Kazak Tiliniŋ Kirme Sözder Sözdigi (The Dictionary of Borrowed Words in the Kazakh Language), which represents a comprehensive corpus of borrowed vocabulary. Through a systematic and detailed examination of this dictionary, a large number of words of Mongolic origin have been identified and compared with their occurrences both in historical records and in modern Kazakh. title: The Legality of US-Israeli Joint Decapitation Operations in Iran: Crime of Aggression or Self-Defense?
abstract: Background: Following 2025's failed negotiations, the US-Israeli military operation Epic Fury on 28 February 2026 marked a sharp escalation against Iran's nuclear and military infrastructure and leadership through a major regional force build-up. Methodology: The study employs a legal doctrinal method, utilizing Article 8 bis of the Rome Statute, the Caroline Test, and International Humanitarian Law (IHL). title: Empowering leadership as a pathway to enhance job satisfaction among college employees
abstract: The study aimed to determine the effect of empowering leadership on employees' job satisfaction. To support the purpose, the literature was reviewed, and theories were established to strengthen the study's title. The study employed a descriptive and correlational research design. To gather the data, validated questionnaires were used, and descriptive and inferential statistics were used to analyze the data. title: ‘The worst of all Turkish peoples’: Ibn Faḍlān’s travel account as British naval intelligence
abstract: Abstract The tenth-century CE Arabic travel account of Aḥmad Ibn Faḍlān has seen many reactions, receptions, and afterlives in Islamicate languages and in European settings. These relate both to the identity and presumed authority of Ibn Faḍlān as an eyewitness observer and presumed diplomat, and to the contents of his account. Considering different presentations of Ibn Faḍlān’s role and identity, this article approaches reactions to and uses of Ibn Faḍlān’s descriptions of the Bāshghird, particularly within a 1918 British military intelligence document, in order to consider Ibn Faḍlān’s poten

title: El descenso al inframundo, el matrimonio sagrado y la renovación de la naturaleza: simbología y función del tesoro de El Carambolo (Camas, Sevilla)
abstract: En la presente publicación se realiza una propuesta funcional y simbólica para el conjunto áureo procedente del santuario tartésico de El Carambolo (Camas, Sevilla). Para ello se han tomado como principales referentes las joyas y representaciones iconográficas chipriotas, sirias y asirias de los siglos X-VI a. C., así como el mito del Descenso de Inanna/Ishtar a los Infiernos. Como resultado, se ha dividido el tesoro en dos lotes. title: Ferry Retrouvé : Leaving the History of Empire Out of the “Liberal Moment” in France
abstract: This article examines how and why empire went missing from the liberal revival that began in 1970s France by examining a nineteenth-century political figure “rediscovered” during it: Jules Ferry, who as premier between 1880 and 1885 oversaw not only the creation of a secular school system in France, but also a huge burst of overseas expansion. In their portraits of him starting in the 1980s, historians such as François Furet and Mona Ozouf emphasized the former, while minimizing or excusing the latter. abstract: Contemporary air transport is one of the fastest-growing segments of the transportation market, providing the mobility of passengers and goods on a global scale. In response to increasing demand and growing interest in this mode of transport, the sector must continuously improve and adapt to changing market needs. This process is closely associated with dynamic changes in tax policy. title: Bajo asedio: la defensa de Filipinas de las incursiones neerlandesas (1600-1648)
abstract: La Compañía de las Indias Orientales neerlandesa (VOC), a lo largo de su enfrentamiento con la Monarquía Hispánica, realizó durante casi medio siglo más de una veintena de ataques de diferente índole sobre las Filipinas. El archipiélago se convirtió en un frente estratégico y activo de la guerra entre la Monarquía Hispánica y la República Neerlandesa durante la primera mitad del siglo XVII. institutions: Universidad Nacional de Educación a Distancia

title: Characterizing Wildlife Response to Biomimetic and Conventional Underwater Vehicles
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are a promising alternative to divers for scalable collection of natural ocean ecology data. However, these robots may disturb local fauna and cause drastic behavioral differences compared to other monitoring techniques, decreasing their value as scientific tools. A promising prospect is to make AUVs that are more biomimetic, with the hope that taking on the form and behavior of a non-predatory animal may reduce adverse responses. title: Towards Effective Visual-Inertial SLAM with Passive-Only Sensors for Low-Cost Autonomous Underwater Vehicles
abstract: Improvements to Visual-Inertial Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (VI-SLAM) for low-cost autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are critical for transitioning advanced marine robotics from specialized labs to broader research and hobbyist applications. While high-end AUVs typically rely on expensive sensor suites - such as Doppler Velocity Logs (DVLs) and Ultra-Short Baseline (USBL) systems - this work demonstrates that robust, high-quality navigation is achievable using a sub-$10, 000(USD) platform equipped only with inexpensive consumer-grade sensors. title: Acoustic-based Guidance for Automatic Docking of Holonomic AUVs
abstract: This paper describes a system to automatically dock an AUV onto a docking station without precise knowledge of the position and orientation of the latter, in the presence of unknown ocean currents, using a fully acoustic sensing architecture. The system relies on a pair of Ultrashort Baseline sensors, one onboard the vehicle and one installed on a seabed-resident docking station, enabling operation in low-visibility environments where cameras are ineffective. title: AquaCap: A Training-Free Underwater Embodied Agent with Code-as-Policy
abstract: Recent advances in vision-language-action models have stimulated growing interest in underwater embodied intelligence. However, their reliance on large-scale interaction data limits their applicability underwater, where data collection is costly and scarce. To address this challenge, we present AquaCap, a training-free Code-as-Policy framework for autonomous underwater navigation and manipulation. title: Range-Aided SLAM Initialization Exploiting Accurate Heading Information
abstract: This paper presents a novel initialization method for range-aided simultaneous localization and mapping (RA-SLAM). The general SLAM problem has a well-known separable structure where landmark and robot positions can be solved for in a linear fashion given known robot headings. This paper considers the case where highly accurate heading information is available, which is typical of autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) navigation, to solve for the range transponder and robot positions. title: Cosmogenic radiocarbon production and glacial cycles control marine radiocarbon archive variations
abstract: Abstract Marine radiocarbon archives are depleted relative to the atmosphere, which is commonly expressed as the marine radiocarbon reservoir age. Here we apply an Earth system model of intermediate complexity equipped with radiocarbon to simulate marine reservoir ages over the past 50,000 years. Globally, our simulated reservoir ages range from 400 to 1200 years at the sea surface and are systematically lower than previous uncoupled model estimates. title: Low frequency offshore wind farm noise affects natural planktonic communities during an in situ microcosm experiment in Norwegian coastal waters
abstract: Abstract The effects of anthropogenic underwater noise, such as operational noise from offshore wind farms (OWFs), on plankton are poorly understood. A significant challenge in assessing the impact of noise on natural communities is the lack of holistic and ecologically relevant experimental setups mimicking soundscapes and communities under close-to-natural conditions. title: Seismic Experiment Studying the Origin of Auckland Volcanic Field: Phase I Seafloor Data Set
abstract: Abstract This article describes an ocean-bottom seismic data set collected offshore New Zealand’s North Island as part of a multinational amphibious experiment investigating the Auckland volcanic field. From August 2023 to September 2024, 20 broadband ocean-bottom seismographs were deployed at water depths of 1200–2700 m, yielding approximately one year of continuous recordings from 15 successfully recovered instruments. title: Changing coastal distribution and life-history patterns of Inconnu in northwest Alaska
abstract: Climate change is driving shifts in fish distributions across Arctic ecosystems. Inconnu (Stenodus leucichthys) are an important subsistence and recreational fishing species and depend upon a mosaic of aquatic habitats that are rapidly changing. The freshwater migratory patterns of these fish are well-documented, but information on their coastal movement patterns and life histories are largely unknown. title: Taxonomic Revision and Field Identification Key of Pyrocystis and Dissodinium (Dinophyceae) Species from Chinese Coastal Waters
abstract: The marine dinoflagellate genera Pyrocystis and Dissodinium are core components of coastal phytoplankton and bioindicators for eutrophication monitoring, yet long-standing taxonomic confusion, misapplied Latin epithets, and inconsistent morphological records widely exist in domestic marine surveys across China’s seas. title: Adaptability Research on Different Civil Engineering Materials in Marine Environment
abstract: This study examines the adaptability of civil engineering materials in marine environments, investigating deterioration laws of five material types under multi - environmental coupling effects. title: A reference dataset for chemical contamination biomonitoring using mussels in the Mediterranean Sea
abstract: This study presents the first Mediterranean-wide assessment based on the complete original MYTILOS database, generated through coordinated mussel transplantation campaigns conducted under a common harmonized monitoring protocol. Although subsets of this dataset have previously supported scientific publications, the complete database has never been analyzed as a single basin-scale synthesis. abstract: Background This study combines cartographic sources with the situated knowledge of the local surfing community to address the lack of information describing intertidal zones in coastal areas, using the mouth of the Douro River as a case study. It employs architectural representation as a means of integrating knowledge from different disciplines and exploring the relationships among wave action, currents, flooding, and shoreline evolution. title: Occurrence of a Dendronephthya cf. sinaiensis-like nephtheid octocoral in the Arabian Sea, India
abstract: The genus Dendronephthya , a soft coral lacking zooxanthellae, is taxonomically complex and poorly documented in the Arabian Sea region. In this study, we collected and identified a colony fragment of Dendronephthya cf. sinaiensis from the Lakshadweep Archipelago in the Arabian Sea. Morphological analysis of the shape of the colony, the pattern of polyps, and the type of sclerite agrees with the description of D. sinaiensis from the Red Sea. title: From a rock to a hard place: how carbonate rocks are born and made
abstract: James Hutton recognised that some components of sedimentary rocks have a biological and marine origin as they contain ‘ solid parts ’ (mainly calcite) of past sea life, and so might offer an archive of Earth's history. Much current research effort on carbonate rocks, those that are dominantly calcite and dolomite, has focussed on the application of diverse imaging and geochemical techniques designed to reveal Earth's record of changing oceanic chemistry, climate, tectonics and carbon cycle dynamics. title: Distribution and Diversity of Coral Growth Forms at Different Depths in Badi Island, South Sulawesi, Indonesia
abstract: Coral reefs are marine ecosystems composed primarily of calcium carbonate and characterized by diverse growth forms that reflect environmental conditions. Physicochemical factors, including water temperature, depth, and salinity, may influence coral growth and community distribution. This study aimed to analyze the distribution and diversity of coral growth forms and the physicochemical characteristics of the waters surrounding Badi Island, Pangkajene and Islands Regency, South Sulawesi, as baseline information for the inventory and assessment of coral reef ecosystem conditions. title: OCEAN ENERGY. CURRENT SITUATION, CHALLENGES AND DEVELOPMENT PROSPECTS
abstract: Human society is facing numerous environmental problems, including climate change, mainly caused by the burning of fossil fuels in power plants to obtain electrical and thermal energy. On the other hand, electricity consumption is increasing due to population growth, urbanization or economic development. In order to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, one of the proposed solutions was the development of renewable energy sources, including oceanic ones. title: Microtidal wetland losses and hydrologic stressors as sea level rise accelerates in the Gulf of Mexico: running with Alice
abstract: Abstract Global sea level rise (SLR) is a widely appreciated threat to coastal wetlands. Modeled estimates of SLR thresholds beyond which coastal wetlands convert to open water suggest that landscape scale estimates of wetland loss vary with geomorphic setting, upland barriers to migration, vegetative tolerances to flooding, sediment supply, and tidal ranges among others. abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) can support monitoring of dynamic river mouths, but its interpretation depends on survey–image timing, validation design and spatially explicit uncertainty. abstract: The Late Jurassic-Early Cretaceous Phytoplankton Ecosystem Evolution and its associated Calcification Event were major evolutionary innovations of calcareous marine pelagic micro-organisms. title: The Impact of the Blue Economy on Economic Development in Lagos State, Nigeria
abstract: The blue economy, which involves the sustainable use of ocean and coastal resources for economic growth and environmental sustainability, has increasingly gained global recognition as a strategic pathway for economic development in coastal regions. Lagos State, Nigeria, with its extensive coastline and maritime resources, possesses significant potential for the development of blue economy sectors such as fisheries, maritime transport, and coastal tourism. abstract: Corrosion control has seen a shift from the traditional corrosion control methods to a more plant mediated green approach. The application of plant mediated nanoparticle for corrosion inhibition has received much research interest in recent times. The aim of this study was the green synthesis of zinc nanoparticles mediated by Hexalobus Crispiflorus bark extracts and zinc nitrate hexahydrate as the precursor for corrosion inhibition on mild steel in seawater. title: Projected Habitat Expansion of the Invasive Striped Eel Catfish Plotosus lineatus in the Mediterranean Sea Under Future Climate Conditions
abstract: The striped eel catfish Plotosus lineatus is a venomous Indo-Pacific species that has rapidly expanded within the Mediterranean Sea following its Lessepsian migration through the Suez Canal. Understanding its current distribution and future invasion potential is essential for evaluating ecological risks under ongoing climate change. title: Occurrence and Abundance of Aphid Species in Coastal Region of Bangladesh
abstract: Aphid samples were collected from bean and brinjal plants in the coastal region (Patuakhali, Barguna, Barishal, Pirojpur, Gopalgonj and Satkhira) of Bangladesh. abstract: Abstract Cross‐shelf interactions and the associated lateral transport of organic carbon remain poorly quantified and constrained by observations, despite their importance for the ocean carbon cycle. While hydropower impacts on river ecosystems have been extensively studied, far less attention has been given to lakes. It remains unclear whether the current knowledge base is sufficient to enable biodiversity conservation. abstract: Caldera-forming eruptions are among the most hazardous volcanic processes, particularly submarine ones. abstract: Purpose Despite growing interest in virtual reality (VR) as a tool to support neurodivergent individuals, limited attention has been given to how immersive and underwater virtual reality (UVR) can be designed and implemented as enabling technologies within leisure and therapeutic contexts. This study aims to develop a sensory-adapted framework to guide the design and implementation of UVR systems that support neurodivergent participation, well-being and accessibility. title: Sonic selves, ancestral archives: Identity, language and cultural memory in amaXhosa sacred practice
abstract: Among the amaXhosa of South Africa’s Eastern Cape, knowledge lives less in texts than in bodies, voices and sacred landscapes. In Hamburg, at the mouth of the Keiskamma River, knowledge of the ocean, river, forest and healing plants is transmitted in isiXhosa through song, carried by elders whose authority rests on accountability to the ancestors rather than institutional credentials. This article examines how amaXhosa sacred spaces function as living archives where language, music and cosmology converge to form identity, sustain memory and enact healing. title: Documenting the coastal erosion-driven collapse of a Cold War underground monitoring station via laser scanning
abstract: Rapid soft-cliff coastal erosion along the Holderness Coast, United Kingdom, continues to result in the loss of infrastructure, including buildings of local historical interest. The terrestrial laser scans presented in this data note were collected to document the post-failure condition of the Tunstall Royal Observer Corps monitoring post; a Cold War structure progressively exposed by ongoing soft-cliff coastal erosion. The structure was discovered to have collapsed onto the beach by local residents on the morning of 23 January 2026 and was subsequently surveyed by the authors on the same day.

title: Bacteriophages in Antarctic Subglacial Lakes Reveal Novel Biodiversity and Biogeochemical Potential
abstract: Abstract Of the more than 600 subglacial lakes identified in Antarctica thus far, Whillans Subglacial Lake (SLW) and Mercer Subglacial Lake (SLM) are the only lakes to have been directly and cleanly sampled. Although hydrologically isolated from direct marine contact for approximately 6.3 ± 1.0 ka, both lakes periodically discharge into the Ross Ice Shelf marine cavity. We present the first direct characterization of bacteriophages in Antarctic subglacial lakes, combining microscopy, metagenomics, and gene-sharing network analyses with bacteriophages found in the Ross Ice shelf marine cavity.

abstract: In a rapidly urbanized world, coastal cities are key arenas for the challenges encountered by coastal communities in the context of sustainable transformations. abstract: As a widely recognized measure of corporate sustainability, ESG performance exerts a significant influence on corporate exports and risk-coping capabilities. Using product–destination-level panel data of Chinese listed firms from 2009 to 2016, compiled from the China Customs Database and the CSMAR Database, this paper employs the High-Dimensional Fixed Effects (HDFE) model to empirically examine the impact of ESG performance on corporate export resilience and its underlying mechanisms. title: ‘We Are White Hot Rebels’ The Life and Times of Musicians Frank Merrick and Hope Squire during the Last Years of WW1
abstract: Abstract This article describes a collaborative, committed and passionate partnership in both music and politics through an analysis of a selection of wartime letters, written between 1917 and 1919, between the Manchester-based pianist and composer Hope Squire Merrick (1878–1935) and her imprisoned husband: pianist, composer and conscientious objector, Frank Merrick (1886–1981). The letters provide insight into the complex background to music making in Manchester during the First World War. title: A Contingent Commodity: Boston, Bombay and the End of the Global Ice Trade
abstract: Abstract In the mid-nineteenth century huge blocks of ice were harvested in New England and transported to port cities as far away as Bombay, Calcutta and even Hong Kong. After expanding in scale for a few decades, the trade would suddenly decline in the latter part of the century. Almost all histories of the ice trade have attributed this decline to the rise of artificial ice. Through a focus on the trade between the United States and India, however, this article argues against this popular conclusion. title: A rare Arctic record of Haliphron atlanticus (seven-arm octopus) from Bodø, Norway
abstract: Abstract Haliphron atlanticus Steenstrup, 1861, the seven-arm octopus, is a large deep-sea octopod with circumglobal distribution, yet it remains poorly documented due to its inaccessible mesopelagic to benthopelagic habitat and elusiveness. Here we report a rare observation, based on disarticulated remains recovered from a stranding event in Bodø, Arctic Norway (67.27°N, 14.43°E) in March 2026, following an initial report by local citizens. title: Global associations between extreme temperature events and childhood cancer incidence and mortality
abstract: Although extreme temperatures are recognized as an environmental threat, their contribution to the global burden of childhood cancer remains poorly quantified. We aimed to estimate childhood cancer incidence and mortality rates associated with heat and cold exposures across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. Daily ambient temperature series from the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration meteorological stations were used to calculate location-specific cumulative heat exposure, cumulative cold exposure, heat waves and cold waves. title: Mangrove reproductive dynamics and the role of honeybee introduction in the vulnerable ecosystems of the Northwestern Arabian Peninsula
abstract: Abstract Mangrove forests are increasingly threatened worldwide and a growing number of regeneration initiatives have surged, aimed at reversing their decline. A critical factor influencing the effectiveness of these efforts is the reproductive success of mangrove plants. In this study, we documented patterns of pollen deposition and fruit set in Avicennia marina and Rhizophora mucronata at two sites at their northernmost range in the Arabian Peninsula. title: Karenia cristata from the 2025 South Australian harmful algal bloom produces potent toxic compounds
abstract: For more than 12 months from March 2025, an unprecedented harmful algal bloom (HAB), dominated by the dinoflagellate genus Karenia , caused catastrophic marine mortalities in South Australia, yet the mechanisms of toxicity remain unresolved. We assessed the toxicity of five bloom isolates (three strains of Karenia cristata , one strain of Scrippsiella sp., and one strain of Karlodinium veneficum ) using fish gill cell line RTgill-W1 viability assays. title: Study of length-weight relationship and relative condition factor of Epinephelus tauvina (Forsskal, 1775) from Veraval Coast of Gujarat, India
abstract: The study of length-weight relationships (LWR) in fish species is crucial for understanding their growth patterns, health status, and for effective fisheries management. Epinephelus tauvina (Forsskal, 1775), commonly known as the greasy grouper, is an important commercial species along the southwest coast of India, particularly in Veraval, Gujarat. The LWR of E. tauvina was assessed based on fish specimens collected between December 2024 and November 2025. title: Primary Productivity in Man-Made Lakes of Northwestern Nigeria: A Review of Recent Evidence, Environmental Drivers and Research Gaps
abstract: Primary productivity is a fundamental ecological process through which aquatic autotrophs convert inorganic carbon into organic matter and introduce energy into freshwater food webs. Northwestern Nigeria contains numerous man-made lakes and reservoirs that support domestic water supply, irrigation, livestock production and fisheries. However, information on primary productivity in these systems remains fragmented, and many investigations have focused on phytoplankton composition and physicochemical characteristics rather than direct measurements of productivity. journal: Nigerian Journal of Biotechnology and Life Sciences

The Global Carbon Budget as a cointegrated system
abstract: Abstract The Global Carbon Budget, maintained by the Global Carbon Project, summarizes Earth’s global carbon cycle through four annual time series beginning in 1959: atmospheric CO2 concentrations, anthropogenic CO2 emissions, and CO2 uptake by land and by ocean. We analyze these four time series as a multivariate (cointegrated) system. Statistical tests show that the four time series are cointegrated with rank three and identify anthropogenic CO2 emissions as the single stochastic trend driving the nonstationary dynamics of the system. title: Hydrological drivers of hydrogen cyanide wildfire emissions from Indonesian peat fires during the 2015, 2019, and 2023 El Niño events
abstract: Indonesian peatlands store vast amounts of carbon that are highly vulnerable to fire during El Niño-driven droughts. When ignited, peat releases large quantities of greenhouse gases and other species with significant environmental impacts, including hydrogen cyanide (HCN), a sensitive tracer of smouldering combustion. title: Migration, Displacement, and Identity Transformation in Gaiutra Bahadur’s Coolie Woman: The Odyssey of Indenture
abstract: This paper examines the interaction between migration, displacement and identity transformation in the context of the nineteenth and early twentieth century migration of Indians as coolies to the Caribbean and in the light of Gaiutra Bahadur's Coolie Woman: The Odyssey of Indenture. It argues that indenture was not just a physical move, but a much more significant social and psychological change, which affected the caste, gender, memory and cultural identity of the people involved. Based on a qualitative close textual analysis, it employs the interdisciplinary theoretical frameworks of ‘hybrid

title: Wood identification and traditional boatbuilding along the Amazonian coast
abstract: Traditional wooden boatbuilding remains essential for mobility, fishing activities, and local economies along the Brazilian Amazonian coast. In this context, wood selection often relies on empirical knowledge and vernacular nomenclature, which may obscure the taxonomic identity and technological attributes of the materials used. This study evaluated macroscopic wood anatomy as an applied tool for identifying timber employed in traditional coastal boatyards in the state of Pará, Brazil. A total of 123 wood samples were collected from active boatyards in the municipalities of Bragança (including

title: Costumbres, instituciones, creencias de los indígenas de Argelia. Noviciado de Santa María, 1910
abstract: In this annex, we present the Spanish translation of the text of an anonymous fifty-six-page booklet written in French, containing seventy-five topics on customs, institutions, and beliefs in Algiers in 1910, from the general archives of the General House of the Society of Missionaries of Africa, «White Fathers». The most important topics covered are birth and childhood, education, marriage, makeup, tattooing and body care, clothing, greetings, and courtesy formulas. We accompany the translation with an introduction and explanatory notes.

title: Micro-fiction: The Song
abstract: Sadie Beaton is a listener, activist and Dalhousie PhD candidate carrying many generations of colonial entanglement in unceded Mi’kmaq territory. Drawing on her own settler histories, her research engages with embodied archival practices, Indigenous politics of water, and collaborative storytelling to trouble the pioneer lies that stifle settler imaginations about what kinds of relations and futures are possible here

title: Design and hardware performance of a LoRa-based vehicle tracking system with local data storage infrastructure
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance evaluation of a LoRa-based vehicle tracking system, emphasizing its hardware architecture and field performance. The system uses custom-built end nodes based on Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 (V3) boards (an ESP32-S3 microcontroller with an integrated Semtech SX1262 transceiver) and u-blox NEO-6 M GPS modules, which transmit position data to a centrally located LoRa receiver node. title: Comprehensive checklist of the flowering plants of the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, South India
abstract: The Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve (ABR), situated at the southern extremity of the Western Ghats, represents one of the most important centres of tropical biodiversity and endemism in peninsular India. Despite more than a century of botanical exploration, information on its angiosperm diversity remains scattered across numerous floras, checklists, unpublished reports and continuously changing taxonomic databases, leading to inconsistencies in nomenclature and distributional records. title: Application of sous-vide technology in aquatic products: a review
abstract: Sous-vide (SV) cooking—a technique combining vacuum packaging with precise low-temperature heating—has emerged as a promising mild processing method for aquatic products, yet existing studies remain fragmented across species and lack systematic comparisons of processing parameters and quality regulation mechanisms. This review systematically examines SV applications across four major aquatic taxa (fish, crustaceans, mollusks, and echinoderms), comparing optimal processing parameters and inter-category differences. title: The Educational Experiences of Students from the Republic of Azerbaijan in Weimar Germany (1920-1924)
abstract: This study aims to examine the educational experiences in Germany of students who were sent abroad with the objective of developing qualified human resources during the establishment of the Republic of Azerbaijan. In particular, the research seeks to reveal the educational activities and cultural interactions of students sent from Azerbaijan to Germany for higher education, as well as their contributions to the Turkic world. The scope of the study encompasses Azerbaijani students who studied in Germany between 1920 and 1924 and their educational experiences. In addition, the study addresses th

title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF PREHOSPITAL HEALTH SERVICES FOR REFUGEES IN TÜRKİYE, GERMANY AND GREECE
abstract: Objective: This study critically synthesises a body of research that documents how national policies affect emergency health service delivery to refugees and asylum seekers in Türkiye, Germany and Greece. A socio - ecological framework is used to analyse a range of factors from policies to local service structures to migrant narratives that create the social context for accessing emergency health. title: Foraging Habits of the Smallest Asian Black Bear Population in Shikoku Island, Japan
abstract: We investigated the foraging habits of the Asian black bear, probably the smallest bear population in the world, using 122 fecal samples, foraging signs, and stable isotope analysis of bear hair in Shikoku Island (SI). Fecal analysis revealed obvious seasonal changes, with the dominant food items being green vegetation in spring, soft masts in summer, and soft and hard masts in autumn. To clarify the characteristics of fecal content in SI, we compared it with that of bears in other areas of Japan. title: FROM ANCESTRAL LANDSCAPES TO THE TWENTY-FIRST CENTURY: A HISTORICAL AND SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL SYNTHESIS OF PARAÍBA, NORTHEASTERN BRAZIL
abstract: The history of Paraíba, northeastern Brazil, cannot be adequately understood as a sequence beginning with Portuguese colonization in the sixteenth century. The territory corresponding to the present state was inhabited, managed and culturally transformed by Indigenous peoples long before European arrival, and its subsequent trajectory resulted from continuous interactions among societies, political systems, economic activities, climate, biodiversity and landscapes. title: Cargo-vessel Congestion at Three Major United States Gateways During the 2020–2022 Supply-chain Disruption
abstract: The 2020–2022 disruption of global supply chains produced severe cargo-ship congestion at United States gateway ports, yet much of the public evidence rests on news reports and proprietary indices rather than open vessel-movement data. This study quantifies and compares cargo-vessel congestion at three major US gateways, Los Angeles/Long Beach, Houston/Galveston, and New York/New Jersey, using open Automatic Identification System (AIS) data from the United States Nationwide AIS archive. title: Impacts of Anthropogenic Aerosol‐Forced North Atlantic SST Variability on the Simulated Historical Global Warming
abstract: Abstract Climate models with identical anthropogenic forcings simulate different historical warming, mainly because aerosol forcing is poorly constrained. The role of uncertainty in regional aerosol forcing, however, has not been systematically studied. title: Suicide Prevention in the US Military: Assessing the Impact of the Brandon Act
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether the Brandon Act, a 2021 legislation establishing confidential, self-initiated mental health referral pathways for US military service members, was associated with reductions in medically attended suicide attempts among active duty service members (ADSMs). STUDY SETTING AND DESIGN: We employed an interrupted time series design using person-quarter panel data from the Military Health System (MHS) from 2018 to 2024. abstract: Background: The seasonal dynamics of the Gulf of Guinea, characterised by alternating dry and rainy seasons, exert profound influences on oceanographic conditions, primary productivity, and fish recruitment patterns. Understanding these seasonal patterns is particularly important for artisanal fisheries that depend on predictable seasonal variations in fish availability and abundance. title: Environmental Determinants of Abundance and Distribution of Selected Neuropteran Families in Eastern Libya
abstract: This study investigates the environmental determinants influencing the abundance and distribution of selected Neuropteran families in Eastern Libya. Field surveys were conducted over a full annual cycle across agricultural, coastal, and semi-arid habitats within the Cyrenaica region. Insect samples were collected using light traps, sweep nets, and sticky traps. Environmental variables including temperature, relative humidity, vegetation density, and soil type were recorded. title: India's Disaster Management Policy: Mandate vs. Ground Reality
abstract: Abstract While India has established a sophisticated, technology-driven policy framework for disaster management, a critical gap remains between these high-level mandates and ground-level execution due to underfunded local authorities, unplanned urbanization, and last-mile communication bottlenecks India’s disaster management paradigm has undergone a major structural shift from a reactive, relief-centric model to a proactive, technology-driven approach, anchored by the historic Disaster Management Act of 2005 and recently updated by the Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill. title: Blue innovation and ecological transitions: a realist synthesis of mechanisms and knowledge asymmetries
abstract: Purpose This study aims to synthesize how scientific literature defines and operationalizes blue innovation and to explain the context-dependent mechanisms linking blue innovation to ecological transitions and blue economy outcomes. The study also examines how geographical asymmetries in knowledge production limit the external validity of dominant blue economy models, particularly for Latin America, Africa and the South Atlantic. title: The Role Geomorphic Origin and Agricultural Legacy on Plant Communities and Surface Soil Organic Matter in Salt Marshes
abstract: Abstract Saltmarsh habitats provide numerous ecosystem services, including carbon storage, but are eroding at increasingly rapid rates due to ongoing sea level rise. Yet, where space and topography permit, saltmarshes are transgressing into adjacent uplands and counterbalancing the lost area. In these areas, older portions of marshes have accumulated more soil organic matter (SOM) over time than more recently formed marshes, though processes driving this pattern can be complex. Sediment deposition dynamics and plant community can influence SOM with both playing important but interacting roles.

title: In water, no one can hear you scream: a new species of parasitic isopod from the genus Zeuxokoma Grygier, 1993 (Isopoda: Epicaridea, Cryptoniscidae) infesting a snapping-shrimp (Caridea, Alpheidae) from Brazil
abstract: Isopods of the suborder Epicaridea Latreille, 1825 are obligatory parasites of other crustaceans, using them as intermediate and definitive hosts during their life cycles. All species of the family Cryptoniscidae Kossmann, 1880 are endoparasitic or mesoparasitic, and can be found as direct parasites of decapods or as hyperparasites of rhizocephalan barnacles infesting decapod hosts. title: Extensive induction of diploid aposporous gametophytes and their application in polyploid breeding of Undaria pinnatifida
abstract: Triploid breeding is a promising strategy for developing Undaria pinnatifida cultivars with higher yield, better quality, and stronger resistance to environmental stresses. We previously developed a triploid breeding method through crossing aposporous gametophytes derived from doubled haploid sporophytes with haploid gametophytes. abstract: Reliable magnetic-materials screening requires more than a model that performs well within one computational catalogue. We develop and audit a composition-anchored library residual (CALR) protocol for transferring density-functional-theory (DFT) magnetic-moment information across heterogeneous databases. title: Turnover-driven β-diversity reveals conservation priorities in Antarctic intertidal benthic communities
abstract: Abstract Antarctic sedimentary intertidal habitats remain among the most understudied and least represented within protected areas designated under the Antarctic Treaty System. Understanding how biodiversity varies across space and time within these habitats is therefore essential for effective conservation planning. title: Nature-based therapy in the UAE: leveraging ecosystems to alleviate depression and anxiety
abstract: This review synthesizes current evidence on the relationship between natural ecosystems and mental health outcomes with a particular focus on arid and rapidly urbanizing contexts such as the United Arab Emirates (UAE). It introduces the Multi-Ecosystem Therapeutic Framework for Arid Urban Environments, which moves beyond generalized "nature exposure" models by systematically linking distinct environmental systems to mental health outcomes through identifiable psychological, physiological and social mechanisms. abstract: Abstract Environmental RNA (eRNA) can potentially augment the biological monitoring ability of the established environmental DNA (eDNA) application in conservation. Despite faster degradation, environmental RNA could offer unique advantages: it may help reduce the legacy signal compared to eDNA, provide insights into physiological status through gene transcription and offer higher detection sensitivity due to the inherent amplification of certain genes in response to physiology and the environmental context. title: The Image of the Danube in Romanian Poetry
abstract: This article surveys the evolving renditions of the Danube in Romanian poetry from the nineteenth century to the present, situating them within broader cultural, historical, and ecological frameworks. Inspired by a personal rediscovery of the river and informed by Bruno Latour’s concept of the “parliament of things,” the study approaches the Danube as a voice-bearing agent, whose meanings emerge from the interaction between natural processes and human histories. title: Conservation Science and the Knowledge Shortfalls
abstract: There is much data publicly available on the biodiversity of the world. It would appear then that conserving biodiversity is just a matter of using the data. In this contribution I argue that conservation requires not only data availability, but also conversations about purpose, and present examples of how just being able to use large biodiversity databases is seldom enough to achieve successful conservation.

title: Temporality, emotion management and emergency governance in housing safety crises
abstract: This article uses archival methods to explore housing disasters and the governance of emergencies, using two cases – the Ronan Point collapse and the Ledbury Estate post-Grenfell Tower Fire – to locate a contemporary housing safety emergency within longer histories of high-rise unsafety. title: A Comparative Study of Solastalgia in Contemporary Post-Disaster Fiction
abstract: The contemporary semiotic landscape exposes a high-tension dynamic between the progressive degradation of a habitat-milieu and the systemic deconstruction of identity structures. By investigating the isotopies of ruin across Jesmyn Ward's Salvage the Bones (2011) and Ahmed Saadawi's Frankenstein in Baghdad (2013), this exegesis interrogates the mutation of actants confronted with the profound erosion of spatiotemporal frameworks in distinct environments of collapse: hurricane-ravaged coastal Mississippi and war-torn Iraq. title: Temporal variability of extreme precipitation in Cotonou: stable climate signal and worsening urban flood impacts
abstract: Urban flooding has worsened significantly in Cotonou (major flood events in 2010, 2018, and 2020), yet this deterioration occurs against a backdrop of largely stable extreme precipitation. This study analyses the temporal variability of extreme precipitation indices in Cotonou over 40 years (1984–2024) in order to explain this paradox. Based on daily rainfall data from the Cotonou synoptic station, eleven standardised ETCCDI climate indices were calculated at four temporal scales (annual, monthly, seasonal, and decadal). journal: Proceedings of the International Association of Hydrological Sciences

title: Transmitting Values Through Maudu’ Lompoa: Vernacular Ritual and Character Education in Pluralistic Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates Maudu’ Lompoa, an annual Islamic-vernacular ritual in Cikoang Village, South Sulawesi, to examine how local ritual structures transmit socio-cultural and moral values in a pluralistic society. Employing an ethnographic qualitative-descriptive design, data were collected through participant observation across the 18-day ritual cycle, documentary analysis, and in-depth interviews with 12 purposively selected informants (customary leaders, ritual committee organizers, female craft artisans, youth representatives, and lay villagers) to ensure empirical adequacy and saturati
journal: ETDC Indonesian Journal of Research and Educational Review

title: From stench to hygiene? Public toilets as liminal spaces in late Ottoman İstanbul
abstract: Abstract This article examines public toilets in late Ottoman İstanbul as liminal spaces where urban governance, public health, and everyday life intersected. It argues that these sites functioned as arenas through which modern notions of hygiene, order, and civilization were articulated and contested. title: Factors that cause flatfoot in school children
abstract: Background: Flatfoot is a common disorder in children, although it often does not show serious symptoms. Over time, it will affect the development and growth of the arch of the foot. This study aimed to determine the factors that cause flatfoot in school children. Methods: This study used the literature review method by utilizing databases containing research articles related to factors that could cause flatfoot in elementary school children. title: Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo: orígenes, desarrollo institucional y contexto de un museo en movimiento
abstract: Introduction: Founded in 1994, the Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo de Costa Rica (MADC) emerged within a Central American context marked by institutional fragility and limited infrastructure for contemporary art. Objective: The paper seeks to analyze the evolution of the MADC in relation to its regional context, Costa Rican cultural policies, and founding process, as well as the conceptual and disciplinary tensions between art and design and its curatorial practices. title: Exploring Nature and Human Phenomena in the Jama Mapun Legend of Adjung-Adjung
abstract: This study examined the Jama Mapun Legend of Adjung-Adjung through an ecocritical and cultural perspective, focusing on how nature and human phenomena shape the sense of place associated with the Jama Mapun community in Mapun, Tawi-Tawi, Philippines. The legend was also examined as a form of living cultural heritage reflecting values, beliefs, language, livelihood practices, spirituality, maritime identity, and collective memory. journal: International Journal of Sustainable and Integrated Studies

title: Exporting nuclear secrecy. The transatlantic diffusion of nuclear secrecy practices in the postwar period (1945-1953)
abstract: This article examines how United States (US) nuclear secrecy standards shaped the domestic nuclear policies of Western European states between 1945 and the launch of Atoms for Peace. title: Analisis Fotografi Sebagai Wadah atau Media untuk Memperkenalkan Jejak Jejak Peradaban di Nusantara sebagai Arsip Sejarah
abstract: Photography has an important role as a visual communication medium that can preserve historical information and represent cultural identity. However, the use of photography as an instrument for interpreting the traces of Islamic civilization in the Nusantara region has not been widely studied from the perspective of visual communication. This study aims to analyze the role of documentary photography in representing the traces of Islamic civilization and the process of cultural assimilation between Islam and local Nusantara culture. title: MINDING THE GAP: A METHODOLOGICAL AND CHRONOLOGICAL REASSESSMENT OF EASTERN MEDITERRANEAN PURPLE‐DYE PRODUCTION IN THE BRONZE AND IRON AGES
abstract: Summary Purple dye was an iconic status symbol in the ancient Mediterranean, yet tracing the expansion and shift of production from the Aegean to the Levant encounters substantial methodological difficulties. Using Tel Shiqmona – a unique industrial centre with a continuous Iron Age sequence – as an archaeological benchmark, this study defines detailed and granular criteria for identifying production. title: The role of educational governance and socioeconomic structures in shaping revolutionary activities in East Bengal
abstract: Abstract This research investigates the intersection of governance, education, and socio-conditions in shaping revolutionary resistance in East Bengal between 1906 and 1917. The colonial rule aimed at centralizing power at Calcutta, and East Bengal was a peripheral province marked by historical marginalization. However, the socio-economic inequalities, infrastructural gaps, geographical advantages, and the paradoxical effects of colonial education generated deep discontent among the emerging middle class and rural populations. title: From the Ottoman Palace to the Last Resting Place in Bosnia: Silahdar Mustafa Pasha’s Tomb and Career Path
abstract: This article revisits the historical details of Silahdar (Perişan) Mustafa Pasha's tomb (died 1799) in Travnik, central Bosnia, and re-examines previously published information about his career. Mustafa Pasha held roles as governor and district governor in several Ottoman provinces (eyalets) and districts (sancaks). He also served as a deputy (ḳā’im-maḳām) for the Grand Vizier and was married to Beyhan Sultan, daughter of Mustafa III. title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Policy and Service Delivery in the Nigerian Public Service: A Case Study of University of Uyo
abstract: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) have been recognized as an effective tool that could assist government and its institutions reinvent itself faster, run cheaply, better and produce newer outcomes. title: Nano-enabled strategies to inhibit mobile genetic elements and antimicrobial resistance in wastewater systems
abstract: The present review explores the role of nanotechnology in mitigating the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) through mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in wastewater environments. The global rise of AMR has emerged as a major public health challenge, with wastewater treatment systems serving as critical reservoirs for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and facilitating their transfer among microbial populations. Mobile genetic elements, including plasmids, transposons, integrons, and bacteriophages, play a central role in horizontal gene transfer, accelerating the spread of resistance

title: Neurosurgery Residency Theses in Türkiye: A Bibliometric Comparison Between the 2016–2020 and 2021–2025 Periods
abstract: This study aimed to bibliometrically evaluate medical specialty theses completed in the field of neurosurgery in Türkiye between 2016 and 2025, and to examine temporal changes in thesis numbers, topic distribution, and gender distribution of thesis authors. In this retrospective bibliometric study, neurosurgery residency theses registered in the Council of Higher Education National Thesis Center database between 2016 and 2025 were reviewed. abstract: DNA extraction from aquatic samples is a critical process that influences the quantity and purity of the DNA obtained. title: A Bibliometric Analysis on Emergency Department Simulation and Discrete Event Simulation
abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the scope of academic articles containing the keywords "emergency department" and "simulation" and to reveal the development and trends in this field. The study aims to present a bibliometric analysis of the literature on articles discussing simulation in emergency department studies based on quantitative data analysis, and to identify research trends and gaps in this field. title: Unveiling the club moss (Lycopodium clavatum L.): Ethnomedicinal uses, phytochemistry and pharmacological insights
abstract: Club moss, scientifically known as Lycopodium clavatum L., is a primitive tracheophyte in the family Lycopodiaceae of the pteridophytes. Lycopodium clavatum thrives on exposed, lightly shaded grassland slopes, forest peripheries and disturbed or human-impacted areas such as road cuts. These traits enable them to have widespread distribution in moist forest margins, temperate, subtropical and polar climates. They are documented in Europe, Asia and America. title: La evolución de los modelos de investigación-acción en la formación inicial docente: Una revisión sistemática
abstract: Background: Initial teacher education faces the ongoing challenge of articulating the theoretical foundations acquired at university with practical experiences developed in educational settings. In this context, action research is recognized as a formative strategy that promotes critical reflection and the development of professional teacher identity. Objective: To analyze the evolution of action research models applied to university-based teaching practice between 2000 and 2026.
